articles.title: Sovereign or not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Sovereign or not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide
Sovereignty is everywhere right now, and most people still can’t agree on what it means and, just as importantly, what it all means to them.
This week theCUBE Research releases its new market report, Sovereign or Not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide. In this Breaking Analysis, we’re joined by its author, Amit Eyal Govrin, lead analyst for sovereign AI at theCUBE Research and CEO of Agentcy Labs, to talk about why he wrote it, what sovereignty is and what it isn’t, and what surprised him most in the findings.
The full scores are in the report. Read the full report online: Sovereign or Not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide https://siliconangle.com/sovereign-or-not
How the research started
Dave: As someone who’s been leading the thought leadership in this domain, how did you come up with the inspiration to research this topic and write the report?
Amit: To understand the how, it helps to understand the why. I’ve been thinking about this subject for a while now. It hasn’t always been called “sovereignty,” but the tenets have always been the same.
It all started around four years ago, as I’ve been a builder in this space for that long. First with Kubiya, one of the industry’s first agentic implementations, deploying agents in enterprise production environments as early as September 2023, before agents were even an industry term.
We were being asked tough questions:
- Are we married to the models of Provider A, or can we host on Provider B?
- We can’t work with Provider C because they didn’t pass our security officer.
- What happens to our work if we leave you for Provider D? Do we start from scratch?
- Can we take our skills, our workflows, our data with us?
- Can we leverage a code escrow in case we ever need to part ways?
We were deploying as a software-as-a-service company, and many of those concerns were legitimate. As a software company, we got to keep our intellectual property and license it out. If we were successful, we would create dependency, which effectively meant customers lost control of their crown jewels.
When we started Agentcy Labs earlier this year, customers familiar with our work approached us, and many of these points crystallized for us. What they told us: We’re relieved you are no longer at Kubiya. It’s not that we ever doubted your technology or the value it brings. Quite the opposite. That was what they were afraid of. Kubiya creates a dependency, adoption balloons, and they lose control of their costs. Or a vendor changes the meter on them because of shareholder pressure or regulatory controls.
What clicked for us is that their resistance was never about Kubiya or our technology. It was about the loss of control of their alpha. Namely, the Agentic Operating System, the key driver of their artificial intelligence transformation, which falls under our technological pillar.
It doesn’t matter if the vendor is a startup, an AI lab or a hyperscaler. No enterprise can afford to mortgage its entire business on an external dependency on such a key issue. It’s far too strategic not to own outright.
That finding forced us to rethink the model behind software, dig deeper into sovereignty as an issue of control, and help the industry define it in a more standardized way.
What sovereignty isn’t
Dave: So control is the heart of it. But when most people hear sovereignty, they think about where the data sits. Is that the wrong way to look at it?
Amit: Sovereignty goes well beyond territory, which is often the most misunderstood aspect. People hear sovereignty and immediately revert to the sovereign state: government initiatives, national security, on-premises air-gapped environments. That can be true in some cases. But by and large, our sovereignty discussions involve enterprises and regulated industries that have sovereignty as a core tenet of their AI initiatives.
It goes beyond buzzwords and sovereign-washing claims. Think back to the explosive Alex Karp interview on CNBC claiming enterprises are losing their alpha to frontier labs. I largely agree with that claim, by the way. Only he finished his pitch by offering customers to move it over to Palantir. In other words: Stop mortgaging your alpha to Anthropic and OpenAI, come rent it from us.
That interview was my trigger point to take up arms and educate the industry on sovereignty: what it is, what it isn’t, and most importantly, what you, as a buyer of AI, can do about it.
The 5 pillars of sovereignty
Dave: And you’ve been out in the field with buyers ever since. What did those conversations teach you, and how did that shape the framework?
Amit: Since then, we’ve been included in dozens of engagements with enterprises, governments and policymakers around the world, from Washington to Brussels, New Delhi, Sydney and even Riyadh. We are in the room when sovereignty discussions happen. That helped us shape our view, tease out the concerns, and focus on what really matters and why. From those discussions came the 5 Pillars of Sovereignty framework. We use it today to assess all vendor relationships, policy and regulation, and geopolitical events.
Sovereign or Not?
Dave: Which brings us to the report. You started with the hyperscalers. Walk us through how you approached it.
Amit: In our first edition, Sovereign or Not? The Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide, we take the buyer’s lens and assess each hyperscaler by its sovereignty posture.
Hint: By definition, working with any hyperscaler means ceding a good portion of control over your Operational, Technological, Legal and Financial pillars. Oftentimes that’s the reality in the real world.
My view: Sovereignty is not a purity test. It’s perfectly acceptable to go with a hyperscaler, as long as it’s a known dependency you priced in as an acceptable risk. If that’s the case, let us guide you through these considerations to the best path forward for your organization.
Who scored what
Dave: OK, let’s get to the part everyone wants to know. Who scored what, and why?
Amit: We looked at seven hyperscalers and 40 of their offerings, from the point of view of buyers in five regions: the U.S., Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and the rest, including the Middle East and Africa. Everything is scored out of 5.
The short version: The most sovereign product a hyperscaler sells is the one the hyperscaler itself can’t reach.
On these tests, sovereignty often runs inverse to how a hyperscaler is built. A shared global control plane and services the vendor runs for the customer make a cloud easy to adopt, but every layer the vendor runs is a layer the buyer does not control. Amazon Web Services and Google built their platforms around that abstraction, which becomes a hindrance once a buyer needs to run the stack without them. The grades measure how much control a buyer can take back, not the quality of the cloud.
Who came out on top, who came in last, and by how much, is in the report. And every score is backed by a source. Don’t like your grade? Publish the document and we’ll re-score it.
What’s inside the full report:
- The Sovereignty Index for all seven hyperscalers, overall and in each of the five buyer regions
- Every offering graded on the 5 Pillars, with 17 tests and a Legal ladder
- A decision tree for buyers with hard constraints
- Region-by-region law, from the CLOUD Act to Europe’s new sovereignty rules
- On-the-record answers from the hyperscalers themselves, and surveys of actual buyers
The CLOUD Act clawback
Dave: What surprised you most when you went through the findings?
Amit: None of the hyperscalers has a practical solution for the U.S. CLOUD Act, and that alone has created a real legal clawback on non-U.S. companies.
In plain English: The U.S. government can ask an American cloud company for data it controls, no matter which country the data sits in. A sovereign cloud in Brandenburg, run by a German subsidiary, doesn’t change the answer. It’s still owned by an American company.
The vendors aren’t hiding it. AWS told us as much on the record. Microsoft’s own lawyer in France told the French Senate he couldn’t guarantee French data would never reach U.S. authorities. That’s honesty, and we don’t penalize honesty. It’s the law, and it applies to every American cloud the same way.
European privacy law says you can’t just hand that data over. So a European company can end up stuck between two governments, breaking one law to obey the other. That’s the clawback.
The fixes buyers are being sold, like keeping data local, holding your own encryption keys, or a contract promise to fight requests, don’t change who the government can go to.
Dave: So what’s a non-U.S. buyer supposed to do about that?
Amit: There’s no perfect answer today, only partial ones.
- Option one: Run it yourself, in your own facility, cut off from the vendor. Several hyperscalers sell a version like that. It gets you a good part of the way there.
- Option two: Go through a local partner the hyperscaler doesn’t control. France has a certification built for this, and only one hyperscaler offering has earned it. Read the report to find out which one.
- What nobody offers yet: Open software you run yourself, including the agentic operating system, so you can keep going even if you walk away from the vendor.
Going with a hyperscaler is fine, as long as you know the risk and priced it in. What’s not fine is believing a data center in Brandenburg, on its own merits, solved your sovereignty problem.
The other surprises
Dave: What else jumped out at you?
Amit:
- Nobody has tested the off switch. Every vendor says it can keep running if it’s cut off from headquarters. None has published a real test. The only one on the record lasted several hours.
- Moving your data out is expensive, with one exception. It costs about $8,400 with one vendor and $54,000 to $79,000 with the others. Read the report to find out which one.
- Latin America is the blind spot. São Paulo is the only city where all seven are present, and none of them can sign Brazil’s government requirement that data won’t be handed to a foreign government.
- Europe’s new sovereignty law stops short. No hyperscaler reaches its top level, and the law doesn’t even ask what it costs you to leave.
What’s next
Dave: And this is just the first of several. Where do you go from here?
Amit: This is the first of a series: neoclouds, OEMs, telcos and specialized sovereign initiatives, wherever you happen to be, whether you’re a U.S., EU, Latin American, APAC or Middle Eastern buyer. Every edition covers the 5 Pillars, plus security, regulation and exit costs. Readers will be surprised by how deep we got, including quotes from the hyperscalers themselves and surveys of actual buyers. I truly think this will be valuable to everyone listening and reading.
Dave: That’s phenomenal, Amit. This is a cutting-edge report on a truly important and timely subject. If previously you were building on the frontier, you’re now squarely on the frontier of research. The scores, the vendor answers and the buyer data are all in the full report.
Read the full report online: Sovereign or Not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide
Sources:
- Sovereign or Not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide, theCUBE Research, November 2026
- Microsoft admits it ‘cannot guarantee’ data sovereignty, The Register, July 2025
- European Commission’s Proposed Cloud Sovereignty Framework Creates New Compliance Tiers, Jones Day, June 2026
- From Tokenmaxxing to Sovereign Alpha, Breaking Analysis 324, theCUBE Research, August 2026
Amit Eyal Govrin is lead analyst for sovereign AI at theCUBE Research and CEO of Agentcy Labs, which designs and builds sovereign AI platforms for enterprises and governments. His research for theCUBE Research is conducted under theCUBE Research’s editorial standards and is not sponsored or directed by Agentcy Labs. Agentcy Labs may hold commercial relationships with vendors covered in this research.

articles.text:
My favorite drawing display offers top-tier drawing performance at a surprisingly low price — here’s why you should be considering the XP-Pen Artist Pro 24 Gen 2 4K
Impressive results for an affordable price
I’ve always loved digital art, but I never seemed to find the time to commit to practicing my drawing skills. That all changed after I came across the XP-Pen Artist Pro 24 Gen 2 4K, meaning I’ve drawn more over the last year than I probably have in the last decade.
The XP-Pen Artist Pro 24 Gen 2 4K has a list price of $1,299.99, which is fantastic considering what it offers for the cost. It’s even better value right now, however, as there’s currently a massive $400 off at XP-Pen, thanks to an early Black Friday sale.
This impressive drawing tablet is now even cheaper when you use the code MD24U400 at checkout, thanks to this early Black Friday sale. Don't deliberate too long though, as this deal's only valid for just over five days, or until stock runs out.
There’s a lot I enjoy about this drawing tablet, as I explored in my full XP-Pen Artist Pro 24 Gen 2 4K review, from its vibrant and expansive 24-inch display to its customizable drawing tools. These tools include the X3 Pro Smart Chip and X3 Pro Slim styli and ACK05 Wireless Shortcut Remote, so I’ve got everything I need to fine-tune my creative process. I enjoyed using all of the tools, particularly the pens, which are easy to glide across the canvas, with no jitteriness or parallax.
My only real criticism is that it’s a little on the chonky side, but I definitely appreciate its sturdiness. The metal stand feels reassuringly stable, and provides a variety of drawing angles. Overall, the Artist Pro 24 Gen 2 4K is a great option for beginners and professionals alike, and I’m seriously impressed that this XP-Pen display offers all this for so much less than a Wacom.
I was already singing this drawing display’s praises, but with an extra 30% off the retail price, it’s an absolute steal. If you’re looking to upgrade your equipment, or if you want to benefit from an expansive and vividly-colored drawing area straight off the bat, it would make the perfect choice.

articles.title: Mails, documents, visio : 6 outils gratuits pour travailler sans Microsoft 365
articles.text:
La panne de Microsoft 365 complique votre journée de travail ? Des alternatives gratuites peuvent prendre le relais pour modifier un document, tenir une visioconférence ou envoyer un message urgent. Nous avons retenu six outils pour vous dépanner, en précisant leurs usages et leurs limites.
Les perturbations de Microsoft 365 compliquent l’accès à Outlook et à plusieurs services associés depuis jeudi 12 novembre. Pour avancer, la solution dépend surtout de la tâche à accomplir.
Cette sélection privilégie les outils gratuits utilisables ponctuellement : des applications locales pour la bureautique et des services en ligne pour les échanges. Deux viennent d’Infomaniak : kMeet pour ses réunions sans inscription et kDrive pour disposer d’un espace de partage indépendant de Microsoft, avec 15 Go gratuits, sans passer par un compte Google.
Ces outils ne débloquent toutefois pas les contenus restés sur les serveurs de Microsoft. En entreprise, utilisez les services autorisés par votre organisation. Pour les logiciels, passez par les sites officiels des éditeurs.
Pour terminer un document ou maintenir une réunion
Si Word et Excel sont déjà installés, activés et fonctionnels sur votre ordinateur, commencez par les utiliser sur vos fichiers locaux. Les alternatives suivantes intéressent notamment ceux qui dépendent des versions web d’Office.
LibreOffice : une suite bureautique complète sur votre ordinateur
Writer pour les textes, Calc pour les tableaux et Impress pour les présentations : LibreOffice couvre les principaux usages bureautiques, gratuitement et sans connexion permanente. Travaillez sur une copie de vos documents importants. Pour les fichiers Microsoft complexes, vérifiez la mise en page, les formules et les fonctions particulières avant de transmettre votre travail.
- Prise en charge des formats Microsoft Office
- Bibliothèque d'extensions et de templates
- Régulièrement mis à jour
ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors : pour travailler avec les formats Office
Disponible gratuitement sur Windows, macOS et Linux, ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors ouvre notamment les fichiers DOCX, XLSX et PPTX. Son interface à onglets rassemble traitement de texte, tableur et présentations, avec une utilisation locale possible sans connexion permanente. Là encore, conservez les originaux et contrôlez le résultat.
kMeet : une solution de repli pour votre visioconférence
Si vous avez encore le lien de votre réunion Teams, essayez-le d’abord. Dans son bulletin de vendredi à 11 h 01, Microsoft indiquait que la participation aux réunions restait fonctionnelle, contrairement à certaines fonctions d’agenda.
Si cela ne suffit pas, kMeet permet de lancer gratuitement une visioconférence depuis un navigateur, sans inscription, avec partage d’écran et messagerie intégrée. Il faudra transmettre un nouveau lien aux participants : les invitations et conversations Teams ne seront pas transférées.
- Un logiciel simple et gratuit pour tous
- Un large choix de personnalisation des arrière-plans.
- Les fonctionnalités phares d'un logiciel de visioconférence.
Pour envoyer un mail urgent ou partager un fichier
Gmail : utiliser une adresse de secours déjà disponible
Une adresse Gmail que vous possédez déjà peut servir à reprendre contact, si son utilisation est autorisée par votre entreprise. Prévenez votre correspondant par téléphone ou par un canal connu : une adresse inhabituelle peut éveiller ses soupçons ou voir son message classé en courrier indésirable. Créer un compte dans l’urgence est moins immédiat qu’il n’y paraît : Google peut demander une vérification téléphonique.
- storage15 Go de stockage
- securityChiffrement natif en option
- alternate_emailPas de domaine personnalisé
- smartphoneApplications iOS, Android
- push_pinJurisdiction USA
Proton Mail : une autre boîte indépendante de Microsoft
Proton Mail propose également une offre gratuite pour disposer d’une adresse de secours. Son stockage et ses fonctions restent limités par rapport aux abonnements payants. Surtout, ouvrir un compte ne récupère pas votre historique Outlook et ne redirige pas les messages destinés à votre adresse Microsoft. Une éventuelle importation dépendra du rétablissement de l’accès à la boîte d’origine.
Dans les deux cas, méfiez-vous aussi des messages « de secours » que vous recevez. Une demande de paiement, de changement de coordonnées bancaires ou d’identifiants doit être vérifiée auprès de votre interlocuteur par un canal déjà connu.
- storage1 Go de stockage
- securityChiffrement natif par défaut
- alternate_emailPas de domaine personnalisé
- smartphoneApplications iOS, Android
- push_pinJurisdiction Suisse
kDrive : un nouvel espace pour les fichiers que vous avez
L’offre gratuite my kSuite d’Infomaniak comprend 15 Go de stockage kDrive. Vous pouvez y déposer les documents présents sur votre appareil et partager un lien avec vos correspondants. Cela dépanne lorsqu’un échange de pièces jointes ou un lien OneDrive ne fonctionne pas. Un fichier uniquement stocké sur un OneDrive inaccessible devra toutefois être récupéré au préalable. Vérifiez aussi les droits de partage du nouveau lien.
- mood15 Go d'espace gratuit
- uploadPas de limite d'envoi
- home_pinServeurs en Suisse
Pour choisir rapidement, partez de votre besoin immédiat : une réunion appelle un lien de visio, un document local une application compatible, un échange urgent un canal de secours connu, en attendant le retour à la normale durable de Microsoft 365.

articles.title: El rastro de los chips de Nvidia prohibidos que llegaron a una empresa china de Alice Huang a través de Singapur
articles.text:
Una empresa china fundada por Alice Huang, la empresaria señalada por los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses como presunta agente de Beijing en el escándalo que sacudió a Nvidia, adquirió chips de inteligencia artificial cuya exportación a China está prohibida, informó este viernes Bloomberg News. El hallazgo amplía las ramificaciones de una crisis que ya forzó la renuncia del cofundador y director general Jensen Huang y borró casi medio billón de dólares de la capitalización bursátil de la compañía.
Según Bloomberg, que citó a una fuente anónima con conocimiento del asunto, Aperia Cloud Services, socio oficial de Nvidia con sede en Singapur, adquirió servidores con procesadores H800 al fabricante Dell Technologies. Esos equipos, en lugar de permanecer en el país insular, terminaron en manos de Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, una empresa radicada en el principal hub económico del este chino que fue fundada por Alice Huang. El medio financiero respaldó la información con documentos presentados ante autoridades chinas. No quedó claro, según la misma fuente, de qué modo se efectuó la transferencia ni si Alice Huang participó directamente en la operación.
Estados Unidos prohibió en 2023 la exportación de chips H800 a China, con el propósito de frenar el avance de Beijing en el desarrollo de sistemas de inteligencia artificial. La restricción forma parte de una política más amplia de control de tecnología considerada estratégicamente sensible.
Megaspeed, en el centro de la trama de desvío de semiconductores
Alice Huang es conocida principalmente como ex directora gerente de Megaspeed International, empresa de centros de datos con sede en Singapur que las agencias de inteligencia de Estados Unidos consideran vinculada al Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado chino. La firma enfrenta acusaciones de haber canalizado chips avanzados de Nvidia hacia China a través de rutas alternativas. El jueves, Megaspeed anunció que investiga si cumplió con los controles de exportación vigentes para semiconductores de alta gama. Por su parte, Malasia informó que lleva adelante una investigación sobre una filial de Megaspeed ante indicios de posible desvío de chips a terceros países.
La firma es señalada como el principal mecanismo a través del cual chips de alto rendimiento de Nvidia habrían eludido las restricciones impuestas por Washington, aunque tanto la empresa como el gobierno chino rechazan las acusaciones. Beijing negó que Alice Huang sea una espía.
El Congreso convoca a Jensen Huang para diciembre
La crisis no se limita al ámbito empresarial. Jensen Huang, de 63 años, cofundador de Nvidia y director general de la compañía durante 33 años, fue convocado a declarar en diciembre ante comisiones del Congreso de Estados Unidos. El senador republicano Tim Scott, presidente de la Comisión de Banca del Senado, anunció el jueves haber solicitado la comparecencia de Huang y del secretario de Comercio, Howard Lutnick, para el 3 de diciembre. “Los informes recientes generan serias preocupaciones sobre nuestra seguridad nacional y la protección de la tecnología sensible de Estados Unidos”, escribió Scott en X.
La iniciativa del Senado se suma a la solicitud conjunta de tres comisiones de la Cámara de Representantes, que pidieron una entrevista a puerta cerrada con Huang para el 1 de diciembre, bajo amenaza de citación judicial en caso de no comparecer.
Jensen Huang reconoció relaciones extramatrimoniales y renunció a la conducción de Nvidia
Jensen Huang, casado desde hace más de cuatro décadas, reconoció el domingo pasado haber mantenido al menos una relación extramatrimonial. La prensa identificó a Alice Huang como la persona involucrada. El miércoles, The New York Times informó sobre una segunda relación, esta vez con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de Nvidia para el sector médico. Al día siguiente, Huang presentó su renuncia.
Nvidia designó a su directora financiera, Colette Kress, para ocupar el cargo de forma interina. Nacido en Taiwán y radicado en Estados Unidos desde la infancia, Jensen Huang cofundó la empresa y la llevó a convertirse, bajo su conducción, en la fabricante de semiconductores más valiosa del mundo. Sus procesadores, diseñados originalmente para los gráficos de videojuegos, se volvieron un componente esencial para el entrenamiento y la ejecución de sistemas de inteligencia artificial.

articles.title: Leak Tips Rainbow Six: Vegas Series Slated To Return From 18-Year Hiatus
articles.text:
Friday, November 13th 2026
Leak Tips Rainbow Six: Vegas Series Slated To Return From 18-Year Hiatus
The last Rainbow Six: Vegas game launched as far back as 2008, and the series has more or less been dormant since then. However, a recent report out of Insider Gaming claims that an insider at Ubisoft has confirmed that a new Rainbow Six: Vegas game is in the works. 
Not much is known about the new Rainbow Six: Vegas game other than that it is in development and that Ubisoft is developing the game in its new Vantage Studios subsidiary, which is partially owned by Tencent. The new game in the Vegas series is known internally by the codename "Spades," and it is one of three new games Ubisoft is working on at Ubisoft Montreal. This also isn't the only Rainbow Six game in development, after Ubisoft's August reveal of Rainbow Six Tactics.

articles.title: European cyber threats are growing much faster than other regions — as new report warns 'AI enables cybercriminals to operate at a scale we’ve never seen before'
articles.text:
European cyber threats are growing much faster than other regions — as new report warns 'AI enables cybercriminals to operate at a scale we’ve never seen before'
AI apps connected via OAuth are a risk many seem to overlook
- Email-borne attacks are increasing, Proofpoint survey finds
- AI-powered apps are creating visibility and identity control problems
- Hospitality and healthcare industries particularly hit
New analysis from Proofpoint has claimed cybersecurity threats are speeding up in Europe faster than anywhere else in the world.
Organizations on the Old Continent are facing increasing numbers of email attacks, rising interest from both state-sponsored and profit-oriented groups, and growing malware infections that don’t discriminate based on industry, organization size, or any other meaningful metric, the company found.
Industries and technologies
In its report, Proofpoint first points the finger at email. This year, its telemetry detected 4.5 times more phishing emails compared to 2025 while, for the rest of the world, that growth has been more modest - 1.5 times. Detections per million inbound messages rose 3.2 times across Europe, it said.
Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks are of particular concern, it seems. These attacks happen when attackers compromise someone’s business email, assume their identity, and reach out to their colleagues, partners, or clients with a seemingly legitimate request. That request usually means wiring funds to an attacker-controlled account, or granting access to valuable business software and data.
Looking at BEC threats specifically, Proofpoint said European electronics companies receive 3.4 times more of these emails than the European average, with supply-chain invoice fraud being the most common pattern.
There are “considerable” variations per industry, the report states. Hospitality and leisure are primarily targeted with malware (21% of all detections, compared to 11% worldwide). Telephone-oriented attack delivery, or callback phishing, has also risen 262% year-on-year. Healthcare organizations are also a major target. TOAD targeting companies in this industry rose 257% compared to 2025, while malware increased 84%. At the same time, malware attacks across Europe are actually declining.
Proofpoint hints as to why Europe seems to be a particular target - people there are more responsive. Apparently, for every 100 threat emails delivered, there were 8.3 clicks, compared to 2.0 worldwide.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The key players remain the same, although there have been a few new - and notable - additions. The researchers primarily mention established Russian and Chinese threat actors who have, over the year evolved their techniques in gaining and maintaining access to European organizations. That includes TA395 (“one of the most prolific actors observed in Proofpoint telemetry”) and TA488, (known for targeting Outlook, Zimbra, and other webmail providers).
However, they also mention India and Pakistan who, historically, were more preoccupied targeting each other. In 2026, it seems, they are shifting their focus on Western Europe, as well.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) isn’t helping, either. Proofpoint says it observed more than 188,000 AI-enabled applications connected through authentication and OAuth frameworks, and while these apps can automate workflows and access APIs and enterprise services at machine speed, they are also opening up visibility and identity control challenges and risks.
Targeting AI building blocks
As a result, threat actors are now also targeting the very mechanisms that enable connectivity - meaning content grants, tokens, and applications with misconfigured privileges.
Almost all (99%) of European organizations observed were targeted by cloud-based attacks, with precision attacks (phishing and session hijacking) proving particularly effective. These attacks impacted 64% of targeted organisations in Europe, proofpoint stressed.
The attackers also going after open source AI technologies such as Langflow and LiteLLM, it was said. “The share of European sensors affected by attacks targeting these AI building blocks increased 4.6× between consecutive 90-day periods, demonstrating how AI infrastructure itself is becoming an increasingly attractive target,” Proofpoint warned.
Breaking in is just means to an end, it seems Across Europe, almost four in five victims (72%) saw threat actors working hard to maintain access, manipulate authentication controls, access files, or abuse compromised mailboxes.

articles.title: Euro-Office libera versões para Windows, Mac e Linux • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Euro-Office libera versões para Windows, Mac e Linux
Pacotes da suíte de escritório Euro-Office para desktops chegam sob o nome Nextcloud Office.
O Euro-Office foi lançado oficialmente em junho de 2026, mas somente agora, em novembro, é que versões da suíte de escritório foram liberadas para instalação imediata no Windows, macOS ou Linux. A novidade tem uma missão desafiadora: ser uma alternativa de código aberto ao Microsoft Office (Microsoft 365).
Se já temos pacotes como o LibreOffice para isso, faz sentido contarmos com mais um? Para os defensores da ideia, faz, pois o projeto consiste em um dos esforços para tornar países da Europa menos dependentes de tecnologias dos Estados Unidos.
Apesar disso, o Euro-Office pode ser usado por pessoas ou organizações de qualquer lugar do mundo. É aqui que o anúncio de hoje ganha sentido: agora, há pacotes de instalação da suíte para Windows em x86 (x64) e Arm (ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon) e Linux (DEB e RPM).
Depois de instalada, a ferramenta permite a edição de textos, planilhas, apresentações (slides) e PDFs, sendo capaz, também, de trabalhar com formatos do Microsoft Office (DOCX, XLSX e PPTX), bem como com os padrões abertos do OpenDocument (ODT, ODS e ODP).
A página de download do Euro-Office é esta aqui. A suíte é gratuita.
Talvez você tenha notado que a página de download e a própria ferramenta têm o nome Nextcloud Office, não Euro-Office. Mas isso não é um engano: o Nextcloud Office (Nextcloud Office Desktop) é a distribuição oficial do Euro-Office para desktops.
Vamos à explicação. A Nextcloud é uma organização alemã, criada em 2016, e uma das participantes do Euro-Office como projeto, junto com outras organizações e colaboradores europeus. Como plataforma, a Nextcloud já oferecia serviços de armazenamento de arquivos nas nuvens, compartilhamento de documentos e colaboração online.
O Nextcloud Office também já existia há algum tempo, mas com ferramentas direcionadas principalmente ao uso via navegador. Até então, a solução era baseada no Collabora Online. Agora, a base passa a ser o Euro-Office que, por sua vez, é um fork do OnlyOffice, vale relembrar.

articles.title: El USB del espacio: Europa crea un conector universal para reparar satélites en órbita en lugar de tirarlos
articles.text:
¿Te imaginas que tu móvil se queda sin batería o te da el más mínimo fallo, lo tiras a la basura y te compras otro? Básicamente eso es lo que se hace con los satélites en el espacio. Cuando se quedan sin combustible o sufren algún daño, generalmente se abandonan y se sustituyen, de modo que el viejo pasa a engrosar las filas de la basura espacial. Lo ideal sería enviar naves capaces de transmitir energía, datos, calor y otros recursos necesarios para reparar los satélites, de modo que puedan seguir usándose. Sin embargo, eso requiere el uso de conectores compatibles tanto con el satélite como con la nave de reparación.
Ante este problema, un equipo de investigadores europeos ha desarrollado un conector universal que valdría para la tecnología de distintos tipos de satélite. Se llama Space USB y de momento solo se ha probado en laboratorio, pero con muy buenos resultados.
Dos años de desarrollo. El proyecto Space USB se puso en marcha el 1 de enero de 2024 y finalizó el 31 de diciembre de 2025, gracias al trabajo de un equipo de científicos coordinado por Raphael Boissonnade, de Thales Alenia Space Francia. El objetivo, a grandes rasgos, era buscar una interfaz común a todas las tecnologías satelitales que hay en el espacio. Se bautizó como Space USB porque el principio es muy parecido al del sistema USB que se emplea en tecnologías informáticas terrestres. A grandes rasgos, además de garantizar la conexión de tecnologías distintas, el dispositivo debía ser ligero y compacto, acoplarse en pocos minutos y requerir poca fuerza para fijarse.
Demostración en laboratorio. Finalizados los años de desarrollo se fabricó un dispositivo de prueba, por lo que a continuación se pasó a los test de laboratorio. Se ha probado con tres conectores robóticos estándar desarrollados por empresas europeas distintas, llamados HOTDOCK, SIROM e iSSI. Todos son capaces de unir módulos o equipos en el espacio y transferir entre ellos carga mecánica, energía eléctrica y datos. Sin embargo, normalmente lo hacen solo con equipos que usen su misma tecnología. Por ejemplo, HOTDOCK con HOTDOCK, pero nunca HOTDOCK con SIROM. Gracias al prototipo de Space USB, esto segundo sí ha sido posible.
Construcción en órbita. Si este tipo de conectores llegan a usarse ampliamente favorecerán la reutilización de satélites, disminuyendo la basura espacial. Sin embargo, esa no sería su única ventaja. Por ejemplo, también podrían facilitar el trabajo de los robots de construcción en órbita. Caltech ha probado recientemente uno de estos robots, convirtiéndose en una institución pionera, pero el objetivo es que en el futuro haya más empresas y centros de investigación trabajando en ello, por lo que un conector universal sería una herramienta indispensable.
Aún es pronto. Actualmente, el prototipo está en fase TRL 3. Eso significa que se ha probado en laboratorio, pero sin ni siquiera simular las condiciones espaciales, en las que se incluirían parámetros como el vacío o la radiación. Se sabe que puede conectar distintas tecnologías, pero no como lo haría en su destino final. Además, el conector que se ha usado es un poco más grande de lo que sería la versión definitiva. Todo esto nos indica que este USB del espacio está aún en pañales, pero también que va por el buen camino. Habrá que esperar para saber cómo evoluciona el proyecto.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday, ce TV 4K de 55 pouces de Samsung perd plus de 200 € sur Amazon
articles.text:
Le Samsung TV AI 55QN80F ne se contente pas de faire le bonheur des cinéphiles puisqu’il ravira aussi les joueurs. En cette période de Black Friday, il passe sous les 570 euros.
Nous sommes entrés dans le mois de novembre et l’été n’est plus qu’un lointain souvenir qui a laissé place à des nuits bien froides. L’occasion est donc parfaite pour passer des soirées devant Netflix ou Disney+. Pour cela, vous avez besoin d’un téléviseur performant. Bonne nouvelle, le Samsung TV AI 55QN80F est en promotion chez Amazon durant le Black Friday.
Le Samsung TV AI 55QN80F est actuellement disponible pour 579 euros au lieu de 799 euros.
Pourquoi choisir le Samsung TV AI 55QN80F ?
- Pour son image : Si le Samsung TV AI 55QN80F fourmille de technologies, il n’oublie pas le plus important : offrir une belle image. Ainsi, ce TV dispose d’un affichage en 4K UHD.
- Pour l’IA : L’intelligence artificielle est un vrai argument de vente de ce Samsung TV AI 55QN80F puisqu'on la retrouve partout. Elle se charge d’améliorer le rendu vidéo ou d’optimiser le son afin de, par exemple, rendre les dialogues plus intelligibles.
- Pour les quatre ports HDMI 2.1 : Les gamers ne sont pas laissés sur le côté avec ce TV puisqu’il embarque quatre ports HDMI 2.1 pour jouer aux consoles récentes en 4K à 144 Hz.
Des soirées cinéma aux petits oignons
Le Samsung TV AI 55QN80F est un TV assez classique au premier abord. Il est fin et il présente l’avantage de disposer d’un pied central pour être installé même sur un meuble TV plus petit que lui. Vous pourrez même faire l’impasse sur ce pied si vous choisissez de l’accrocher au mur puisqu’il est compatible VESA.
Vous l’aurez compris, le principal argument de vente de ce téléviseur, ce n’est pas son design, mais évidemment la qualité de son image. Ce Samsung TV AI 55QN80F possède une dalle QLED avec un affichage en 4K.
Pour améliorer l’expérience, ce téléviseur tourne avec le processeur NQ4 AI Gen2. Celui-ci se sert de l’intelligence artificielle pour améliorer le rendu vidéo. Une technologie qui prend tout son sens si vous avez besoin d’adapter des films anciens à la taille de l’écran sans perdre en qualité.
Samsung pense aussi aux joueurs
Si l’expérience vidéo est une réussite, la partie audio souffle le chaud et le froid. Pour commencer par les bons points, le Dolby Atmos est présent pour une expérience sonore immersive qui donne l’impression que le son vous englobe. Sur le papier, c’est une bonne idée, en pratique, le rendu est mitigé. La cause de tous les problèmes de ce Samsung TV AI 55QN80F est la puissance limitée de ces haut-parleurs à part si vous avez un petit salon.
Samsung a bien conscience de ce défaut. Preuve en est, le TV est compatible avec Q-Symphony pour synchroniser une barre de son de la marque et avoir une meilleure expérience sans aucune latence.
Enfin, les joueurs seront ravis avec ce TV. Il possède quatre ports HDMI 2.1, ce qui permet de connecter votre PlayStation 5 ou votre Xbox Series X/S et de jouer en 4K à 144 Hz. Un Gaming Hub est présent pour affiner les paramètres si nécessaire.
✅ Les points forts
- La présence du Dolby Atmos
- Un écran 4K boosté par l’intelligence artificielle
- 4 ports HDMI 2.1 pour le gaming
❌ Les limites
- Le Dolby Atmos, mais pas de Dolby Vision
- Un rendu audio qui manque de peps, mais le Q-Symphony est présent en renfort
Vendu habituellement pour 729 euros, le Samsung TV AI 55QN80F profite du Black Friday pour chuter à 579 euros sur Amazon.
Logiquement, pour ce prix contenu, le Samsung TV AI 55QN80F fait l’impasse sur l’OLED. Hormis cette absence, l’appareil de Samsung réussit à être un TV polyvalent qui pourra plaire à toute la famille.
Seule la puissance des haut-parleurs peut soulever quelques questions, mais pour un TV en promotion, ce n’est pas gênant de faire quelques concessions.

articles.title: Data management layer eases VMware exit for Kubernetes teams - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Leaving VMware starts as a cost decision, but day-two operations decide whether it works
Enterprises leaving legacy hypervisors are finding that moving virtual machines is only half the job, and that a portable data management layer often decides whether a Kubernetes migration succeeds. Rising license costs are pushing teams to run containers and VMs on one platform.
That shift is playing out at Mouser Electronics Inc., one of the world’s largest electronic components distributors. After running Red Hat Inc.’s OpenShift for containers for five to six years, the company is now building a production OpenShift Virtualization cluster to move workloads off Broadcom Inc.’s VMware, according to Ronald Waller (pictured, left), systems engineer at Mouser.
“It doesn’t matter if we’re running containers or VMs, we’re running it on the same foundation, which really works well,” Waller said. “Because we can manage those things with the same tool sets and same skill sets.”
Waller and Jon Owings (right), assistant vice president of global technical presales, cloud and data services, at Portworx by Everpure, spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how the data management layer helps run VMs and containers on OpenShift. (* Disclosure below.)
A data management layer for VMs and containers
Kubernetes already serves as a common control plane for containerized AI workloads, and pulling VMs onto it extends that standard to older applications. Everpure Inc., which rebranded from Pure Storage Inc. this year as part of a data-centric pivot, positions Portworx as the matching abstraction for storage.
“Kubernetes provides that ubiquitous control plane for all of them, and that’s what customers are asking us for,” Owings said. “The one thing that was missing was the same thing but for data.”
The learning curve for VMware administrators moving to Kubernetes is steep, and Waller has climbed it over the last year. Storage turned out to be the easy part when he built Mouser’s proof-of-concept cluster, he explained.
“I asked the storage guy what I needed from him, and he handed me a user ID and an API key. I went to Portworx Central. I configured my spec for the operator and the storage cluster, created my secret, and boom, Portworx Enterprise did everything else on the backend,” Waller said. “I didn’t even have to think about it.”
Portworx keeps building for that use case. It made data management native to OpenShift in May and unveiled new AI and VM capabilities at KubeCon. For teams following Mouser’s path, Owings sees the exit from a legacy hypervisor as a chance to rethink day-two operations on a data management layer that travels across clouds and Kubernetes distributions.
“What can we change that we didn’t like about the last 15 years? … Were we dependent on a vendor? Were we dependent on shell scripts or PowerShell?” Owings said. “We have this great opportunity to do something new, and Kubernetes has that open API that allows you to be creative.”

articles.title: Corea del Sur confirmó que Google cumplió las condiciones de seguridad para exportar mapas detallados del país
articles.text:
El Gobierno de Corea del Sur confirmó que Google cumplió las condiciones de seguridad que le exigió para exportar mapas detallados del país a sus servidores en el extranjero. El Ministerio de Tierra, Infraestructura y Transporte lo informó tras una reunión de un comité con funcionarios y expertos privados, un paso hacia la navegación completa en Google Maps.
Seúl había aprobado el pedido de forma condicionada el 27 de febrero, tras 19 años de disputa. Google entregó su informe final sobre las medidas el 4 de noviembre. Según el ministerio, la empresa eliminó las coordenadas de latitud y longitud del territorio surcoreano de Google Maps y Google Earth, en sus versiones web y móvil.
Para evitar que reaparezcan, Google desarrolló un sistema de control exclusivo para Corea del Sur que bloquea las actualizaciones de sus aplicaciones si detecta información de ubicación restringida.
La exportación abarca solo los mapas base y los datos de transporte: calles, nombres de rutas, cantidad de carriles, límites de velocidad y trazado de las vías. Un socio coreano procesará esa información en servidores del país, y Google deberá cargarla sin modificar la forma del terreno.
Bases militares ocultas y un socio local
Los mapas pedidos son de escala 1:5.000, en los que un centímetro equivale a 50 metros reales. Según el medio coreano MK, permiten identificar rutas, formas de edificios y variaciones de altura del terreno, también alrededor de instalaciones militares, y por eso las autoridades rechazaban estos pedidos de las grandes tecnológicas.
Google ocultó de forma temporal los sitios sensibles que identificó con imágenes satelitales comerciales de proveedores extranjeros, incluidas las imágenes históricas de Google Earth. También retiró las fotos de Street View de esas instalaciones y de las calles a menos de 50 metros de sus límites.
Esa etapa no está terminada. Según un acuerdo firmado el 31 de agosto, la empresa recibirá imágenes satelitales procesadas por el Instituto Geográfico Nacional a través de un socio local y deberá reemplazar las actuales apenas estén disponibles. The Korea Herald informó que el socio elegido para procesar los datos de mapas es Tmap Mobility.
Control del gobierno y respuesta en un día
El presidente de Google Corea será el contacto local para temas de mapas. La compañía montó un sistema de atención las 24 horas para las solicitudes oficiales: si el gobierno detecta una infracción, como una instalación de seguridad visible, la actualización debe estar hecha en un día hábil.
La empresa también preparó medidas para emergencias de seguridad nacional, como conflictos armados o grandes desastres naturales. En esos casos podría ajustar las zonas restringidas o desactivar funciones de mapas en consulta con el gobierno. Además, se comprometió a un programa de cooperación de varios años con la industria geoespacial coreana.
En febrero, Reuters había anticipado que la decisión perjudicaría a Naver y Kakao, que dominan los mapas digitales en Corea del Sur. Aquel despacho señalaba que el país era uno de los pocos donde Google Maps no funcionaba con todas sus prestaciones.
Un funcionario del comité dijo que seguirán de cerca la exportación de datos e imágenes procesados y que comprobarán si las restricciones de coordenadas se mantienen. Las violaciones graves pueden llevar a suspender o revocar el permiso, y Google quedará sujeta a las órdenes correctivas que rigen para los proveedores locales.

articles.title: AI privacy starts with your data
articles.text:
AI privacy starts with your data
Protecting data privacy as AI gains greater access and autonomy
As businesses give AI applications and agents access to more internal systems, data privacy is becoming harder to manage. Much of the focus has been on the risk of AI models surfacing sensitive or confidential information in their responses. But the privacy challenge starts earlier. Organizations also need to understand what data AI systems can access in the first place, where that data comes from and how it is being used.
Technical Product Marketing Director at Qlik.
That challenge is already holding AI adoption back. 95% of enterprises have delayed or cancelled AI projects because of infrastructure and data governance challenges. As AI gains greater autonomy and access to company data, businesses need to get the foundations right before privacy risks become impossible to contain.
Before information reaches the model
Data privacy is not just a legal or compliance concern. It should matter to everyone who touches data within an organization. With AI, the consequences of getting it wrong are growing, from exposing sensitive information to damaging customer trust and brand reputation.
These risks can emerge before sensitive data ever reaches an AI model. Poorly classified, duplicated or outdated data can carry existing privacy problems into AI applications, turning weaknesses previously contained within individual systems into much wider risks.
Agentic AI raises the stakes further. As agents gain greater autonomy and access to more company systems, they can increasingly surface and act on information across multiple parts of the business. A privacy issue that was once contained within a single dataset or system can therefore become much harder to control.
Know where sensitive data is going
Identifying sensitive data is only the first step in managing that privacy challenge. Businesses also need to track where it moves, particularly when information is copied from live systems into testing or development environments which may not have the same security controls in place.
Personally identifiable information (PII), such as names, addresses or financial details, should be clearly labelled so it can be spotted before it is moved. Wherever possible, sensitive information should remain within the live systems where it is needed. If it does need to be used elsewhere, removing or masking identifying details can reduce the risk of unnecessary exposure.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The same principle applies when data is moved from existing systems into cloud platforms or prepared for AI. Maintaining accurate metadata - information that describes what data contains and where it came from - can make sensitive information easier to identify and trace. Combined with a clear record of how data has moved and changed, this helps businesses spot privacy risks before information ends up somewhere it shouldn't.
Scaling AI without scaling the risk
Knowing where sensitive data sits and moves provides an important foundation, but these safeguards also need to work as AI tool use grows. The gap between AI ambition and data readiness remains significant, with recent research finding that while 97% of organizations have active AI initiatives, just 5% believe their data is fully ready to support them. Privacy, compliance and poor data quality remain key barriers.
Managing these risks at scale means building checks into how data is handled. Businesses should automate data transformation and monitor data quality continuously, while automatically recording where data came from, how it has changed and which AI applications use it. This helps teams prioritize higher-risk data and quickly investigate unexpected changes or quality issues.
Training data also needs regular scrutiny. Organizations need to check for inaccurate or biased information that could lead to unreliable or discriminatory results, while ensuring personal data is only used where appropriate and individuals' rights are respected. Making responsible data use part of how AI is developed and deployed can help create a more secure environment and build confidence in the resulting services.
Keep access and retention under control
But getting data into good order is not the end of the privacy challenge. Businesses also need to regularly check who can access sensitive information and whether that access is still appropriate. One practical step is to compare access permissions with HR records for people joining, leaving or changing roles.
This can flag cases where employees retain access to information they no longer need. The same principle should apply to AI systems and agents: access should be limited to the information needed for a specific task, rather than giving them blanket access to company data.
Managing data responsibly also means questioning whether information still needs to be kept. Businesses can regularly identify personal or customer data that is no longer required and flag it for deletion in line with retention policies. Holding less unnecessary sensitive data reduces the amount of information that could be exposed, helping firms reduce privacy risk and protect customer trust.
Building trust as AI evolves
Clear regulation will become increasingly important as AI becomes more capable and takes on greater responsibility in everyday business. Where AI is used to make or inform decisions involving personal data, clear privacy rules can give organizations the guardrails to innovate while ensuring progress does not come at the expense of protecting people’s information.
By embracing responsible AI practices, organizations can harness the power of AI while protecting fundamental rights and fostering greater trust in its outcomes.

articles.title: Démission de Jensen Huang chez NVIDIA : pourquoi l'avenir de l'IA est remis en question
articles.text:
Jensen Huang a quitté NVIDIA, et l’on se rend un peu plus compte à quel point l’industrie dépendait de lui. Distribution des puces, financements géants, défense de l’open source… Tout passait par l’emblématique patron à la veste de cuir.
Cette dernière semaine a résonné comme un véritable coup de tonnerre dans l’écosystème de l’intelligence artificielle (IA). Jensen Huang, P.-D.G incontesté de l’entreprise la plus valorisée au monde, a démissionné.
En cause, une relation extraconjugale avec une espionne chinoise présumée, mais également avec l'une de ses subordonnées directes au sein de NVIDIA. Au-delà de l’impact interne, cette décision risque de créer une véritable onde de choc dans la tech, et même en dehors.
Un patron omnipotent
Car chez NVIDIA, Huang dirigeait tout d'une main de maître. Le conseil d’administration est donc chargé de trouver un successeur pour une entreprise dirigée par une figure unique sans véritable second. Jensen Huang avait évidemment des lieutenants ; on pense à Colette Kress, la directrice financière qui a pris la relève en attendant la nomination d’un successeur, et à Vishal Bhagwati, responsable du développement de l’entreprise.
Mais l’ensemble des grandes décisions revenaient au P.-D.G. À tel point que pour certains financements, ses équipes attendaient sur place l’atterrissage de son avion pour obtenir son feu vert. Une concentration du pouvoir qui pèse lourd quand on considère à quel point NVIDIA pèse sur le marché. L’entreprise contrôle près de 80 % des puces IA, et Jensen Huang décide comment, quand et où ses GPU sont distribués.
Les premiers servis sont les « hyperscalers » : Amazon, Google, Meta et Microsoft, qui ont besoin de ces puces pour bâtir leurs propres services d’IA et les proposer à leurs clients cloud. OpenAI figure aussi parmi les gros acheteurs. Mais pour élargir sa clientèle, Huang a aussi réservé de la capacité à des neoclouds comme CoreWeave et Nebius, en entrant à leur capital pour les aider à bâtir leur activité de location de GPU. Toutes ces entreprises n’hésitent pas à s’endetter massivement pour mettre la main sur les précieuses cartes graphiques, à l’instar d’Oracle ou de SpaceX.
Huang voulait aussi que le monde se standardise sur NVIDIA, et il savait imposer ses conditions. Difficile de savoir qui sera en mesure de reprendre ce rôle d’arbitre.
Le financement de l’IA repose sur NVIDIA
Mais NVIDIA ne se contente pas de vendre des puces, elle finance aussi ceux qui les achètent. Ce sont les fameux « deals circulaires », qui attirent de plus en plus les régulateurs. Le principe : NVIDIA prend des parts dans des sociétés pour financer leur expansion, afin que celles-ci puissent lui acheter ses puces. Ces engagements atteignaient 750 milliards de dollars en juillet. Un mois plus tard, la firme est allée encore plus loin en garantissant jusqu’à 105 milliards de dollars de financement pour un data center d’OpenAI dans l’Ohio, qui pourrait devenir le plus grand du monde.
Mais ce n’est pas tout, car Jensen Huang a aussi convaincu Wall Street de mettre la main au portefeuille. Toujours en août, il a réuni les géants de la finance Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs et KKR, qui se sont ensuite engagés à hauteur de 500 milliards de dollars pour des centres de données. Son pari : faire des GPU des » actifs investissables », en leur promettant que ces puces conserveraient leur valeur et pourraient servir de garantie.
Problème, les prêteurs commencent à se lasser. Sur environ 80 milliards de dollars d’obligations émises cette année pour des data centers, près de la moitié est classée à haut risque. Et surtout, les promesses reposent souvent sur la crédibilité de Jensen Huang.
Dans ce contexte, la Bourse commence évidemment à sanctionner NVIDIA : le cours de son action a chuté sur 5 jours consécutifs, et il est sur le point d'enregistrer sa plus longue série dans le négatif depuis 2012.
Un poids lourd très écouté dans l’industrie
Autre point notable, Jensen Huang est un fervent défenseur des modèles dits « open-weight », c’est-à-dire ouverts et pouvant être utilisés librement. Preuve en est avec le rachat récent de Hugging Face pour 12,9 milliards de dollars. Une opération qui doit encore recevoir l’aval des régulateurs pour se conclure au premier semestre 2027.
Au mois de juillet, alors qu’Anthropic et OpenAI auraient poussé l’administration Trump à interdire les modèles chinois, il a réuni des centaines d’entreprises autour d’une lettre de soutien aux modèles ouverts en général. Un énième exemple de la capacité du dirigeant à fédérer autour d’une cause.
D’autant qu’il défend aussi l’autorégulation. Après les incidents d’agents IA qui ont piraté des réseaux, il a répété à maintes reprises que le secteur n’a pas besoin de régulation. Selon lui, les alertes sur l’IA sont infondées, une parole cruciale dans une industrie divisée autour des risques de la technologie.
Sources : CNBC, TechCrunch
Un hyperscaler est un opérateur cloud capable de déployer des infrastructures à très grande échelle (centres de données massifs, réseau mondial, capacité d’achats colossale). Ces groupes (comme AWS, Google, Microsoft ou Meta) achètent des GPU IA en volume pour entraîner des modèles et fournir des services d’IA à leurs propres clients. Leur priorité vient de leur puissance de commande, de contrats pluriannuels et d’une capacité à intégrer très vite le matériel dans des plateformes déjà industrialisées. Dans un marché sous contrainte, être un hyperscaler aide à sécuriser des livraisons, des options de production et parfois des conditions d’approvisionnement plus stables.
Un néocloud est un acteur cloud plus spécialisé, souvent centré sur la location de ressources GPU pour l’IA plutôt que sur une offre cloud généraliste. Son activité consiste à acheter (ou réserver) beaucoup de GPU, les installer en data centers, puis les louer à l’heure ou au mois à des entreprises qui veulent entraîner ou exécuter des modèles. Le point critique, c’est que les GPU IA coûtent très cher et s’achètent souvent avant que les revenus ne soient totalement sécurisés, d’où un recours important à la dette ou aux levées de fonds. Si l’accès au capital se tend ou si les livraisons ralentissent, le modèle peut se retrouver sous pression (retard d’ouverture de capacité, rentabilité décalée, risque de surcapacité).
Contrôler la distribution signifie arbitrier qui reçoit les volumes disponibles, à quel rythme, et parfois avec quelles configurations (cartes, serveurs, interconnexions) et quelles conditions contractuelles. Dans un contexte de production limitée, l’allocation devient un levier stratégique : elle peut favoriser certains segments (cloud géant, startups, laboratoires) et en freiner d’autres. Cela influence directement la vitesse à laquelle les concurrents peuvent entraîner des modèles, lancer des services ou baisser leurs coûts. Cet effet se renforce quand l’écosystème logiciel et les outils de développement sont fortement optimisés pour une même plateforme matérielle, ce qui augmente les coûts de bascule vers des alternatives.

articles.title: Muchos anuncios de GTA VI no muestran armas: no es que el juego se haya moderado, es que Rockstar sabe que muchos jugadores son menores
articles.text:
Estamos viendo, desde hace un par de días, cómo las ciudades se van empapelando con carteles de 'GTA VI', para cuyo lanzamiento queda apenas una semana. Algunos de los ejemplos más espectaculares están en París, donde Rockstar ha colocado unos Lucia y Jason de 3.000 metros cuadrados en la fachada acristalada del Westfield CNIT. Y también en Paris se censuró una imagen de una pistola. Mientras tanto, en la televisión estadounidense lo que sale de los spots es el sexo. Todo ello nos lleva a una cuestión que va mucho más allá de una maniobra publicitaria puntual, y es cómo afrontamos la publicidad de un juego para adultos... que quiere llegar a todo el mundo.
Pistolas fuera. El pasado 18 de junio, Rockstar enseñó la portada oficial de 'GTA VI' al anunciar la fecha de reservas: la cuadrícula de viñetas propia de la saga, con Jason y Lucia en el panel central superior. Pronto surgieron comparaciones con la lona terminada, a partir de fotos de la web francesa Rockstar Mag. En el recuadro de la pareja, la pistola de Lucia y la mano que la sostenía desaparecieron. En la viñeta inferior central, un personaje levanta el brazo hacia un fusil de asalto que también se esfumó.
Solo fue el principio. El 15 de octubre veíamos una pantalla LED en Times Square sin armas y después, otra de un autobús en Chicago donde a Lucia también le faltaba la pistola. Se había hablado del retoque como un ajuste pensado solo para París, pero pronto se vio que era una cuestión internacional. De hecho, en Nueva York conviven incluso ambas imágenes: en la Séptima Avenida con la calle 49, la pistola de Lucia y el fusil siguen en su sitio.
En la tele. El 20 de octubre, durante la noche inaugural de la NBA, NBC emitió el primer anuncio de televisión del juego, el tráiler de lanzamiento que Rockstar había publicado cinco días antes, pero con cambios: de las tres escenas de la pareja en la ducha solo queda la primera, mientras que las armas, las explosiones y los atracos se mantienen. En la versión oficial, la pareja protagoniza varios cortes íntimos repartidos por el minuto y medio.
El motivo de la censura: el juego tiene la calificación M de la ESRB, con descriptores como violencia intensa, desnudez y contenido sexual. La ESRB puede imponer multas de hasta un millón de dólares a las editoras que no respeten esas pautas como evitar desnudez o armas apuntando al espectador.
Las contradicciones de un juego violento. Joost Van Dreunen, profesor de negocio del videojuego en la NYU, recordaba esta semana que parte del gancho de Rockstar era ser el juego que "mi madre no me deja jugar". ¿Puede conservar Rockstar ese mojo con GTA VI? Posiblemente la compañía decide qué y cómo censura soporte a soporte, según quién gestiona la publicidad y a qué tipo de público alcanza. Una lona no tiene franja horaria ni filtro de edad, pero un anuncio en la NBA llega a una audiencia muy específica, y ahí Rockstar ha cortado el sexo. Para un juego que ha puesto la relación entre Jason y Lucia en el centro de su trama, cada recorte se mide milimétricamente.
Eso sin contar con la nada disimulada censura que en lugares como los Emiratos Árabes que difuminan a las mujeres de portada y carátulas del juego, aunque aquí no es Rockstar quien tiene la última palabra.
Menores mayores. Strauss Zelnick, CEO de Take-Two, decía en marzo que no entendía cómo alguien con consola y más de 17 años podía decidir no jugarlo, y que esperaba llegar a "cada persona apropiada", un adjetivo que deja fuera muy conscientemente a los menores de edad. Sin embargo, en una encuesta de YouGov publicada esta semana, el 63% de los británicos que han jugado a 'GTA' lo hizo por primera vez antes de los 18 años, y uno de cada cinco antes de los 12. Christoph Hartmann, exjefe de 2K, contaba que su hijo de 14 años insiste en jugarlo porque su padre trabajó en él.
Visto así, una compañía que necesita la mayor audiencia posible no puede reconocer abiertamente que parte de ella no tiene la edad que exige la calificación correspondiente, y quitarle la pistola a Lucia en una fachada es una forma de asumirlo sin entrar en polémicas morales. De momento, tenemos anuncios con y sin pistolas. Por si acaso.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt departure shakes AI industry's foundations - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure shakes AI industry’s foundations
Oh, Jensen… really?
Honeypot or not, the Chinese executive/accused spy with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair this week should have been a flashing red light to him. So should fraternizing with one of your own VPs — and reportedly another employee too!
In the end, all that, and maybe more to come, was just too much for Nvidia’s board to bear despite the commanding position Huang (pictured) held not only at Nvidia but in the entire artificial intelligence industry. Indeed, the speed with which he resigned — spectacularly stupid as his behavior was — still makes me wonder if there are other shoes to drop, especially on the legal or national security fronts. Market researcher SemiAnalysis thinks it came down to pressure from the U.S. intelligence community that’s very unhappy Nvidia chips have apparently been smuggled to China.
Huang was something of an AI puppet master, providing the chips and software to power the entire industry as well as seemingly unlimited cash to fund and backstop everyone from AI leaders such as OpenAI and Anthropic to innumerable cloud compute providers worldwide. No single person inside or outside Nvidia seems likely to fill that role.
However, Nvidia really is much more than Jensen Huang. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress helped craft the financial arrangements that in part put Nvidia at the center of AI — though for what it’s worth, Huang himself wasn’t a fan lately. Some of his direct reports such as high-performance computing chief Ian Buck seem quite capable of carrying on, if perhaps not with Huang’s panache. One company is never one person, and shouldn’t be. I expect a less centralized Nvidia going forward, whoever’s at the top.
More than that, AI is much more than Jensen Huang, and it will continue to be going forward. It’s easy to forget that although Huang brilliantly helped create this new wave, AI and its enablers also are what made him a rock star. But that time is now over. Nvidia and certainly the AI industry shouldn’t be depending on one person to keep everything afloat anyway.
The reverberations of his sudden and shocking departure will continue to echo for a long time to come across Nvidia, its investors watching hundreds of billions of market cap evaporate, legions of Jensen fanboys and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem. A lot of people are hoping desperately that he didn’t just pop the AI bubble (though others are hoping he did). It seems unlikely this will be the pin, but we’re dealing with a lot of unlikely things in the past week or so, for better and worse, and this shock is clearly rattling the foundations.
All that managed to overshadow what otherwise would be the big news this week: Anthropic went on the road to pitch its initial public offering. It’s hoping to raise more than $64 billion and keep the AI trade humming in Nvidia’s near-term absence. Looks like next Thursday is the big day.
And it’s not the only good news in AI — that is, if the IPO is successful. After a difficult month on the stock front, uber neocloud CoreWeave provided a pleasant AI surprise with upside earnings and guidance, lifting its shares almost 25% Wednesday. AI chipmaker Cerebras’ shares rose almost 18% in late trading Thursday on positive guidance and a Microsoft deal. Cisco Systems said demand is strong for AI infrastructure, even if investors shrugged, and chipmaking equipment supplier Applied Materials said AI boosted demand as well.
Not everyone fared so well, though. Dutch neocloud Nebius saw its shares drop almost 17% Thursday as it lowered its outlook despite close to sevenfold revenue growth in the last quarter. The stock drop no doubt was partly because of Nvidia, which is, of course, an investor. CoreWeave –yes, another Nvidia investment — lost 7% Thursday.
Sovereignty is on many enterprise buyers’ lips these days, the notion that enterprises need a way to assert more control over their technology estates and protect their customers’ data. TheCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and Amit Eyal Govrin just completed the first of a series of reports on how to approach sovereignty, this one focused on the hyperscale cloud providers.
The software orchestrator Kubernetes has become boring, but as SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier said at this week’s KubeCon in Salt Lake City, that means it’s a success — with lessons for AI developers. “A lot of things that are happening in cloud-native that were involved in microservices in Kubernetes world are actually the same challenges in the AI world,” he noted.
IBM has been working hard on quantum computing for a long time now, but at its Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago this week, it showed significant progress, according to Dave Vellante. Its goal now is to show actual industry impact by 2028, a laudable goal that presents a lot of challenges, Dave said in his Special Breaking Analysis this week.
Next week the SC26 high-performance computing conference comes to Chicago, and theCUBE and theCUBE Research will be onsite with interviews and analysis. There’s also Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco. And earnings next week include… Nvidia! Bring the popcorn.
Here’s all of this week’s enterprise and emerging tech news, most of it not salacious, along with analysis and commentary from SiliconANGLE and beyond:
Analysis, opinion and food for thought
Breaking Analysis: Sovereign or not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide
Breaking Analysis: AI cyber resilience and the trust gap
Dario goes overboard with AI claims ahead of Anthropic’s IPO — the same guy who says AI could also extinguish us. Somebody give him back his Xanax! Also, I really don’t think mental illness is a compute problem.
Gartner forecasts AI infrastructure spending to represent 59% of total global AI spending in 2027
Gartner also forecasts AI will drive a net increase of 1.7M jobs by 2030 That one number hides a lot of job losses and especially job “transformations,” and not to throw shade on Gartner in particular, anyone betting on AI’s impact out in 2030 is barely more than guessing.
United Airlines is banning AI bots from booking flights, following Amazon and Walmart doing the same thing for shopping. Aren’t travel and shopping a prime use case for AI agents?
Getting too close to Trump was a mistake, says Nick Clegg. Amen. We’ve already seen them trying to backpedal, starting with Palantir CEO Alex Karp, who had the audacity to call his company “progressive.” Dude, sit down.

articles.title: Razer Introduces the Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics Gaming Chairs
articles.text:
Friday, November 13th 2026
Razer Introduces the Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics Gaming Chairs
Razer, the leading global lifestyle brand for gamers, today announced the Razer Soma Pro and the Razer Soma Sensa HD Haptics, two gaming chairs with wireless connectivity that bring haptics into the seat, with the Soma Pro adding THX Spatial Audio and Razer Chroma RGB for a complete immersive experience.
Following the debut of the Soma Chroma, Razer's first RGB gaming chair, the Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics complete a line built on one idea: immersion has evolved through sight and sound, yet the chair often stayed on the sidelines. Both chairs turn the seat into an active part of every session - built for gaming first, and just as immersive for movies, music, and streaming.
Addie Tan, Global Head of Lifestyle Division at Razer"The Soma Pro is where the chair finally joins the game. For years, gamers have upgraded everything they see and hear, while the seat they spend every session in stayed on the sidelines. With Soma Pro, the chair becomes part of the game - you feel it, hear it and see it."
Feel It. Hear It. See It.
Bringing sight, sound, and touch to the seat, the Soma Pro is the only gaming chair to combine the Razer Sensa HD Haptics, THX Spatial Audio, and Razer Chroma RGB.
Powered by Razer Sensa HD Haptics, six haptic motor actuators programmed with advanced algorithms deliver multi-zone feedback that is designed to match the intensity, direction, and distance of in-game action as it unfolds in real time.The result is dynamic, lifelike sensation rather than simple rumble, so hits and explosions are felt as well as seen and heard. Enabled through the downloadable Razer Synapse software and built into the seat with no external accessories required, Sensa HD Haptics also converts audio into haptics for movies, music, and games without native support.
With THX Spatial Audio enabled, the Soma Pro's built-in speakers deliver immersive surround sound that integrates seamlessly with multiple audio setups. Players can use it solo or pair it with front speakers for a widened soundstage with greater precision and depth, with the chair at the center.Razer Chroma RGB Reactive Game Lighting responds to the action on screen with 16.8 million colors and dynamic effects custom-made for more than 300 integrated games. Players can sync the chair with the rest of their Razer setup through Razer Synapse for a fully immersive visual experience.All-Day Comfort. Effortless Control.
Both chairs are built for long sessions. A Built-In Lumbar Arch gently supports the lower back and is designed to encourage a neutral sitting position to ease fatigue, while a Dual-Density Cold-Cured Foam Seat Cushion pairs a plush upper layer for immediate pressure relief with a resilient core for solid support. The backrest reclines up to 132°, moving from upright, competition-ready play to a full lean-back for a movie.
The Soma Pro also features 4D armrests, a magnetic head cushion, a frog tilt mechanism, and a 5-star powder-coated aluminium alloy wheelbase for the most adjustable, premium fit in the line.
A Built-In Control Panel keeps everything within reach, letting players tweak settings and switch between Razer HyperSpeed Wireless (2.4 GHz) and Bluetooth LE connections at the touch of a button.
A single USB Type-C connection draws power from either a wall outlet or a compatible standard power bank for a pristine, wireless-aesthetic setup, while a steel frame gives both chairs the durability and stability to anchor the battlestation through years of daily use. Both chairs are backed by a 3-year warranty on mechanisms and moving parts and a 2-year warranty on electronic parts.
Razer Soma Sensa HD Haptics: Feel Every Moment
For gamers who want to feel the action, the Soma Sensa HD Haptics brings Razer Sensa HD Haptics to an all-day comfort chair. Six haptic motor actuators drive multi-directional feedback, designed to convey the intensity, direction, and distance of in-game events in real time, unlocking hyperrealistic sensations for games, films, and more. Players can adjust haptic intensity and cycle through haptic profiles directly from the Built-In Control Panel.Two New Chairs. One Immersive Line.
- Immersion: The Soma Pro unites Razer Sensa HD Haptics, THX Spatial Audio, and Razer Chroma RGB in one seat, while the Soma Sensa HD Haptics brings six-actuator HD haptic feedback to a wireless, all-day comfort chair.
- Comfort: A Built-In Lumbar Arch and Dual-Density Cold-Cured Foam Seat Cushion on both chairs, with the Soma Pro adding 4D armrests, a magnetic head cushion, and a frog tilt mechanism for the most adjustable fit in the line.
- Convenience: A Built-In Control Panel, single USB Type-C power from a wall outlet or standard power bank, and a premium steel frame to anchor the battlestation on both chairs.
True Integration. Pure Immersion. Feel the action with the Soma Sensa HD Haptics or experience total sight, sound, and touch immersion with the Soma Pro; the new Soma chairs are built for anyone who wants their chair to be part of the experience, not just the setup.
