articles.title: Razorpay, Sembcorp Green Infra get Sebi nod to float IPOs
articles.text:
Razorpay, Sembcorp Green Infra get Sebi nod to float IPOs
Razorpay filed draft documents with Sebi via the confidential route in June for an IPO.
Fintech firm Razorpay Software Ltd and Sembcorp Green Infra, a renewable energy independent power producer, have secured Sebi's approval to launch initial public offerings (IPO), an update with the markets regulator showed on Friday.
Razorpay filed draft documents with Sebi via the confidential route in June for an IPO.
Sembcorp Green Infra filed preliminary papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) in August to raise up to Rs 3,750 crore through an IPO.
After examining the draft documents, the regulator issued its final observations to Razorpay and Sembcorp Green Infra on November 3 and November 13, respectively, the update showed.
Sebi's observations mark an important step in the IPO process, allowing the companies to proceed with preparations for their public issues, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.
Razorpay did not disclose the size of the proposed issue. However, people familiar with the matter estimate the issue size in the range of Rs 5,000-6,000 crore.
Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay offers payment acceptance, banking, payouts, payroll, lending and other financial services through an integrated platform. The company serves millions of businesses across India, ranging from startups and small and medium enterprises to large corporates.
Razorpay attained unicorn status in 2020 and has since expanded beyond payments into a broader financial services ecosystem for businesses. Its offerings enable merchants to manage collections, payouts, payroll, cash flows and access to capital through a single platform.
The company is backed by investors like Peak XV Partners, GIC, Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Lone Pine Capital, Alkeon Capital and TCV.
The confidential filing route allows companies to submit draft offer documents to Sebi for review without immediately disclosing sensitive business information to the public.
According to the draft red herring prospectus, Sembcorp Green Infra's proposed IPO is entirely a fresh issue of equity shares with no offer-for-sale (OFS) component.
The IPO proceeds will be used for payment of certain borrowings by the company and the subsidiaries.
The proposed capital raise will help strengthen its balance sheet as it scales up its renewable energy portfolio.
Sembcorp Green Infra had 3.60 GW of operational renewable energy capacity and about 4.04 GW/GWh under construction as of March 31, 2026. Its under-construction portfolio includes 2.61 GW of renewable energy capacity and 1,433 MWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity.
The company is also increasing its focus on complex renewable projects, including hybrid, storage-backed, round-the-clock (RTC) and firm and dispatchable renewable energy (FDRE) projects.
Promoted by Sembcorp Utilities Pte Ltd and Sembcorp Industries Ltd, SGIL has 105 projects across 13 states and union territories.
Earlier this month, Nasdaq-listed travel booking platform MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary received Sebi's approval to launch its maiden public offering.

articles.title: Exclusive: This young startup wants to power floating data centers with the ocean’s heat, and investors are already on board | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Anyone who has weathered a hurricane can tell you that the oceans — which fuel the storms — contain a tremendous amount of energy. Thanks to global warming, they’re holding more than ever.
A new startup wants to harness that energy to power data centers.
Drogue, which has kept a low profile until now, is building a system that harvests heat from the ocean to power data centers on board floating vessels. According to co-founder and CEO Sam Sipe, the first prototype should be bobbing around the ocean, crunching bits, less than two years from now.
The goal, Sipe said, is to help data center developers deploy servers in AI-friendly timelines. “The data center industry is a real estate game, and so they’re playing on 8- to 10-year timelines, including interoperability with utilities and [independent system operators]” that manage regional power grids, he said. “AI demand has increased 10x in just the last three years. It’s completely incompatible.”
Drogue was founded just six months ago in Washington, D.C., and the startup told TechCrunch exclusively that it has already raised $20 million, including from XYZ Venture Capital, Toyota Ventures, Tamarack Global, Dream, FDVC, Garuda Ventures, Flexcap, Boost VC, and Slow Ventures, among other investors.
In those six months, Drogue has designed a multi-megawatt prototype that will be installed on a traditional oceangoing ship and sent out to sea in early 2028. Future versions will be built on floating structures that more closely resemble offshore oil platforms.
To Sipe, the decision to turn to the ocean was obvious.
After years flying E-2D Hawkeyes off U.S. Navy aircraft carriers, he had an appreciation for the ocean’s immense power. “Most people think, oh, ocean — hard waves, storms, corrosion, biofouling. And I just see this majestic place and resource that we just ignore,” he said.
As the planet warms, the oceans have been absorbing an additional 5.8 million terawatt-hours of energy every year. By comparison, all of human civilization uses about 180,000 terawatt-hours each year. If Drogue were to take some, surely the ocean wouldn’t miss it.
The startup’s technology works like a heat pump run in reverse. A heat pump uses electricity to move heat from one place to another; Drogue’s system instead uses a difference in temperature to generate electricity. This approach, known as ocean thermal energy conversion, or OTEC, was first developed in the 1950s.
Surface waters are warmer, heated by the sun, while down-deep temperatures are much colder, about 39°F on average (4°C). “There’s basically no amount of heat we can pull out of that that will collapse that temperature differential,” Sipe said.
To leverage the temperature differential, the startup’s system draws in warm surface water, uses it to cool the data centers, and then sends the now-warmer water to boil ammonia, a chemical that turns to gas at -28°F. That ammonia gas is then sent through a turbine to generate electricity. Once through the turbine, it courses through a condenser, which turns the gas back into a liquid. There, cold water drawn from 1,000 meters deep passes over the condenser’s fins to absorb the heat. The warmed water is then pumped back down to 1,000 meters, where it dissipates into the ocean. The ammonia gets sent back to the start of the sealed loop, and the cycle repeats.
The basic idea was tested in the 1980s but tossed aside. “A lot has changed since the ’80s, specifically manufacturing techniques around the pipe and the heat exchangers,” Sipe said.
To find out why, Sipe sought out people who had worked on those early efforts. “I just talked to everyone, basically interviewed them and figured out what went wrong, what went right, what would you do next. And everyone was like, dude, this stuff works. It’s just a matter of being able to raise enough capital to build something big enough, because there’s a sweet spot,” he said.
There also had to be customers who could use that power while still at sea. Sending power to shore would require lengthy, expensive cables, and manufacturing on board would require similarly expensive shipping of materials and finished goods. Data centers are ideal — the servers are compact relative to other equipment, and shipping data off the platform is incredibly cheap. Each vessel would live at sea for about a decade, Sipe said.
Drogue already has “approval in principle,” a preliminary sign-off, from the American Bureau of Shipping, which sets and checks safety standards for ships. Now it’s in the process of buying its first ship to start building a prototype ready for the open ocean.
In many ways, Drogue’s concept is similar to Elon Musk’s plan for orbital data centers: find a cheap source of power, and get the data centers as close to it as possible. Except unlike orbital data centers, Drogue’s don’t need to launch expensive rockets to get there. They can just sail a ship on the ocean, something humanity has been doing for millennia.

What is NYT Connections?
NYT Connections is one of several increasingly popular word games made by the New York Times. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult.
On the plus side, you don't technically need to solve the final one, as you'll be able to answer that one by a process of elimination. What's more, you can make up to four mistakes, which gives you a little bit of breathing room.
It's a little more involved than something like Wordle, however, and there are plenty of opportunities for the game to trip you up with tricks. For instance, watch out for homophones and other word games that could disguise the answers.

articles.title: One outage, millions affected. What went wrong at Microsoft?
articles.text:
One outage, millions affected. What went wrong at Microsoft?
Problems with Exchange Online spread across Microsoft 365 and external businesses, highlighting how dependent workplaces have become on shared cloud infrastructure.
Outlook marks the official start of the working day for millions globally. It also serves as a hub for daily workplace communication and scheduling across the world.
So, when Microsoft’s email service began failing on Thursday, November 12, the disruption quickly spread beyond missed messages to calendars, workplace tools, and businesses that depend on its cloud systems.
The massive outage continued into Friday, November 13, showing how a fault in one widely used service can cause ripples across the entire work ecosystem.
What happened and when
Microsoft’s incident records list Exchange Online incident EX1550543 as starting at 4.17 pm UTC on Thursday, or 9.47 pm in India. Users were unable to connect to their Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods.
Microsoft Exchange Online is the back-end server that stores and manages user data, while Microsoft Outlook is the front-end app used to view and interact with the data.
The wider Microsoft 365 incident, MO1550821, which disrupted multiple Microsoft 365 enterprise and consumer services worldwide, began at 6.26 pm UTC, or 11.56 pm IST.
First reports came from the Americas, but Microsoft later warned that users in any region could be affected.
Downdetector, a real-time platform that tracks online service disruptions and outages, recorded more than 1,30,000 reports of Outlook problems in the United States at its peak on Thursday afternoon. In India, complaints began shortly before midnight and reached 2,157 at 11.42 pm. Reports rose again to 1,960 at 8.42 am on Friday as people started work.
In its latest post on X, Microsoft said traffic-optimisation measures were producing positive results for service stability and capacity. It was applying these measures more widely across affected regions as it worked towards sustained recovery. While this indicates progress, it is not an all-clear from the company.
Microsoft directed users to incident MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin centre or its public status page. MO1550821 is one of the official incident tracking IDs assigned by Microsoft for the ongoing service degradation and outage.
Why this happened
Microsoft’s explanation emerged in stages. It first said a number of servers had unexpectedly become unavailable, putting extra load on the remaining infrastructure. The higher load, it stressed, was not caused by a sudden rise in customer traffic.
Later, Microsoft said a process on affected servers responsible for establishing secure connections had become overwhelmed, causing servers to stop handling requests. It also began rolling back a recent network configuration change that it said correlated with the start of the incident. Earlier updates had said no recent change had been linked to the problem.
Recovery was complicated with servers becoming unresponsive again when traffic returned. Microsoft tried restarting and rebuilding affected servers, restricting certain types of traffic, moving connections to alternative routes, and improving capacity. The challenge was not to simply bring servers back online, but also to keep them stable as traffic returned.
Microsoft said it had no indication that malicious activity had caused the outage. The precise root cause remained unconfirmed, and the company said it would publish a post-incident report.
Why so many services were affected
Exchange Online is Microsoft’s cloud-hosted email and calendar service. Other Microsoft 365 features use it for mail, contacts, calendar entries, and meeting information. When Exchange Online became unreliable, features that depended on it were disrupted even where the wider app was still running.
Users struggled to access mailboxes through Outlook on the web, desktop, and other connection methods, while email delivery was delayed. Copilot for Microsoft 365 failed to load or respond, or struggled to retrieve work data. In Teams, calendars and meeting scheduling were affected, but core calls, meetings, group chats and channel messages remained available. SharePoint files stored directly in the service remained accessible, although some connected features were affected.
Microsoft also listed problems with specific functions in Planner, To Do, Defender, Purview, Power BI, Intune, and Microsoft Graph, a set of programming interfaces that lets software exchange data with Microsoft services.
The impact beyond Microsoft, including India
Reuters reported that OpenAI and Anthropic had problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors, which link the AI services to users’ work information.
In India, IndiGo and Akasa Air said their email-support services were affected. There was no indication that flights were disrupted.
The effects reached public institutions too. Reuters reported that Australian government bodies, including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation and the Australian Federal Police; Japan’s government IT infrastructure; and users in the US House of Representatives were affected. Taiwanese financial firms also reported disruption to fund-management work.
Social media saw a meme fest. On X, users combined frustration with humour, as they joked about closing laptops, skipping meetings, and taking Friday off. Others linked another Microsoft outage to the long wait for Grand Theft Auto VI.
Different incidents, similar risks
This is not Microsoft’s first major 365 disruption this year. Another outage began on August 31 and was resolved on September 3. Microsoft attributed it to a problem with a core authentication configuration used by several services, affecting Exchange Online and parts of Copilot, OneDrive and SharePoint. However, that was a different, identified problem.
A cloud-related outage similar to the current disruption happened in October at Google, when an electrical failure at a data-centre facility disrupted services in Google Cloud’s europe-west2 region, a cloud computing data centre location in London.
Google’s incident report said the main impact lasted about six hours and eight minutes. The cause was different, but the incident showed how a local infrastructure failure can affect customers across a cloud region.
The CrowdStrike incident in July 2024 was different again. A faulty software update from the cybersecurity firm caused Windows machines worldwide to crash. Microsoft estimated that 8.5 million devices were affected. The mechanism was different, but the disruption underlined the risks when a small number of providers underpin critical systems.
What happens next
The test now is whether the traffic-optimisation changes keep servers stable as Microsoft increases traffic and capacity across regions. The company has promised a post-incident report covering the root cause and measures to prevent a repeat.
Customers need to know not only what failed but also why safeguards did not contain the disruption sooner.
The ongoing incident shows how dependent workplaces have become on shared cloud infrastructure.
For organisations, the lesson is to plan for a key provider failing. They must keep emergency contact channels outside the main email system, make critical information available by other means, and maintain alternative ways to reach staff and customers. Cloud services make apps work together, but these connections can also create shared points of failure. Products may look separate but they rely on the same underlying systems.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

O Galaxy S25 é um celular premium mais potente que o posterior S25 FE, equipado com chip Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite de 3 nm e 12 GB de RAM, contra o Exynos 2400 de 4 nm e 8 GB. Os 256 GB de espaço interno são adequados para guardar fotos e vídeos.
Seu kit principal de câmeras filma em 8K. Ele inclui wide de 50 MP com OIS, ultrawide de 12 MP e telefoto de 10 MP com zoom óptico 3x, além de frontal de 12 MP. O S25 FE possui uma telefoto de 8 MP, e as demais são iguais.
A tela LTPO AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,2″ possui taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de até 2.600 nits, enquanto a do S25 FE possui 1.900 nits; ambas oferecem cores excelentes, alta fluidez e visibilidade garantida.
O corpo em alumínio Armor 2 do S25 é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Gorilla Glass Victus 2, resistente contra pancadas e quedas. A certificação IP68 confere proteção em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.000 mAh resiste a até 29 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a Samsung. O suporte ao carregamento de 25 W via USB-C e de 15 W sem fio garante o uso para o dia inteiro.
O Galaxy S25 de 256 GB (R$ 3.429 em até 12x sem juros com cupom AEMEGA8) será atualizado até o Android 23 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.

articles.title: « Ramenez LE patron » : des employés Nvidia réclament déjà le retour de Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Jensen Huang, le désormais ex-dirigeant de Nvidia, a officiellement remis sa démission. Cette démission est l’aboutissement d’une affaire qui est devenue particulièrement sensible. Pour rappel, l’homme est suspecté d’avoir entretenu une relation extraconjugale avec une employée de l’entreprise, mais aussi une cliente suspectée par Washington d’être une espionne au service de la Chine.
En parallèle, Trump a défendu Jensen Huang, le FBI a ouvert une enquête et Pékin a nié toute implication dans cette affaire. Nous avons par ailleurs appris que Jensen Huang aurait eu une relation avec une autre salariée de l’entreprise, ce qui porterait à trois le nombre de relations entretenues dans le cadre professionnel. Quoi qu’il en soit, Jensen Huang n’est plus à la tête de Nvidia et certains employés réclament déjà son retour.
Certains employés de Nvidia réclament le retour de Jensen Huang
D’après le média américain Wired, une vingtaine d’employés ont publié sur LinkedIn des messages de soutien à Jensen Huang. L’un d’entre eux affirme que leur confiance en son leadership est inébranlable. Toujours selon Wired, un employé, qui travaille au sein de Nvidia depuis plusieurs années, affirme que le désir de voir Huang réintégré est largement partagé parmi les salariés. Il craint par ailleurs que l’absence de son dirigeant historique ne porte atteinte à l’entreprise : « Nvidia est Nvidia grâce à Jensen ».
Un message dans une boîte à idées pour empêcher son éviction
Quelques jours avant la démission de Jensen Huang, un ingénieur de longue date chez Nvidia a publié dans une boîte à idées interne un message exhortant le conseil d’administration à prendre en compte l’avis des employés avant toute décision. Ce message a suscité plus de 1 600 commentaires, en majorité favorables, et dont certains réclament maintenant le retour de Huang. Un salarié anonyme déclare ainsi : « Si vous croyez en cette mission, ramenez LE patron ». Un autre explique : « Nous sommes tous humains et pouvons faire des erreurs. Jensen a fait tellement de bonnes choses et il mérite une seconde chance ». Dans un courrier interne un autre employé estime que : « Si l’Amérique trahit celui qui a contribué à bâtir son avenir, alors ce monde ne mérite pas Jensen Huang ».
Ces différents messages seraient sans doute salués par Tim Sweeney, fondateur et PDG d’Epic Games. Ce dernier a déclaré que le licenciement de Jensen Huang serait « un niveau de stupidité comparable à celui d’Apple lorsqu’il a licencié Steve Jobs », et que « cela porterait gravement atteinte aux intérêts des États-Unis ». De son côté, Donald Trump appelle maintenant à ce que Tim Cook reprenne les rênes de Nvidia : « Une légende remplace une légende ! ».
Il reste maintenant à voir si les différents appels de ces salariés de l’entreprise pourraient être entendus d’une quelconque façon. Autant dire que rien n’est moins sûr. La question consiste maintenant plutôt à savoir qui remplacera Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia, et quel sera dorénavant le climat au sein de l’entreprise.

articles.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday.
That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago, led by IVP.
LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence.
With its open source roots, the startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem, unlike the major clouds or frontier AI labs. It also promises that LangSmith will contain agent behavior and is easy to use.
True, there are plenty of other startups pitching similar advantages these days and also doing well (case in point is newcomer Mintive). However, LangChain has had a head start and now claims 7,000 LangSmith customers, including big-name startups like Harvey, Rippling, and Clay, and enterprises like Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce.

articles.title: Unannounced Intel Core Ultra 7 260K CPU surfaces in Newegg prebuilt gaming PCs — Intel doesn’t have official specs list available for exclusive Arrow Lake chip
articles.text:
Unannounced Intel Core Ultra 7 260K CPU surfaces in Newegg prebuilt gaming PCs — Intel doesn’t have official specs list available for exclusive Arrow Lake chip [Updated]
Some of the specs of the chip are still fuzzy.
Update 11/13/26 at 12:10pm ET: Intel has confirmed the 260K Plus as a "limited-availability" SKU and says it's not currently available as a boxed retail chip. Specs should go live on Intel's website within the next few days.
A new Intel Arrow Lake SKU is listed for sale in multiple prebuilt PCs on Newegg, despite no official acknowledgement of the model from Intel. The Core Ultra 7 260K is a downclocked version of the Core Ultra 7 265K from Intel's main Arrow Lake stack, not the Arrow Lake Refresh stack that's infiltrated our list of the best CPUs for gaming. Outside of a few areas on Newegg's website, you'll find no mention of the CPU elsewhere online (including Intel's official Core Ultra Series 2 specs page).
Although retailer-exclusive and late-generation variants are common from AMD and Intel — we recently reviewed the Ryzen 5 5500F, for instance — they almost never fly completely under the radar, as is the case with the Core Ultra 7 260K. The chip itself is identical to the Core Ultra 7 265K based on the specs we know, fitted with 20 cores, eight of which are P-cores. The 260K tops out at 5.4 GHz, however, while the 265K reaches 5.5 GHz.
Otherwise, the specs are all the same. It comes with the same 125W TDP, same 30 MB of L3 cache, and same support for up to 256 GB of memory running at DDR5-6400. We only know of these specs from an image shown on the two ABS prebuilt listings available with the 260K. It's available in the ABS Kaze II paired with an RTX 5060, as well as the Flux II Aqua with an RTX 5070.
The image is below, captured hastily, as you can see, from a Microsoft Teams call. Again, we weren't able to find any information from Intel about the chip outside of this slide.
One critical detail this slide confirms is that the Core Ultra 7 260K belongs to the Arrow Lake family, not the range of Arrow Lake Refresh processors like the Core Ultra 7 270K Plus. It tops out at DDR5-6400, while Arrow Lake Refresh climbs up to DDR5-7200. That means the chip doesn't have access to the hardware-level enhancements available in Arrow Lake Refresh, nor the software-based Intel Binary Optimization Tool that boosts performance in select games.
Although that's enough to categorize the 260K, there are some details that are unclear. In the two PCs it's available in, the chip is referred to as the 260K across the full product page except in Newegg's option selector (pictured below), where it's referred to as the U7-260KF. Intel's KF models are unlocked for overclocking but lack integrated graphics.
Additionally, the slide from Intel referenced above shows the chip boosting up to 5.4 GHz, but the product page lists the chip at 5.2 GHz for maximum boost clock.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Newegg has told us that the chip is exclusive to the retailer and will only be sold through its in-house ABS prebuilts. ABS machines are normally sold with components Newegg already sells piecemeal, offering a convenient way to get a full rig with parts you can identify. The ABS Flux II Aqua, which is available with the chip, is on sale at Newegg now for $300 off.
The ABS Flux II Aqua gaming PC comes with an Intel CPU, an Nvidia GeForce GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card, a 1TB NVMe SSD with Gen 4 speeds, and 32GB of DDR5-6000 RAM. This is a 1440p gaming powerhouse with the potential for 4K.
We've reached out to Intel to get more details about the Core Ultra 7 260K, and we'll update this story when we hear back (see update log above). Although the specs suggest the 260K should perform almost identically to the 265K, we haven't had a chance to test the CPU ourselves. And, as you can see from the rankings in our CPU benchmark hierarchy, we recommend most Intel shoppers move toward an Arrow Lake Refresh SKU.

Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

articles.title: Apple HomeView : on a lu les premiers tests américains, faut-il regretter son absence en France ? — Frandroid
articles.text:
Joanna Stern vient de passer une semaine entière à se disputer avec un écran de 7 pouces posé sur son comptoir. Dans son test vidéo pour le Wall Street Journal, la journaliste américaine tente en vain de demander au nouvel Apple HomeView d’ouvrir sa porte de garage.
Non seulement Siri refuse d’obtempérer, mais l’assistant finit par lui soutenir avec aplomb que l’appareil ne possède aucune caméra, à quelques centimètres à peine de son objectif frontal de 12 Mpx. Prise de court, Apple a précisé que les serrures et portes de garage ne se déverrouillent pour l’instant qu’au doigt sur l’écran par mesure de sécurité, avant une mise à jour promise le mois prochain pour débloquer la commande vocale. La conclusion de l’essayiste est délicieusement pince-sans-rire : elle a déjà deux enfants à la maison qui ne l’écoutent pas, et doute fort d’en vouloir un troisième.
Au-delà des caprices de Siri, ce HomeView revêt une importance particulière pour Cupertino : il s’agit du premier grand lancement matériel hors iPhone de l’ère John Ternus, qui a succédé à Tim Cook à la direction générale d’Apple le 1er septembre dernier. Affiché à 299 dollars hors taxes aux États-Unis (en version sur socle comme en déclinaison murale), l’appareil vise à rattraper des années de retard face aux Echo Show d’Amazon et aux Nest Hub de Google.
Sous le capot, sa puce radio Thread et son contrôleur Matter, les deux standards universels de la domotique moderne, le transforment en chef d’orchestre capable de piloter sans latence ampoules, serrures ou thermostats de marques tierces sans boîtier additionnel. L’écran promet aussi d’identifier jusqu’à six membres de la famille par le visage ou par la voix afin d’afficher à chacun ses messages et son agenda personnels en puisant directement dans son iPhone. Mais comme nous l’expliquions lors de sa présentation en octobre, Apple a choisi de priver le Vieux Continent de son nouveau jouet, faute d’avoir déployé son nouveau Siri AI sur les iPhone européens.
    Pour aller plus loin
Apple présente HomeView, son premier écran connecté intelligent qui boude l’Europe
            
Redoutable en domotique, mais indiscret en famille
Chez The Verge, la spécialiste de la maison connectée Jennifer Pattison Tuohy lui attribue la note de 7 sur 10 à l’issue d’un test très complet. Sur le pilotage pur du foyer, le contrat est brillamment rempli : les éclairages répondent aussi instantanément qu’avec un interrupteur mural classique, et le mode cuisine découpe n’importe quelle recette glanée sur le web en étapes claires assorties de minuteurs multiples.
En revanche, la cohabitation familiale tourne vite au casse-tête de confidentialité. Installée devant l’écran, la journaliste a pu lire et faire défiler librement les SMS privés de sa fille de 15 ans tout simplement parce que l’objectif grand-angle captait encore la silhouette de l’adolescente assise au fond du canapé.
Du 10 au 30 novembre, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1000 passe à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 499 €, support de lavage offert ! Vision IA tri-caméra, sans fil périmétrique, tonte des bordures, adaptation à toutes les conditions de luminosité… Bref, il a tout pour tondre à votre place !
Côté intelligence artificielle, Siri AI s’est même permis d’inventer de toutes pièces un temps de trajet de 1 h 47 pour rejoindre un rendez-vous situé en réalité à cinq heures de route, lui inspirant ce tacle : « je la virerais pour lenteur ».
De son côté, la rédaction d’AppleInsider résume toute l’ambiguïté du produit dès son titre, « imparfait, j’en veux trois de plus », tout en regrettant l’absence d’App Store dédié, des widgets qui se contentent trop souvent de renvoyer la balle vers l’iPhone et des boutons domotiques bridés à un simple marche/arrêt.
Plus gênant sur le plan technique, l’équipe de la chaîne Short Circuit souligne que la reconnaissance faciale du HomeView n’a strictement rien à voir avec le Face ID sécurisé des iPhone.
Dépourvue de projecteur infrarouge capable de cartographier le volume 3D d’un visage, la caméra se fie à une simple analyse d’image 2D et pourrait, en théorie, être bernée par une banale photographie.
Reste que face à l’Echo Show d’Amazon, l’écran d’Apple conserve deux avantages décisifs : une interface garantie sans la moindre bannière publicitaire et un assistant Siri AI inclus gratuitement, là où Amazon facture son nouvel Alexa+ 20 dollars par mois hors abonnement Prime.
Une cage dorée pensée pour les foyers 100 % Apple
Dans son test, le youtubeur spécialisé en domotique Shane Whatley explique que son épouse a immédiatement adopté l’écran en cuisine pour suivre ses recettes et lancer des podcasts vidéo. À l’inverse, sa fille adolescente l’a prévenu dès le déballage qu’elle n’y toucherait probablement jamais, préférant tout gérer depuis l’écran de son téléphone.
Surtout, le HomeView impose une allégeance totale à la pomme, et trouve bien mieux sa place dans une grande maison truffée d’accessoires Apple Maison que dans un petit studio d’étudiant, note Short Circuit. Si un conjoint ou un colocataire utilise un smartphone Android, il sera relégué à un simple « mode invité », privé d’agenda, de rappels et de messagerie. Les amateurs de vidéo devront aussi faire une croix sur des applications natives pour Netflix ou YouTube, tandis que la facture grimpe vite : la version murale est livrée nue, obligeant à débourser au moins 60 dollars supplémentaires pour le support et l’alimentation.
Faut-il craquer et l’importer en France ?
Pour les technophiles pressés, glisser un HomeView dans sa valise depuis Londres ou New York est techniquement possible, mais l’appareil perdrait aussitôt en France l’essentiel de son intérêt.
Outre le fait que Siri AI ne maîtrise que l’anglais sur cet écran, toutes ses fonctions personnalisées (lecture des messages, calendrier, rappels) dépendent directement d’un iPhone situé à proximité.
Or, cette brique Siri AI demeure verrouillée sur tous les iPhone rattachés à un identifiant Apple européen, un blocage qu’Apple impute au DMA, le règlement européen sur les marchés numériques. À moins de basculer son compte principal hors de l’Union européenne, une gymnastique pénible qui perturbe les abonnements et les achats, seule la partie interrupteur domotique (Matter, Apple Maison et les caméras HomeKit Secure Video) fonctionnera normalement dans l’Hexagone.
- Côté prise secteur : l’adaptateur fourni avec la version sur pied est au format américain ou britannique, mais n’importe quel chargeur USB-C de 30 W européen suffit à l’alimenter.
- Côté fixation murale : le support encastré raccordé directement aux fils électriques est conçu pour les boîtiers d’encastrement nord-américains ; seul le support mural alimenté en USB-C est exploitable chez nous.
- Côté portefeuille et SAV : il faudra ajouter 20 % de TVA et des frais de douane à l’importation, sans aucune garantie de prise en charge dans un Apple Store français en cas de panne.
En attendant une éventuelle sortie officielle, si vous voulez simplement piloter vos objets connectés, vous avez tout intérêt à vous rabattre sur le HomePod mini 2 (169 €) ou l’Apple TV 4K (349 €), deux produits vendus chez nous qui remplissent exactement le même rôle de concentrateur Matter et Thread, l’écran tactile en moins.
Tant que le bras de fer entre Apple et Bruxelles restera dans l’impasse, l’écran connecté d’Apple n’a aucune raison de traverser l’Atlantique.
Au vu des premiers essais, il n’y a pourtant pas de quoi nourrir trop de regrets : si le matériel fait l’unanimité comme tableau de bord domotique, son cerveau logiciel essuie encore les plâtres aux États-Unis. Importé aujourd’hui dans un salon français, le HomeView se résumerait à un très bel interrupteur mural à 300 dollars condamné à vous parler en anglais. Franchement, ça ne vaut pas le coup, sauf, peut-être, pour les macophiles.
    Pour aller plus loin
Siri AI bloqué en Europe : « c’est le choix d’Apple, et d’Apple seul », tranche Bruxelles

articles.title: Google puso en su buscador un nuevo modelo de IA que responde con más imágenes y tablas comparativas
articles.text:
Google activó Gemini 4 Hydrogen, un nuevo modelo de inteligencia artificial, para todos los usuarios de su buscador en el mundo. La empresa lo describió como la mayor mejora de modelo en Search hasta ahora. Responde preguntas de varias partes y muestra más imágenes, tablas comparativas y herramientas a medida.
Según el anuncio de Google, el modelo entiende mejor la intención de quien busca, incluso con errores de tipeo o pedidos muy específicos. También promete respuestas más fáciles de recorrer a simple vista y mayor calidad en todos los idiomas que admite el modo de búsqueda con IA.
Robby Stein, vicepresidente de producto de Search, afirmó en X que Hydrogen es ahora el modelo predeterminado de AI Mode, la búsqueda conversacional de Google. También se usa para las preguntas más difíciles en AI Overviews, los resúmenes con IA que aparecen sobre los resultados, según recogió Search Engine Roundtable.
Google no publicó cifras de velocidad ni pruebas comparativas. PPC Land, un medio especializado en publicidad digital, señaló que la entrada no menciona anuncios, clics hacia sitios web ni el efecto sobre los modelos de pago que ya funcionan en el buscador.
Tres modelos de Gemini 4 en 30 días
Según PPC Land, el primero de la serie, Gemini 4 Argon, salió el 13 de octubre solo para suscriptores de los planes de pago AI Pro y Ultra. El 28 de octubre, el director ejecutivo de Google, Sundar Pichai, presentó Gemini 4 Carbon como su modelo más potente.
El 10 de noviembre, Carbon llegó a AI Mode únicamente para los suscriptores de Ultra, un plan que PPC Land ubica desde USD 99,99 al mes. Hydrogen es el tercero y el primero que Google ofrece sin pago en el buscador.
Hydrogen reemplaza a Gemini 3.8 Flash, el modelo que usaba AI Mode desde el 2 de septiembre, según PPC Land. Ars Technica informó que el cambio alcanza a los productos de la empresa en general, aunque Google no detalló cada uno.
Qué reciben la app, los desarrolladores y los sitios web
En la aplicación Gemini, Google indicó que los usuarios gratuitos accederán a Hydrogen mediante la selección automática de modelo, cuando el sistema lo considere adecuado para la consulta. Ars Technica señaló, en cambio, que el selector de modelos ya lo ofrece a los suscriptores de AI Pro y Ultra, y que los usuarios gratuitos y los de AI Plus siguen con un modelo anterior.
Para los programadores, Ars Technica informó que Hydrogen cuesta USD 1,50 por millón de unidades de texto enviadas y USD 7,50 por millón generadas, igual que su predecesor. Carbon y Argon cuestan hoy USD 2 y USD 10, y subirán a USD 4 y USD 20 a partir del mes próximo.
Para los sitios web, Google sostiene que su técnica de lanzar varias búsquedas simultáneas sobre los subtemas de una pregunta ahora conecta con más enlaces. Ars Technica recordó que la empresa ya había hecho promesas similares antes. PPC Land añadió que la entrada no aclara si el despliegue ya se completó en todos los países.
Gemini 4 Carbon: máxima inteligencia y eficiencia de costos para flujos de trabajo reales
Gemini 4 Carbon ya se encuentra disponible para desarrolladores, empresas, científicos y el público general, consolidándose como nuestro modelo de mayor potencia. Esta herramienta ofrece un desempeño de vanguardia en ciberseguridad y en la ejecución de flujos de trabajo inteligentes a largo plazo, lo que resulta fundamental para abordar tareas complejas de ingeniería de software, gestión del conocimiento y razonamiento científico.
Tras su lanzamiento inicial —dirigido exclusivamente a especialistas en ciberseguridad mediante el programa Fairwind— y después de la reciente presentación de Gemini 4 Argon, este nuevo modelo lleva nuestras capacidades a un nivel superior.
Si bien Argon continúa siendo la alternativa óptima para la mayoría de las labores cotidianas de desarrollo y administración de información, Carbon ha sido concebido para enfrentar desafíos que exigen el máximo nivel de inteligencia artificial.
Por ello, está especialmente orientado a procesos de codificación y depuración complejos de múltiples pasos, así como a la investigación científica abierta, empleando una mayor cantidad de tokens para analizar en profundidad, razonar con rigor y realizar ciclos de verificación prolongados.
Finalmente, los resultados en diversas evaluaciones independientes enfocadas en entornos de trabajo reales demuestran que Carbon logra un equilibrio excepcional entre máxima precisión y eficiencia de costos en producción. De hecho, lidera las clasificaciones en pruebas como CursorBench 4.0, WANDR de Perplexity y AutomationBench de Zapier, destacando por ofrecer un costo por tarea más de dos veces inferior al de su competidor externo más cercano.

articles.title: Snap contrata a Robert Downey Jr. para impulsar sus nuevas gafas de realidad aumentada SPECS
articles.text:
Robert Downey Jr. pasó más de una década interpretando a Tony Stark, un multimillonario que utilizaba todo tipo de tecnología futurista en las películas de Marvel. Ahora, el actor ha decidido acercarse un poco más a ese mundo al fichar por Snap (la empresa detrás de Snapchat) para promocionar sus nuevas gafas de realidad aumentada SPECS. Y lo más llamativo es que el dispositivo le convenció al instante, ya que aseguró que solo necesitó 40 segundos para quedarse sin palabras.
Según ha anunciado la propia Snap, Downey Jr. ocupará un cargo honorífico como director de experiencia del cliente. Así, ayudará a desarrollar nuevas funciones, contenidos y experiencias para las gafas, así que protagonizará anuncios y colaborará con los equipos responsables tanto del hardware como de las apps de realidad aumentada.
De interpretar a Iron Man a promocionar unas gafas de más de 2.000 dólares
¿Y qué tienen de especial estas SPECS? A diferencia de unas gafas convencionales, permiten colocar elementos digitales sobre el entorno real y controlarlos mediante movimientos de las manos o comandos de voz. De hecho, Snap ya ha publicado una serie de vídeos protagonizados por el actor en los que muestra cómo pueden utilizarse para trabajar, practicar golf, aprender habilidades artísticas o disfrutar de contenido audiovisual.
Downey Jr. asegura que lleva unos 20 años probando dispositivos tecnológicos que se pueden llevar puestos y que la mayoría no terminaron de convencerle. Con SPECS, sin embargo, dice haber cambiado de opinión en apenas 40 segundos, llegando incluso a bromear con que estas gafas cumplen la promesa de realidad aumentada de cierto superhéroe tecnológico al que interpretó.
Eso sí, no son precisamente baratas. Las SPECS cuestan 2.195 dólares y por ahora las reservas están limitadas a Estados Unidos, Reino Unido y Francia, con envíos previstos para otoño de 2026. Mientras tanto, Snap está utilizando la colaboración con Downey Jr. para enseñar qué pueden hacer sus gafas, con nuevos episodios que se irán incorporando a YouTube y a la web del producto.

articles.title: Notre sélection des 6 meilleurs TV Oled et Mini-Led du Black Friday, de 490 € à 2000 €
articles.text:
Notre sélection des 6 meilleurs TV Oled et Mini-Led du Black Friday, de 490 € à 2000 €
Un Mini-Led à moins de 500 €, un Oled polyvalent à prix plancher ou un téléviseur haut de gamme pour profiter pleinement de ses films et séries : voici notre sélection des meilleurs bons plans TV de ce Black Friday 2026, selon votre budget et vos envies.
Les promotions du Black Friday sont l’occasion de s’équiper d’un bon téléviseur à des prix très intéressants et les prix sont enfin en train de chuter après un début novembre assez mollasson il faut l’avouer. Encore faut-il choisir le modèle adapté à son salon, à ses usages, mais surtout à son budget ! Parmi les références passées dans notre laboratoire, nous avons retenu six TV Oled et Mini-Led, du modèle abordable pour le quotidien aux Oled les plus performants pour le cinéma.
LG C6 : un des meilleurs rapport qualité prix Oled
Le LG C6 reste l’un des choix les plus équilibrés de cette sélection. Il conserve les noirs parfaits et l’absence de blooming propres à l’Oled, avec une colorimétrie très juste et une luminosité qui progresse enfin sensiblement. Les joueurs sont également bien servis avec une dalle qui monte à 165 Hz sur PC, quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et une excellente réactivité.
Le C6 constitue donc une excellente option, d’autant que le 55 pouces tombe à 1200 €, son prix le plus bas jamais atteint depuis sa sortie. Le 65 pouces est quant à lui proposé à 1600 €.
LG 55C6
Samsung S92H : l’Oled à privilégier si les reflets vous gênent
Pour ceux qui regardent souvent la télévision en journée, le Samsung S92H a un argument de poids : son filtre antireflet. Avec une réflectance mesurée à environ 8 % dans notre laboratoire, il atténue beaucoup plus efficacement les reflets des fenêtres et des luminaires. Sa qualité d’image est par ailleurs très convaincante, avec une dalle Oled 165 Hz et quatre ports HDMI 2.1.
À 1300 € en 55 pouces, le supplément de 100 € face au C6 se justifie donc surtout par l’antireflet. En 65 pouces, les deux concurrents sont au même prix : 1600 €.
Samsung 55S92H
LG G6 : un Oled haut de gamme désormais bien plus accessible
Si vous pouvez augmenter votre budget, le LG G6 apporte un vrai supplément de luminosité face au C6. Sa dalle Tandem Oled atteint environ 2340 cd/m² sur une fenêtre de 10 %, et dépasse même les 3100 cd/m² sur les petites zones lumineuses. L’antireflet est également plus efficace que celui du C6, tandis que les quatre ports HDMI 2.1, la dalle 165 Hz et le faible retard à l’affichage en font un excellent compagnon pour jouer.
Le 55G6 est proposé à 1600 € et le 65G6 à 2000 €, là encore, leurs meilleurs prix depuis leur sortie.
LG 55G6
Philips OLED951 : une belle image Oled avec de l’Ambilight en bonus
À 2000 € en 65 pouces, le Philips OLED951 constitue une alternative particulièrement intéressante au LG G6 pour les amateurs d’Ambilight. L’éclairage sur quatre côtés prolonge les couleurs de l’image sur le mur et reste un vrai élément de différenciation pour ceux qui apprécient cette ambiance lumineuse.
Le Philips ne mise pas uniquement sur cet équipement. Sa dalle Tandem Oled délivre un pic lumineux proche de 2700 cd/m², une colorimétrie très fidèle et des noirs impeccables. Il prend également en charge le Dolby Vision et le HDR10+, tout en proposant quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et une fréquence maximale de 165 Hz. Notre réserve concerne surtout Titan OS, moins complet et moins abouti que Google TV ou webOS. Un boîtier multimédia externe pourra contourner cette limite si nécessaire.
Philips 65OLED951
TCL C89L : du Mini-Led très lumineux à partir de 800 €
Pour profiter d’une image lumineuse sans atteindre les tarifs de l’Oled, le TCL C89L mérite clairement le détour. Son rétroéclairage Mini-Led lui permet de dépasser les 3000 cd/m² avec un contraste solide. Google TV, le bon système audio et les quatre ports HDMI 2.1 associés à une dalle 144 Hz complètent une fiche technique très convaincante.
L’Oled conserve l’avantage sur les angles de vision et l’absence de halos autour des objets lumineux, mais le TCL fait valoir un tarif nettement plus accessible. Le 55C89L est affiché à 800 € et le 65C89L à 1200 €. Une bonne piste pour ceux qui veulent un plus grand écran. On le trouvera d’ailleurs à 1500 € en 75 pouces et 2000 € en 85 pouces.
TCL C69K : un Mini-Led à moins de 500 €
Enfin, les budgets plus serrés pourront se tourner vers le TCL C69K, proposé à 490 € en 55 pouces et 650 € en 65 pouces. Ce modèle de 2025 conserve plusieurs atouts appréciables : une bonne colorimétrie en SDR, Google TV, une dalle 144 Hz et un système audio Onkyo dont la spatialisation nous avait agréablement surpris.
Il faut bien sûr accepter davantage de compromis que sur le C89L. Le pic lumineux est plus limité, les reflets sont présents et les halos lumineux restent visibles dans les scènes sombres. Pour regarder la télévision, profiter des plateformes de streaming et jouer sans trop dépenser, il demeure néanmoins une option intéressante à ce tarif.
TCL 55C69K

articles.title: Nova Scotia Bets on Microelectronics Integration, Not Chip Fabs - EE Times
articles.text:
Nova Scotia is unlikely to become the next great destination for wafer fabs. But its semiconductor and microelectronics opportunity may be more relevant to the region’s economy: assembling the right mix of sensing, processing, communications, power, photonics, AI, and packaging technologies to solve hard problems in the ocean, in defense, in healthcare, and in energy.
It’s an important distinction, Jean-François Bousquet, program director of Dalhousie University’s MINDI Hub, said in an interview with EE Times. The province’s strength is not necessarily inventing the next standalone semiconductor device but building highly integrated systems that must work reliably in remote, power-constrained, and unforgiving environments, he said.
“Semiconductors will scare people away if we talk about semiconductors, but if we talk about integration of microelectronic systems, I think there’s a strong capability of integrating into various domains, especially in ocean tech,” Bousquet said.
Integration, not just chips
Semiconductor ecosystems are frequently measured in fabs, process nodes, venture funding rounds, or the presence of global chipmakers.
Nova Scotia’s ecosystem is developing by starting with an operational problem to define applications: ocean observation, underwater robotics, sonar, fisheries, environmental monitoring, naval systems, medical technology, and renewable energy. The technology stack, which includes microelectronics, follows.
For an autonomous underwater vehicle operating below Arctic ice for months, that stack can be formidable. The vehicle must sense, communicate, navigate, classify events, process data locally, and conserve every possible joule of energy. It may need AI acceleration, FPGA-based processing, GPUs in some applications, MEMS devices, photonics, lasers, specialized communications, and advanced sensing. It also needs to fit inside a very small, rugged, waterproof package.
“We have to find innovative ways of integrating our microelectronics and make our autonomous vehicles smart enough to be able to go under the ice in the Arctic,” Bousquet said. “They have to communicate, they have to sense, and they have to know what’s around them.”
Nova Scotia’s microelectronics story is increasingly an edge computing story—and the edge can be underwater, far offshore, or embedded in a compact defense or environmental platform.
Bousquet’s group is working on a project involving autonomous underwater drones, as well as coordination between underwater and aerial systems for remote-area monitoring. Those are inherently dual-use capabilities. The same class of integrated electronics can support defense and surveillance requirements while also enabling scientific research, environmental monitoring, resource exploration, and climate-related observation.
“We developed sensors that will measure the biological, chemical, and geological content of water in the ocean,” Bousquet said.
Nova Scotia’s semiconductor and microelectronics development is driven by Atlantic Canada’s industrial geography. The province’s capital, Halifax, is home to a great deal of defense research, naval presence, defense primes and suppliers, universities, ocean-technology companies, and the Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship. The region’s proximity to the Atlantic, Arctic routes, fisheries, offshore resources, and shipbuilding is less a branding exercise than a set of practical engineering requirements.
At the local level, the MINDI Hub (short for Microelectronics Innovation Design Hub) is meant to provide some connective tissue. Backed by the provincial government, the initiative is designed to support industry, develop curriculum around microelectronics for ocean technology, train students, and expand the workforce available to local companies.
MINDI is part of a wider Canadian tapestry. It is hosted at Dalhousie University, which collaborates with Quebec-based experts, including those at the University of Sherbrooke and Zero Point Cryogenics, while exploring international partnerships. Rather than duplicate every capability locally, the goal is to link Nova Scotia’s systems-level strengths to the specialized facilities, research talent, and suppliers available elsewhere in Canada and among allied countries.
“This is an incubator that’s intending to support industry, and we’re training students,” Bousquet said. “We’re building new curriculum around microelectronics for ocean technology. We want to create more momentum, and we want to create a bigger workforce that will actually support the local industry.”
Low-power innovation beneath the surface
Bedford-based Innovasea is a concrete example of how Bousquet’s regional thesis works in practice.
The company designs and manufactures aquatic technology, including acoustic telemetry systems used to track fish in oceans, lakes, and rivers. Its products are used by scientists and biologists studying animal movement and behavior, but the engineering behind them is broadly recognizable to anyone working in ultra-low-power embedded electronics.
Innovasea’s small acoustic tags attach to (or, in some cases, are implanted in) fish. Underwater receivers detect the transmitted acoustic signals, allowing researchers to identify tagged animals and, using multiple receivers, determine their locations with fine precision. The tag can also carry sensor data, such as temperature or pressure.
Jean Quirion, VP of R&D for fish tracking at Innovasea, told EE Times in an interview that the company’s competitive advantage lies in integrating components into compact, power-efficient systems that operate reliably in demanding environments.
He said increasingly efficient microcontrollers let designers perform more computation within an existing power budget or maintain performance while consuming less energy.
But these component improvements are not the only factors contributing to Innovasea’s engineering gains, Quirion said. “Most of the innovations that we’ve come up with that really reduce power consumption and reduce size have been in some tricks that we’ve developed internally to just make the system behave in a more power-efficient way.”
The expertise developed at Innovasea is due in part to connections between industry and universities. Quirion described Dalhousie as both a source of engineering talent, through co-op placements and full-time hiring, and a partner for research that carries more uncertainty than routine product development.
Collaboration with Dalhousie and other regional universities helps companies explore emerging technologies. Alongside organizations such as COVE, those relationships connect research, workforce development, and commercial engineering, supporting an Atlantic Canadian ecosystem whose opportunity lies in turning semiconductor capabilities into useful, exportable systems.
Building a connected ecosystem
Chris Morrissey, CEO of Invest Nova Scotia, sees microelectronics as an enabling layer within a wider economic strategy rather than a standalone vertical. The province has identified six priority sectors, including energy, defense, natural resources, AI, and the digital economy. Semiconductor and embedded systems capabilities intersect with all of them.
That is particularly evident in defense. Nova Scotia has naval and Coast Guard activity, shipbuilding, aerospace and drone-related capabilities, defense primes, and a growing supplier base. Morrissey said the province has between four and six major defense prime contractors and more than 100 defense companies, creating both procurement opportunities and demand for locally relevant R&D.
“The advantage that Nova Scotia has is the research and development expertise that we have here, both in the public and private sectors,” Morrissey said, citing MINDI as a good example of public funding.
Opportunities are not limited to military contracts, he said. Sonar and tracking technologies can apply to naval requirements and fisheries; drones can serve defense missions and support wildfire management; and sensing systems can contribute to environmental monitoring, energy operations, and safety.
Dual-use technology is a recurring theme in Nova Scotia, with companies able to extend a core competence into adjacent markets.
Within Atlantic Canada, Morrissey argued that provinces should identify complementary strengths rather than chase identical projects. Newfoundland and Labrador’s Marine Institute, for example, has capabilities in marine simulation and related areas. Nova Scotia can develop where it has distinct advantages in ocean technology, digital systems, defense, research, and talent. Morrissey said sustainable growth must align with available talent, capital, and infrastructure rather than build around a speculative attempt to replicate Silicon Valley.
“We can be complementary to each other,” he said. “We’re trying to find each of our own lanes and what’s the competitive advantage for each one but also working together and leaning on each other to make sure we can take advantage of the greater opportunity.”
That cooperative stance increasingly extends across the country. Bousquet’s quantum sensing work depends on Quebec partnerships; companies in Atlantic Canada can access expertise and markets nationally; and defense, ocean technology, photonics, and AI systems all depend on supply chains that exceed provincial borders. Internationally, Nova Scotia’s ocean-facing industries have natural links to Europe, NATO allies, and global marine research communities.
Bousquet said Nova Scotia does not need to reproduce another region’s semiconductor cluster to matter. It can build technologies that fit the problems in front of it and connect those systems to capabilities across Atlantic Canada, the country, and the world.
“We do have a lot of the capability; it’s just a matter of growing it,” he said.

articles.title: SpaceX va tenter de récupérer les deux étages de Starship : comment suivre le lancement historique aujourd'hui ?
articles.text:
Starship s’élance aujourd’hui pour son 15e vol. Et c'est un essai qui pourrait marquer un tournant dans l’histoire des fusées. SpaceX va en effet tenter une manœuvre jamais réalisée jusqu’ici.
Le 28 septembre dernier, l’entreprise d’Elon Musk a franchi un cap crucial lors du 14e vol de sa mégafusée : Starship a atteint l’orbite pour la première fois. C’est aujourd’hui une tout autre paire de manches qui se profile. Car SpaceX va essayer de récupérer le booster Super Heavy, une manœuvre déjà effectuée par le passé, mais aussi le second étage, le « Ship ».
Du jamais-vu
Ainsi, après un peu plus de 6 minutes après le décollage, Super Heavy doit revenir au-dessus du complexe Starbase pour être rattrapé par les gigantesques bras de la tour de lancement, surnommés « Mechazilla ». Ce sera le premier essai du genre avec un propulseur de nouvelle génération, la V3. Le Ship, lui, poursuivra seul sa route jusqu’à environ 275 kilomètres d’altitude pour y larguer 26 satellites Starlink V3.
Et il faudra s’armer de patience pour observer la tentative de sa capture, car avant de revenir sur Terre, il doit réaliser 14 tours de notre planète pendant 22 heures. Si, et seulement si, ses systèmes sont jugés en bon état, les équipes donneront leur feu vert pour la récupération grâce aux bras mécaniques.
Il faut en effet savoir que cet exercice s’annonce beaucoup plus périlleux que pour un premier étage, comme c’est le cas avec le Falcon 9. Car la fusée reviendra de l’orbite à une vitesse vertigineuse et va donc devoir supporter la chaleur extrême de la rentrée atmosphérique. Elle devra ensuite descendre à plat, se redresser et rallumer ses moteurs au dernier moment pour se glisser entre les bras mécaniques. Si les deux captures aboutissent, ce sera la première fois qu’une fusée orbitale est récupérée en totalité.
Cette étape est indispensable pour SpaceX qui ambitionne, à terme, de faire voler sa fusée plusieurs fois par jour. C’est aussi pour cette raison que Starship est la pièce maîtresse de quasiment tous ses projets d’envergure, de Starlink en passant par les data centers orbitaux puis, sur le long terme, Mars.
Suivre le lancement de Starship
Pour suivre le vol, il faudra vous rendre sur le compte X de SpaceX, qui diffusera l’événement en direct dès 23h15 heure de Paris. Et puisque le second étage ne redescendra que samedi, il faudra patienter jusqu’à 21h15 ce samedi pour l’allumage de désorbitation. La capture, elle, est prévue à 22h15.
Gardez en tête que le décollage peut glisser, car la fenêtre de tir sera ouverte jusqu’à 1h du matin. De même, une mauvaise météo ou une autorisation tardive de la FAA pourraient retarder l’échéance.

articles.title: Melhor TV Hisense: 10 modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Melhor TV Hisense: 10 modelos para comprar em 2026
Encontre a TV Hisense ideal para sua casa ou escritório; guia reúne smart TVs 4K, QLED e Mini LED em diversos tamanhos e faixas de preço
TVs Hisense são conhecidas por recursos avançados como upscaling de resolução e som imersivo com Dolby Atmos, além da boa relação custo-benefício.
Há modelos topo de linha como a UR9SG, com miniLED RGB e precisão de cores. Já TVs QLED equilibram boa qualidade de imagem com preços justos. E também existem televisores mais básicos com sistema operacional VIDAA, a exemplo da A6NV.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog lista 10 opções de TVs Hisense para diferentes perfis de uso. Veja os prós e contras de cada modelo.
A Hisense U7ESG é uma TV com painel QLED e retroiluminação miniLED que entrega cores mais vibrantes e controle preciso de iluminação em zonas individuais. Com isso, ela chega a uma cobertura de cores com bilhões de tons, tornando a experiência visual mais rica.
A taxa de atualização de 144 Hz deixa os jogos mais fluidos, e o suporte ao AMD FreeSync sincroniza a frequência da tela com a placa gráfica eliminando travamentos e cores de imagem.
Destaque também para o subwoofer embutido que dá ênfase aos graves e torna os áudios mais imersivos. E o upgrade de áudio por IA ajusta a equalização, seja em jogos ou em apps de streaming compatíveis com o sistema Google TV.
Tamanhos disponíveis: 65″ e 75″
A Hisense UR9SG é o modelo topo de linha da marca. Com tamanhos de 85″ ou 100″, o televisor 4K apresenta um painel Obsidian que reduz reflexos de iluminação. Já os miniLEDs RGB com até 100% de cobertura BT.2020 conseguem gerar cores mais fiéis do que miniLEDs convencionais devido à emissão de cores primárias.
Graças ao processador Hi-View AI Engine RGB, o televisor consegue ajustar cor e brilho em tempo real. E além de oferecer suporte às tecnologias HDR10 e HDR10+, o aparelho também consegue aprimorar conteúdos padrão a qualidades próximas ao HDR.
O televisor ainda traz som surround com Dolby Atmos e DTS Virtual X para criar uma experiência imersiva 360º. O sistema operacional é o Google TV, empoderado com o assistente Gemini para pesquisas ou conversas (chatbot).
A Hisense U7 Pro oferece alta performance para streaming ou jogos. Enquanto a resolução 4K UHD (3840 × 2160 pixels) exibe imagens mais detalhadas, a retroiluminação com miniLED oferece pretos mais profundos e maior controle de cor em comparação com telas LED.
O televisor é compatível com a tecnologia Dolby Vision para garantir imagens mais fiéis aos conteúdos originais. E também oferece taxa de atualização de 165 Hz para jogatinas mais fluidas, além de um painel gamer que exibe dados de desempenho em tempo real.
O aparelho chega rodando a interface Google TV e ainda apresenta sistema de som surround 2.1.2, que dá mais profundidade aos áudios sem a necessidade de equipamentos extras.
Tamanhos disponíveis: 75″, 85″ e 100″
A Hisense QLED U7Q é outra opção de TV miniLED com tamanhos a partir de 55″. Ela tem várias especificações similares às da TV U7ESG, como resolução 4K e painel QLED com retroiluminação miniLED para uma experiência de contraste e nitidez superior a TVs de LED convencional.
No entanto, a Hisense U7Q entrega menos brilho devido ao pico mais baixo de 833 nits. Ao menos, o ajuste de brilho inteligente com base na luz ambiente tenta equilibrar a qualidade da imagem e aumentar a economia de energia.
O televisor também roda a interface Google TV e possui sistema de som surround com subwoofer integrado para que você sinta graves com mais profundidade.
Tamanhos disponíveis: 55″, 65″ e 100″
A Hisense Q7Q é uma smart TV voltada para o público gamer. Seu painel QLED adiciona uma câmada de pontos quânticos que amplia a gama de cores — mais de um bilhão de tons ao todo. Por outro lado, a retroiluminação de LEDs convencionais oferece controle de iluminação menos preciso em comparação com TVs miniLED.
Como o foco é para jogatinas, o aparelho tem taxa de atualização de 144 Hz (com VRR) para uma experiência mais fluida. Também há suporte ao AMD FreeSync Premium e às tecnologias AI Smooth Motion e AI Sports Mode, que reduzem o desfoque em cenas dinâmicas.
Já o sistema de som com Dolby Atmos cria um ambiente de som tridimensional, deixando os jogos ainda mais imersivos. Enquanto isso, a interface Google TV oferece ampla compatibilidade com os principais apps de streaming.
Tamanhos disponíveis: 55″, 65″, 75″, 85″ e 100″
A Hisense U6Q é uma opção de entrada dentre os modelos “U”, mas com bom equilíbrio de brilhos e cores. Isso porque a TV adota a tecnologia QLED Color com mais de um bilhão de tons, aliada a miniLEDs que melhoram o brilho, sombras e nitidez das imagens.
O aparelho é compatível com Dolby Vision e usa IA para aprimorar conteúdos padrão com qualidade próxima ao HDR. O modo gamer oferece taxa de atualização variável (VRR) e modo de baixa latência (ALLM), mas a frequência da tela é de 60 Hz e pode limitar a fluidez durante as gameplays.
A TV traz o sistema operacional VIDAA U9, criado pela própria Hisense. Trata-se da versão mais recente do SO da marca, contudo, ele não oferece a mesma compatibilidade com apps como o Google TV.
Tamanhos disponíveis: 55″ e 65″
A Hisense Q6Q é uma TV QLED com preço mais acessível e que ainda assim entrega boa cobertura de cores. O aparelho com resolução 4K utiliza a tecnologia Hi-QLED Color da marca, com mais de um bilhão de cores para alcançar imagens mais vivas.
Apesar da taxa de atualização ser limitada a 60 Hz, a tecnologia AI Smooth Motion reduz borrões de movimento com o objetivo de oferecer mais fluidez a conteúdos esportivos ou jogos.
Já o sistema de som não é dos mais potentes (14 W no total), mas traz o selo Dolby Atmos para garantir áudios mais realistas. E o televisor roda o sistema operacional VIDAA, com a versão mais recente disponibilizada (U9).
Tamanhos disponíveis: 43″, 50″, 55″, 65″, 75″ e 85″
A smart TV Hisense Q6N tem a premissa de oferecer imagem com cores vivas a um preço justo. O televisor QLED com resolução 4K possui uma câmada de pontos quânticos que emitem cores mais precisas. Enquanto isso, a tecnologia Direct Full Array ajusta a luminosidade em diferentes áreas para alcançar pretos mais intensos.
O aparelho tem ampla compatibilidade com conteúdos HDR, incluindo suporte ao HDR10+ e Dolby Vision (não associado a HEVC). E para completar a experiência de streaming, o sistema de som com Dolby Atmos cria uma experiência de áudio tridimensional inspirada nos cinemas.
O televisor roda a interface Google TV, que é compatível com vários apps da Play Store e sugere conteúdos com base nas preferências de visualização.
Tamanhos disponíveis: 50″, 55″, 65″, 75″ e 85″
A Hisense QD68SG é uma ótima opção de TV QLED sem tantos recursos adicionais. O principal destaque está na tecnologia Hi-QLED Color baseada em pontos quânticos, que aumenta a gama de cores reproduzidas na tela. São mais de um bilhão de tons ao todo.
Além disso, o televisor traz um display antirreflexo para uma imagem mais nítida mesmo em ambientes iluminados. E o sensor de luz adaptativo ainda ajusta o brilho da tela de acordo com a luz do espaço.
A TV chega com a interface Google TV (baseada no Android TV) e traz sistema de som Dolby Atmos para uma experiência sonora mais imersiva.
A Hisense A6NV é ideal para quem quer uma TV 4K gastando o mínimo possível. A TV não possui uma camada de pontos quânticos vista em TVs QLED, mas usa a tecnologia Precision Color para reforçar as cores com mais precisão.
O recurso 4K AI Upscaler adapta conteúdos de resoluções mais baixas em imagens 4K, melhorando o streaming de filmes e séries mais antigas. E o sistema de som DTS:X (concorrente do Dolby Atmos) cria uma sensação tridimensional, como se os sons saíssem de diferentes direções.
Já a navegação acontece na interface do VIDAA U9, que é o sistema operacional da Hisense. O problema é que nem todos apps são compatíveis com o sistema.
Tamanhos disponíveis: 50″, 55″, 58″, 65″ e 75″
A escolha pela melhor TV Hisense deve considerar se as especificações e recursos atendem às suas preferências de uso. Vale ficar de olho nos seguintes aspectos:
A Hisense RGB-MiniLED UR9SG é a TV topo de linha da marca. Ela traz resolução 4K e miniLEDs RGB com boa cobertura de cores. Além disso, o aparelho oferece amplo suporte a conteúdos HDR e experiência sonora imersiva, com som surround Dolby Atmos e DTS Virtual X.
A Hisense RGB-MiniLED UR9SG também é a melhor TV para PS5 e jogos no geral. A tela 4K tem frequência de 180 Hz para gameplays mais fluidas e a TV ainda conta com frequência variável (VRR) e baixa latência. Fora isso, o sistema de som multicanais (com subwoofer integrado) e a alta gama de cores tornam a jogatina ainda mais imersiva.
Outra opção mais acessível é a Hisense MiniLED U7 Pro, que também oferece resolução 4K, VRR e baixa latência. A taxa de atualização da tela é de 165 Hz e, apesar de ser inferior à do modelo UR9SG, entrega ótima fluidez para uma gameplay limpa.
Sim. A Hisense tem mais de 50 anos de trajetória e é uma marca bastante popular lá fora. Inclusive, a Hisense foi a terceira maior fabricante de TVs do mundo no primeiro semestre de 2026, segundo dados da Counterpoint. A empresa ficou atrás apenas da Samsung (líder) e TCL (segunda colocada).
Não existe unanimidade. Ambas as marcas são confiáveis e populares no mercado de TVs, mas a escolha entre uma e outra varia muito de acordo com o portfólio oferecido e as experiências individuais.
A TCL é mais conhecida por estar em operação há mais tempo no Brasil. Seu portfólio inclui TVs com bom custo-benefício, de diferentes tamanhos, e com sistema operacional mais “amigável” (Roku OS e Google TV).
A Hisense também oferece televisores com preços mais acessíveis, de modelos LED ao miniLED RGB. Muitos aparelhos chegam com Google TV, mas outros usam o sistema proprietário VIDAA, que traz limitações de compatibilidade com alguns apps.
A Multi (antiga Multilaser) é a fabricante das TVs Hisense no Brasil, como revelado com exclusividade pelo Tecnoblog. A empresa brasileira produz os televisores na fábrica de Extrema, em Minas Gerais. Já a Hisense controla a parte comercial e decide para onde vai cada aparelho produzido.

articles.title: Si hay un videojuego que pueda romper internet, ese es GTA VI: su precarga está dejando picos de récord en tráfico
articles.text:
Este martes 10 de noviembre se abrió la precarga de Grand Theft Auto VI, el próximo juego de Rockstar Games que apunta a batir todos los récords posibles. Llega a las tiendas el 19 de noviembre, y hasta entonces está llevando al límite el tráfico de algunas teleoperadoras desde los servicios de Xbox y PlayStation.
Anticipando una saturación en la red. Se supone que la precarga de un juego distribuye la demanda a lo largo de varios días para que el día del lanzamiento no sature la red. En este caso, la precarga en sí ya ha batido récords. Dos de los mayores operadores de infraestructura de Europa han informado de nuevos máximos históricos desde que se abrieron las descargas el 10 de noviembre
Según las cifras. Virgin Media O2 afirma que el martes 10 de noviembre su red de banda ancha registró su pico vespertino más alto y su mayor volumen de datos diario total de la historia.
Según el operador británico, el pico superó en un 3,8% al récord anterior, establecido durante el partido de semifinales de la Champions entre el Arsenal y el Atlético de Madrid. Además, el volumen diario ha superado en un 4% al récord anterior, fijado por el lanzamiento de una temporada de Fortnite el 1 de noviembre.
Virgin Media informa de que el tráfico entre medianoche y la 1:00 AM. fue un 51,6% superior al de la misma hora de una semana antes, y que a las 9:00 AM el total de datos descargados se encontraba un 73,3% por encima del punto equivalente del martes anterior.
Probando hasta dónde llega la red. DE-CIX, que opera puntos de intercambio de internet, afirma que su nodo de Fráncfort alcanzó los 22,30 terabits por segundo a las 20:20 CET del 10 de noviembre. La empresa señala que esto representa un 19,06% por encima del récord anterior, establecido en enero de 2026.
En el conjunto de todos sus nodos a nivel mundial, DE-CIX registra un pico histórico sin precedentes de 33,01 terabits por segundo, registrando además nuevos máximos en EEUU, concretamente en Dallas, Phoenix y Chicago.
El director de tecnología (CTO) de DE-CIX, el Dr. Thomas King, declaraba que los grandes lanzamientos de videojuegos pueden disparar el tráfico en muy poco tiempo y que la magnitud de este repunte “no tiene rival”.
La predescarga es gigantesca. El tamaño de la instalación es de hasta 212 GB, dependiendo de la plataforma. Así que tiene todo el sentido del mundo que un juego de este calibre cuente con varios días de antelación para la predescarga, ya que la cantidad de datos que van a pasar entre un nodo y otro para satisfacer la demanda de millones de usuarios va a ser histórico.
Un portavoz de 1&1 confirmaba al medio alemán Golem un incremento insólito durante la noche del 9 al 10 de noviembre, que afectó a las conexiones tanto con PlayStation Network como con Xbox Live. Desde 1&1 indicaban que el tráfico hacia dichas plataformas multiplicaba por diez el nivel habitual para esa hora de la noche. La precarga de PlayStation 5 comenzó a medianoche del 10 de noviembre y la de Xbox Series X/S una hora más tarde. Vodafone indicaba además al medio que apreció un pequeño pico en torno a la 1:00 AM y que prefería esperar un día más antes de valorar el impacto.
De momento, sin problemas. 1&1 contaba además que el repunte no supone una sobrecarga para su red y prevé una mayor utilización en torno al 19 de noviembre, añadiendo que está bien preparada. DE-CIX señala que mantiene la utilización en el 75% o por debajo para dejar margen ante picos imprevistos.
Una encuesta encargada por Virgin Media O2 revelaba que el 46% de los jugadores espera descargar el juego antes del día de lanzamiento, el 78% ha modificado o planea modificar sus horarios para jugar, y el 18% ha comprobado o planea comprobar la velocidad de su banda ancha.
Lo que queda es ver cómo se comporta la red durante el día de lanzamiento, ya que involucra, no solo a los que aún no descargaron el juego, sino a los que van a proceder a descargarlo y a jugar en ese momento, y a los posibles parches y actualizaciones que traiga consigo el juego.
