articles.title: StarAgile Celebrates 10 Years of Excellence in Professional Training and Transformation
articles.text:
StarAgile Celebrates 10 Years of Excellence in Professional Training and Transformation
A decade after its founder left a 16-year IT career to build a training company, StarAgile has trained professionals across 100+ countries and is now preparing learners for the AI era.
Every journey has a starting point. For StarAgile, it began with a simple idea: learning should lead somewhere. Ten years on, that idea has grown into a community of 3,00,000+ professionals in more than 100 countries, each one building a better career, one skill at a time. In 2016, Narshimma walked away from a 16-year career in IT. The founder grew from a software professional into a project manager and Agile coach, with a stable job and a young family at home. What came next was a two-seater coworking space, one colleague from sales, no investors, and a plan to deliver Scrum training people could actually use.
Its learners include first-time Scrum Masters, project managers preparing for PMP, testers moving into automation, and engineers learning DevOps and cloud. The company says the milestone belongs as much to them as to the team behind it.
The vision behind StarAgile
The idea began while training people who joined the founder’s projects. Teaching turned out to be something Narshimma loved, especially watching people put new skills to work the very next day. That raised a question: what if learning was about building skills people could take straight back to their careers?
“I genuinely loved teaching,” Narashimma says. “And I loved something even more, seeing people learn something today and use it in their work in the future.”
That thinking still shapes every course. Sessions are built around real projects, case studies, and capstone work, so learners practise what they will face at work.
Key milestones in StarAgile’s journey
The early days were quiet. The first enrolment came from a former colleague, and the first batch had nine students. For the team, those nine proved something real had begun.
Growth came by word of mouth, as each satisfied learner recommended another. A few numbers show the scale of the journey.
StarAgile at 10
- 3,00,000+ professionals trained
- 100+ countries reached
- 300+ hiring partners
- 50,000+ enrolments in Certified Scrum Master alone
- 4.7/5 on Truspilot and 4.8/5 on Google
Beyond Scrum, Leading SAFe Agilist has crossed 25,000 enrolments, and PMP certification has drawn close to 21,000 learners.
The company has also received recognition along the way. It has been named Best Skill Learning Institute of the Year by Brands Impact, Edutech Company of the Year by The Corporate Titan, and Institute with the Best Placement by Mantra.
Responding to evolving needs
The skills employers want today are not the ones they wanted in 2016. Back then, learners asked about Scrum. Today, they ask about agentic AI. Agile was once a software team’s concern. Now it is used in banks, hospitals and marketing departments.
StarAgile has adjusted its catalogue accordingly. Learners can now choose from Generative AI and Agentic AI programs, AI-focused micro-credentials for Scrum Masters and product owners, and AI-Powered versions of project management and analytics courses. Several advanced programs are offered with Vishlesan i HUB at IIT Patna.
The company has also worked to make learning more accessible. Beyond live instructor-led classes, it offers self-paced courses for busy professionals, interview preparation bootcamps, and DevOps training in Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada. Corporate training programs help companies upskill whole teams.
Offering Industry-relevant certifications
StarAgile’s catalogue now runs across Agile and Scrum, project management, DevOps and cloud, AI, data science, software testing, software development, digital marketing, quality management, and IT service and architecture. Learners can prepare for well-known credentials, including CSM, CSPO, SAFe, PMP, PRINCE2, ITIL, TOGAF and Lean Six Sigma.
These are credentials that employers already know and trust. Whether someone is looking for a first job, a promotion, or a career change, a recognized certification gives them something concrete to show. StarAgile’s role is to teach it in a way learners can use at work from the very first week.
Placement support is part of that approach. Programs in DevOps, data science, and automation testing include placement preparation, and the company says its learners have gone on to roles at well-known organizations.
Building trust through quality, expertise
Training is a trust business, because the people spend their money and time, and demand good results. StarAgile has earned that trust through experienced trainers, clear pricing, and easy-to-find information on its site.
Trainers carry much of that reputation. Many have years of hands-on experience, and learners often mention in their reviews that trainers turn difficult frameworks into everyday language and stay available for questions after class.
StarAgile says it will keep investigating trainer quality as the catalogue grows. “StarAgile wasn’t built overnight,” Narshimma says. “It was built through belief, persistence, and the courage to keep going.”
Looking ahead
The next 10 years will bring hard-to-predict changes, but StarAgile already knows where it wants to put its energy.
AI will stay central. As it keeps reshaping how people work, StarAgile plans to keep refreshing its courses, so learners joining in 2030 aren't studying yesterday’s tools.
Access will widen. Companies want to bring more programs to learners in regional languages, and StarAgile will build on its DevOps courses in Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada, so language is never the reason someone misses out on a better career.
Collaborations will deepen StarAgile's aim to work more closely with academic partners such as Vishlesan I Hub IIT Patna, and with companies that need skilled teams, through corporate training built around what each team actually needs.

articles.title: iRobot Roomba Max 875 Combo, análisis: si tienes alfombras, este es el robot que te va a alegrar la vida
articles.text:
iRobot inventó las Roomba, logró la metonimia con el robot aspirador y ahora está en manos chinas y se nota porque bajo el capó cada vez se parece más a los modelos rivales y ojo, esto no siempre es una mala noticia. Sin ir más lejos, de pasar a tener modelos que friegan con cuentagotas y hacer experimentos de lo más variopintos, su propuesta final (de momento) pasa por un rodillo autolimpiable que usa agua caliente y sale un poquito a los lados. Spoiler: es todo un acierto.
Al final, es cuestión de dar con la tecla entre la innovación propia y los derroteros del sector, donde si bien es cierto que goza de madurez, todavía tiene algunas asignaturas pendientes. Este Roomba Max 875 Combo es el actual buque insignia de iRobot y, además de venir cargado hasta la bandera para fregar, también esconde algunas armas con las que quiere diferenciarse y convertirse en el mejor robot aspirador del año. ¿Lo conseguirá? Lo hemos probado a fondo y esta ha sido nuestra experiencia.
✅ Cómpralo si...
- Tu casa es grande.
- Tienes muchas alfombras.
- Buscas un modelo completo y con una app fácil de usar.
❌ No lo compres si...
- Necesitas que tu aspirador sea compatible con Matter.
- Quieres lo mejor en calidad precio.
- Tienes un hogar con mascotas.
Lo esencial en 30 segundos
El Roomba Max 875 Combo es el mejor robot aspirador de iRobot en lo global, y en este sentido cabe esperar unos acabados premium, su app facilísima y cuidada, una navegación esmerada o que tenga batería para rato, pero hay un segmento donde no tiene rival: aspirar alfombras. Aquí el "truco" está en que además de tener mucha presión, hace una especie de vacío que le permite atrapar mejor el polvo que queda atrapado en el textil y que cuesta horrores (a mano, suele suponer ponerlo a tope y dar varias pasadas) sacar.
Dicho esto, también friega como pocos, gracias a que tiene un rodillo largo, extensible y que además rota mucho y presiona la superficie, que cuando lo requieres además pulveriza con agua jabonosa. Ya no es solo una limpieza de mantenimiento, es que si hay manchas secas como por ejemplo de café, las detecta y elimina. En pocas palabras: es EL ROBOT para casas con alfombras y hay muchas manchas, por ejemplo porque hay peques en casa. Oye, ¿y las mascotas? Bastante bien, pero no es el mejor de la casa para lidiar con el pelo.
Roomba Max 875 Robot Aspirador, 35000Pa, 80°C Autolimpieza Mopa | iRobot Base AutoWash, Fregado con Agua Caliente,Flujo de Aire Ciclónico, Pretratamiento de Manchas, Navegación LiDAR
Nuestra experiencia con el Roomba Max 875 Combo
La Roomba de siempre ya no es la de toda la vida. Una Roomba, especialmente a partir de la gama media, se caracteriza por unos acabados sublimes: texturas llamativas que emulan la madera, el tejido o el metal, líneas sobrias... y este este Max 875 Combo lo cumple a rajatabla. Vamos, que entra por los ojos: su base aúna elegancia y practicidad. Pero donde llegan las curvas es el robot al darle la vuelta: sorpresa mayúscula con el rodillo, que no es doble ni de goma como es costumbre en esta gama, sino un único rodillo de cerdas y goma, un paso atrás si me preguntan. Asimismo, solo tiene un cepillo lateral, pero en el lado bueno es extraíble al igual que el rodillo de fregar, una excelsa mopa cilíndrica con tapa que va de lado a lado.
Qué navegación. Las Roomba se han resistido históricamente a la típica txapela láser, pero eso no significa que que carezca de esa tecnología: combina LiDAR con cámara e IA con reconocimiento de objetos y no se pierde ni queriendo. Navega rápido, bien y además mide muy bien por dónde cabe y por dónde no y eso es una buenísima noticia para los hogares con muchos recovecos. El algoritmo de navegación de iRobot siempre ha estado por encima de la media, pero ahora mismo no tiene rival: es cierto que en la gama alta es difícil que un aspirador se pierda, pero que no se pierda, ni atropelle y además llegue bien a los sitios donde cabe es otra historia en la que las Roomba destacan.
Brilla en alfombras. Este robot aspirador aspira y friega que da gusto en líneas generales. Es cierto que al ser algo grandote le cuesta pasar por debajo de las puertas de los armarios de la cocina, pero se mueve bien y se mete bien y ahí, el aspirador rinde bien y gracias al cepillo lateral extraíble llega a casi todas las esquinas, aunque obviamente mejor despejar la casa antes de limpiar. El fregado es de matrícula de honor y es más, incluso esas manchas pequeñas y secas salen si activas el pulverizado en esa zona, que esencialmente humedece más el agua.
¿Que hay una alfombra? Pues cubre el rodillo de fregar con una tapa y, algo diferencial es la tecnología Sealforce, que despliega una especie de faldón desde el chasis para sellar físicamente el robot contra el tejido y concentrar la succión. Aunque solo se forma cualitativa, las alfombras finas las deja limpísimas (aunque a veces corre el riesgo de arrastrarla) y donde más impresiona es en las gruesas a las que sube: ahí logra que al agitarla prácticamente no suelte partículas.
Incombustible. La prueba estándar que usamos para medir la duración de la batería es ponerlo solo a aspirar en su versión más exigente (en este caso, limpieza profunda, que además refuerza las pasadas). Le ha costado aspirar los 55 metros cuadrados que tiene mi piso unos 60 minutos, gastando un 28% de batería en la operación. Vamos, que podría limpiar más de tres casas como la mía, la verdad es que pocos robots aspiradores gastan tan poco en este modo. No obstante y teniendo en cuenta que la mayor parte de las ocasiones he usado el modo normal o el modo inteligente, la batería da para mucho más. Aún así, en caso de quedarse a medias, deja la tarea pendiente y la vuelve a retomar cuando se ha recargado lo suficiente.
Mantenimiento: traga agua que da gusto. Al volver de aspirar y fregar, el robot depósito de sólidos se vacía por succión, el rodillo se limpia y se seca con aire caliente, quedando listo para la próxima misión de limpieza. En estos días lo único que he tenido que hacer es preocuparme de llenar el depósito de agua limpia, ya que gasta bastante en la autolimpieza y el modo pulverización, vaciarlo una vez y eso sí, preocuparme de quitar los pelos que se quedan enganchados en las cerdas de los rodillos, algo que cuando solo son de goma sucede menos y además se retiran mejor.

Roomba Max 875 Combo, la opinión de Xataka
Hay algo indudable en esta nueva iRobot: quiere llegar a todos los públicos y además, ser la mejor opción para todo tipo de perfiles. De hecho, hasta tiene un modelo que barre y friega por poco más de 200 euros. Y con este Roomba Max 875 Combo el nicho es claro: un buen aspirado que brilla en hogares con alfombras y aderezado con un fregado superlativo.
Si además tenemos en cuenta que su app sigue siendo magnífica en interfaz y claridad, lo que permite que no solo gente tecnológica como yo puedan sacarle todo el jugo, sino también mi madre. Puede que este modelo concreto no sea el aspirador que le compraría a mi madre, pero sí que tengo claro que sería una Roomba porque su aplicación es fácil de usar como ninguna otra.
Asimismo, también es sobresaliente en diseño, acabados, cómoda de mantener siempre listo y tiene batería para rato. Eso sí, teniendo en cuenta el PVP de este robot aspirador, yo le pediría la excelencia en todo y creo que con los hogares con mascota ha dado un paso atrás. Sin ir más lejos, su hermano pequeño el Roomba Max 775 Combo es una opción mejor: tiene dos rodillos para aspirar y son solo de goma.
¿Lo recomiendo?
Si tu casa tiene muchas alfombras, es de lo mejor que hay para olvidarte de aspirarlas a mano o quieres reducir esa limpieza manual a lo mínimo imprescindible. Asimismo, es una opción de lo más completa en general y con una app intuitiva, por lo que puede ser interesante para aquellas personas que no sean techies y quieran un robot aspirador de calidad. Eso sí, hay una premisa en ambos casos: que el precio no sea un problema.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.text:
Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.
On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.
Turning a Windows defense against itself
The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.
By manipulating Windows Object Manager symbolic links, the attacker causes Defender to open the CLFS container in the security context of the antimalware engine. If an associated authentication file is missing, CLFS creates it using Defender’s System privileges. Because CLFS assigns the newly created file the Discretionary Access Control List of the original file, the attacker may gain access to a file created with System privileges, allowing the file-creation operation to be abused as part of a privilege-escalation attack.
Ironically, the vulnerability stems from a security measure Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to prevent attackers from exploiting other vulnerabilities in CLFS.
“If everything is chained correctly, funnily this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation [of] privileges,” Nightmare Eclipse wrote. “Everything is done properly by Microsoft here but the logic allows abuse.”

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.
U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.
The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 13, 2026: Huang was not confident in his successor, Colette Kress; reports describe Huang as ‘broken’
More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.
Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”
Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.
November 12, 2026: Democrats launch investigation into Nvidia; Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick summoned to testify before Senate Banking Committee
In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.
“Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.
That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.
“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.
November 12, 2026: Huang was having a third affair with another Nvidia employee, according to Reuters
After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.
November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO; Huang agrees to testify before Congress
Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.
Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.
Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.
November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says
The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.
According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.
November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair
Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing
Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.
“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy
U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”
Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.
Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action
Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.
The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations
Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.
Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.
Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.
These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”
“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.text:
Popular gaming chair and desk maker Secretlab launches dedicated US brick-and-mortar locations — new shop in LA, spaces in Best Buy
Just in time for Black Friday
Secretlab, maker of some of the best gaming chairs and also popular for its gaming desks, is launching a brick-and-mortar retail initiative in the US, giving customers the chance to see its hardware in person for the first time. The new stores will open on November 18; the company is opening a dedicated retail store in West Hollywood, LA, as well as dedicated retail spaces at 15 Best Buy locations.

As noted, Secretlab's new stores will open on November 18. Its LA store is located at 8464 Melrose Avenue, West Hollywood, and will feature a physical showcase of its most popular products as well as 1-on-1 consultations. Opening day will feature a luck draw giveaway, with the first 50 visitors entered into a lottery to win a Secretlab Magnus Evo desk. The LA store will include showcases of some of the company's special edition and limited designs, such as its Pokémon collaboration.
Beyond LA, the company is launching 15 dedicated retail spaces at Best Buy, in a total of 9 states. Early locations are California, Florida, Colorado, Virginia, Washington, Idaho, Alabama, Pennsylvania, and Texas. The company says more stores are to come. These stores will feature a Secretlab retail setup for hands-on with its chairs and desks.
For a product lineup with a heavy physical focus, the opportunity to try out products before you buy should be a welcome one for customers. There will be stock on hand so that customers can take products home with them on the day, rather than having to order online.
Secretlab recently unveiled its new Secretlab Atlas, the company's first task chair designed for office work and productivity, rather than gaming. Meanwhile, it still maintains its Titan Evo for games, as well as the Secretlab Magnus Pro and Magnus Evo sit-stand desks.

articles.title: "Hey Gemini": Dieses Google-Gerät bekommt als erstes ein neues Aktivierungswort
articles.text:
„Hey Gemini“: Dieses Google-Gerät bekommt als erstes ein neues Aktivierungswort
Google arbeitet seit geraumer Zeit daran, Gemini zum neuen Platzhirsch auf seinen smarten Produkten zu machen. Zunächst hat der KI-Assistent den Google Assistant auf Smartphones abgelöst. Android-User:innen waren davon nicht allzu begeistert und haben Umwege gefunden, um den alten Sprachassistenten zu reaktivieren. Trotz der Gegenwehr zieht Google seine Pläne weiter durch. Das zeigt sich jetzt mit einem neuen Produkt-Release.
Hey Gemini startet auf dem ersten Google-Gerät
Google hat in Zusammenarbeit mit Warby Parker, Gentle Monster und Samsung neue Smartglasses vorgestellt. Die cleveren Brillen sollen User:innen „Echtzeithilfe im Laufe des Tages liefern, immer dann, wenn sie sie benötigen.“ Die Hilfe kommt in diesem Fall von einer Künstlichen Intelligenz, genauer gesagt von Gemini. Nutzer:innen können etwa ein Plakat mit einem Event ansehen, Gemini aktivieren und die KI bitten, das Datum als Termin im Kalender einzutragen.
Wie es in der Ankündigung heißt, können User:innen die KI-Hilfe auch per Sprachbefehl aktivieren. Und dafür können sie nicht nur wie gewohnt „Hey Google“ oder „OK Google“ sagen. Daneben reagiert Googles KI auch auf den Smartglasses auf „Hey Gemini“. Die alten Aktivierungswörter funktionieren zwar weiterhin, doch beginnt Google durch diese Neuerung den Schritt zur finalen Umstellung.
Damit geht Google einen ähnlichen Weg wie schon bei der Implementierung von Gemini als Assistant-Ersatz. Zunächst konnte die KI optional auf Android-Smartphones eingesetzt werden. Zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt wurden alle User:innen zwangsweise auf die KI umgestellt. Ähnlich dürfte es auch bei „OK Google“ und „Hey Gemini“ ablaufen, sobald sich die Nutzer:innen an das neue Aktivierungswort gewöhnt haben.
Für ältere Geräte dürfte aber wohl noch einige Zeit ins Land gehen, bevor ein neues Aktivierungswort ansteht. Denkbar wäre, dass Google „Hey Gemini“ vorerst nur auf neuen Produkten anbietet, bevor ein Update die neue Methode auch auf anderen Geräten verfügbar macht. Denkbar wäre auch, dass einige ältere Geräte nicht mehr auf das neue Aktivierungswort umgezogen werden, da sie ohnehin nicht mehr lange von Google mit Updates versorgt werden.

articles.title: Cogeco-owned Oxio suffers data breach, customer data affected
articles.text:
Oxio, a home internet service provider owned by Cogeco, announced that it suffered a data breach.
In an email sent to customers (including MobileSyrup’s own Jon Lamont) on Thursday evening, Oxio said the breach involved a third-party software and service provider and records associated with both current and former accounts. Oxio says that, by law, it must keep its records for a certain period of time after an account is closed.
Oxio says that on Oct. 15, 2026, the data platform of an account management vendor that services Oxio and “several other” telecom companies was hacked. Following the breach, Oxio says it began an investigation with external forensics specialists. The good news is that Oxio says its internal networks and operational structure remain unaffected, and the incident is fully contained.
Oxio said hackers accessed names, email addresses, usernames, physical and mailing addresses, account notes, and statuses. But no passwords or financial information were accessed.
An Oxio customer on Reddit noted some additional details they received in response to an email to Oxio. The response noted that Oxio has “no evidence indicating that financial data was used fraudulently as a result of this incident.” Moreover, Oxio told the Redditor that “no credit card information was taken because our systems do not store or display customer credit card information.”
Comment
by
u/zalier26 from discussion
In its initial email notifying customers of the breach, Oxio said no immediate action is required but advised customers to watch for unsolicited calls, messages, or emails asking for verification codes, and to avoid reusing passwords across multiple services.
We reached out to Cogeco, and they issued this statement in response:
“On October 15, 2026, Cogeco was made aware of a security incident involving one of our third-party software and service providers supporting the oxio brand. Upon learning of this incident, we took immediate action to confirm containment and to understand the impact of the incident. The third-party service provider has confirmed that the incident is fully contained, and we can confirm that Cogeco and oxio’s own internal networks, systems, and operations were not affected and remain secure. We are committed to maintaining the privacy of personal information, and we regret any concern this third-party service provider incident may cause our customers. We have communicated directly with impacted individuals to provide tailored support and guidance.”
Oxio isn’t the only Canadian telecom service provider that’s been affected by a data breach recently. Quebecor’s Freedom suffered two breaches of its customer account management platform; Rogers and its subsidiary Fido suffered a similar breach back in March that leaked names, contact information, account numbers, and language preferences; and Telus suffered a breach that saw customer accounts accessed between Feb. 2025 and June 2026.

articles.title: Grosse chute de prix pour Borderlands 4 sur PS5
articles.text:
Borderlands 4 est actuellement proposé à 13,69 € sur PS5 chez E.Leclerc, alors qu’on le trouve habituellement autour de 30 €. L’offre est disponible jusqu’au 3 janvier 2027.
Bienvenue sur Kairos, planète de tous les excès
Vous aimez ouvrir des coffres et tomber sur un fusil qui tire des roquettes électriques ? Bienvenue dans Borderlands 4. Cette fois, Gearbox envoie ses Chasseurs de l’Arche sur Kairos, une planète sous la coupe du Gardien du Temps, un tyran qu’il va falloir déloger à grands coups de plomb. Quatre nouveaux héros sont jouables dès le départ, chacun avec sa façon bien à lui de semer le chaos.
La grosse évolution de cet épisode, c’est son monde ouvert d’un seul tenant. On file d’une région à l’autre au grappin, en planeur ou au volant de son véhicule, et on passe beaucoup moins de temps devant les écrans de chargement. Pour le reste, la formule fait ce qu’elle sait faire de mieux. On peaufine son build, on enchaîne les boss pour récupérer des armes toujours plus folles, et on recommence. Le tout prend une autre dimension à plusieurs, puisque le jeu se joue jusqu’à quatre en coopération. Et une fois l’histoire terminée, un mode de fin de partie avec plusieurs paliers de difficulté prend le relais. De quoi y passer des dizaines d’heures.
Un loot légendaire à prix cassé ?
Le jeu était sorti à 79,99 €, et Leclerc le vendait encore 53,99 € lors de notre test. À 13,69 €, son prix a été divisé par près de quatre depuis.
En comparaison, il est actuellement disponible à 17,99 € sur la Fnac et à 16,99 € chez Cdiscount.
Selon notre test, Borderlands 4 garde quelques petites marges de progression. Les armes pourraient avoir un peu plus de punch, et l’exploration séduit surtout dans les premières régions. Rien qui empêche de passer de bonnes soirées à se défouler entre amis, d’autant que le jeu ne coûte plus que le prix d’une place de ciné et d’un paquet de pop-corn.
Le jeu se retire gratuitement en Click & Collect dans les 164 magasins participants, ou se fait livrer à partir de 4,90 €.
Les extensions sorties depuis ne sont pas comprises dans l’offre.

articles.title: Firefox : vous pouvez désormais tester Mini Window en version stable
articles.text:
Mozilla publie Firefox 160. Le navigateur ajoute la fenêtre flottante Mini Window, une vitesse de lecture réglable en Picture-in-Picture, les fichiers MKV avec audio FLAC, MP3 ou PCM et la reconnaissance vocale pour les sites web.
La mise à jour est disponible depuis quelques jours. Rappelons que Mozilla sort une version tous les quinze jours, et la dernière touche autant l’interface que les outils des développeurs.
Mini Window, fichiers MKV et reconnaissance vocale au programme
La fonctionnalité Mini Window permet de sortir un onglet, ou une partie de page, dans une petite fenêtre toujours au premier plan. La fonction était testée dans Firefox Nightly, derrière une option cachée des paramètres avancés de about:config. Elle arrive déjà dans la version stable, mais Mozilla parle d’une première version et réclame des retours sur sa plateforme Mozilla Connect.
Le lecteur Picture-in-Picture, qui détache une vidéo de sa page, propose désormais un réglage de vitesse de 0,25x à 2,0x. Il s’affiche seulement si la fenêtre est de taille moyenne ou plus grande. Firefox lit aussi les fichiers MKV dont l’audio est en FLAC, MP3 ou PCM. Mozilla a longtemps boudé le MP3 faute d’usage mais les développeurs ont finalement changé d’avis. Sur macOS, WebGL passe désormais par Metal, l’API graphique d’Apple, ce qui peut accélérer certains sites.
- Gratuit et open source
- Protection renforcée contre le pistage
- Nombreuses extensions et personnalisations
Côté développeurs, Firefox gère SpeechRecognition, un volet des interfaces de programmation Web Speech API. La reconnaissance fonctionne en temps réel, dans 40 langues, et « sur l'appareil ». Le son est donc traité par la machine elle-même, pas par un serveur distant.
Dans Smart Window, l’outil Organize Tabs parle désormais français. Il propose des groupes d’onglets sur un même sujet et nomme chaque groupe. Le déploiement est progressif. Nous rapportions en août que Smart Window était réservée aux Américains et aux Canadiens, en anglais. La bêta s’est ouverte en France le 17 septembre, avec l’intégration de Mistral Small 4. Le quotidien évolue aussi. Les entrées de l’historique se glissent de la barre latérale vers les onglets. Le menu de la barre d’adresse affiche « Paste and Search » pour un terme copié. Le domaine y contraste mieux avec le reste de l’adresse. Un bouton « Never allow » bloque les sites qui réclament sans cesse de gérer les liens mailto:. Mozilla corrige aussi la perte du premier caractère tapé vite, un gel sur certains intranets et plusieurs bugs macOS. La version inclut des correctifs de sécurité.

articles.title: Sense G1 : Huawei lance un capteur de glycémie certifié au plus haut niveau médical — Frandroid
articles.text:
Huawei prépare le terrain de la santé au poignet depuis plusieurs années. Ses montres mesurent déjà la tension artérielle avec un vrai tensiomètre intégré au bracelet, comme la Watch D3. Fin septembre, He Gang, patron de la branche grand public, avait aussi promis un appareil de mesure de la glycémie après quatre ans de recherche.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelles sont les meilleures montres connectées en novembre 2026 ?
            
Ce produit a maintenant un nom, le Sense G1, que Huawei a présenté ce vendredi 13 novembre en Chine avec une simple affiche publiée sur Weibo. Contrairement à la Watch D3 pour la tension, la montre se contente ici d’afficher les valeurs : la mesure est faite par un capteur séparé, collé à l’arrière du bras.
Le Sense G1 prend la forme d’un petit disque blanc, que Huawei Central compare à un AirTag d’Apple. D’après l’affiche officielle, les valeurs s’affichent sur le smartphone ou la montre connectée, avec une alerte quand la glycémie sort des limites. Le capteur a obtenu le 30 octobre l’autorisation de l’agence chinoise du médicament comme dispositif médical de classe III. C’est le niveau le plus élevé en Chine, alors que la marque n’avait obtenu jusqu’alors que des homologations de classe II, pour son tensiomètre au poignet ou sa détection de l’apnée du sommeil.
Une aiguille sous la peau, comme chez Abbott et Dexcom
Sur le papier, le Sense G1 reprend la recette des capteurs déjà vendus en pharmacie. Le site chinois IT Home s’appuie sur des fuites publiées avant l’annonce. Il décrit un filament souple glissé sous la peau, recouvert d’une enzyme (la glucose oxydase) et relié à une électrode. Ce filament mesure le glucose dans le liquide interstitiel, celui qui baigne les cellules, puis en déduit la glycémie. Le FreeStyle Libre 3 d’Abbott et le Dexcom ONE+, les capteurs de glycémie connectés les plus populaires, fonctionnent exactement de cette façon.
Huawei mettrait en avant une aiguille cachée dans l’applicateur et un capteur qui supporte la baignade, mais il faut toujours se percer la peau, comme avec les concurrents. Le délai de 5 à 15 minutes s’explique d’ailleurs par cette méthode : le sucre met quelques minutes à passer du sang vers ce liquide.
Toujours selon IT Home, le MARD serait inférieur à 10 %. Cet indicateur donne l’écart moyen entre les valeurs du capteur et une prise de sang de référence, et plus il est bas, plus le capteur est précis. À titre de comparaison, le FreeStyle Libre 3 affiche 8,9 % chez l’adulte, d’après le guide de l’American Diabetes Association, qui reprend les chiffres d’Abbott. Le Sense G1 se porterait environ deux semaines. C’est autant que le Libre 3 et un peu plus que les 10 jours du Dexcom ONE+ retenus par la Haute Autorité de santé.
La mesure sans piqûre reste le vrai objectif
Huawei ne cache pas que la suite se jouera au poignet. Dès 2025, Rico Zhang, patron des montres connectées de Huawei, nous expliquait ne pas vouloir de montres réservées au sport, et la glycémie faisait partie de ses projets. Certaines montres de la marque proposent déjà une évaluation du risque d’hyperglycémie, mais elle classe l’utilisateur par niveau de risque, sans jamais donner de valeur chiffrée. Le Sense G1 ouvre à Huawei le suivi médical du diabète, avec une homologation de classe III, en attendant une mesure non invasive par la montre.
Aucun concurrent ne mesure encore la glycémie sans piqûre. En janvier 2025, Hon Pak, responsable de la santé numérique chez Samsung, a confirmé que le groupe développait un capteur optique de glycémie en continu. En juin 2025, Garmin a déposé un brevet pour estimer avec les capteurs optiques de ses montres l’hémoglobine glyquée (HbA1c), qui reflète la glycémie moyenne sur environ trois mois. Ce chiffre montre une tendance de fond et ne remplace pas une mesure en temps réel. Apple travaille aussi sur le sujet depuis des années sans avoir rien lancé : en attendant, ses montres affichent les valeurs d’un capteur Dexcom.
Pour l’heure, Huawei n’a donné ni prix ni date de sortie. Le capteur pourrait être présenté officiellement fin novembre, en même temps que le Mate X8 et le MateBook Fold S, dont les précommandes ouvrent ce samedi 14 novembre en Chine. Pour arriver en France, le Sense G1 devra obtenir un marquage CE de dispositif médical, et Huawei n’a encore rien dit sur les montres de sa gamme qui seront compatibles.

articles.title: Cómo saber si una tienda online es real antes de pagar y qué hacer si ya compraste en una falsa
articles.text:
Antes de pagar en una tienda online conviene hacer tres comprobaciones: que la empresa exista, que la dirección web sea la oficial y que el cobro se haga dentro del sitio. Los organismos de defensa del consumidor de Argentina las recomiendan de cara a las compras de Black Friday y de fin de año.
El Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires publicó el 30 de octubre de 2026 cinco consejos para el Cyber Monday, que se realizó del 2 al 4 de noviembre del mismo año. Su Dirección General de Defensa y Protección al Consumidor advirtió sobre correos y mensajes de WhatsApp con enlaces a supuestas ofertas exclusivas.
Para esos casos, el organismo recomienda no ingresar datos personales ni bancarios en páginas sospechosas, entrar directamente a los sitios oficiales de las marcas y guardar capturas de las publicaciones, de los precios y de la confirmación de compra.
Tres controles antes de cargar la tarjeta
El primero es comprobar que el comercio existe. Según la página de derechos del consumidor del Gobierno nacional, las empresas argentinas deben informar su nombre y su número de CUIT, la clave de identificación tributaria. Ese dato y la razón social permiten verificar la veracidad del comercio.
Otra página oficial agrega que la existencia legal de un sitio con dudas puede constatarse en NIC Argentina, el organismo que registra los dominios terminados en .ar. Si una web que se presenta como una cadena conocida figura a nombre de un particular, el dato no coincide.
El segundo control es la dirección. El Gobierno nacional aconseja no entrar a una tienda desde un correo o un mensaje de aplicaciones como WhatsApp, porque pueden llevar a sitios falsos que copian la identidad de la página real. Lo indicado es escribir la dirección en el navegador.
El candado y la sigla “https” no bastan como garantía de autenticidad. Los organismos recomiendan exigirlos antes de ingresar datos de tarjeta, pero indican que cifran la conexión: no prueban quién está del otro lado.
El tercer control es el medio de pago. Un documento del Gobierno nacional sugiere evitar pagos en efectivo, giros o empresas de envío de dinero que no permitan verificar al vendedor, y preferir la tarjeta de crédito. Pide no pagar fuera de la plataforma donde se compra, porque la mayoría ofrece protección al comprador.
Qué hacer si ya se pagó
Ante una situación sospechosa, el Banco Central aconseja contactar al banco por sus canales oficiales. Conviene hacerlo cuanto antes y conservar todo lo que documente la operación: comprobantes, capturas de la publicación, mensajes, correos y la dirección web donde se compró.
Si la tienda existe pero incumple, el comprador puede reclamar. En la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, el reclamo se inicia en el sitio de la Dirección General de Defensa y Protección al Consumidor, y a nivel nacional en la ventanilla única federal de reclamos de Defensa del Consumidor.
Si el sitio era una estafa, el caso es penal. El Gobierno nacional indica hacer la denuncia en la comisaría o en la oficina receptora de denuncias del domicilio, con todo el material disponible. Se puede avisar a la Unidad Fiscal Especializada en Ciberdelincuencia del Ministerio Público Fiscal, por correo a denunciasufeci@mpf.gov.ar.
Arrepentimiento y garantía
En las compras por internet, el consumidor puede cancelar dentro de los 10 días corridos desde que recibe el producto, sin dar motivos. Los costos de la devolución corren por cuenta del vendedor, según la Ciudad de Buenos Aires.
Los sitios que venden deben incluir un botón de arrepentimiento, un enlace visible desde la página de inicio, según la Resolución 424/2020 de la Secretaría de Comercio Interior. Nadie puede pedir un trámite previo, y el vendedor tiene 24 horas para informar el código de identificación del trámite.
Los productos nuevos tienen por ley una garantía mínima de 6 meses y los usados de 3 meses, según el Gobierno nacional. El comercio puede ofrecer más tiempo, pero no menos.

articles.title: Denuncian un intento de estafa telefónica con el recién estrenado prefijo 400 de llamadas comerciales
articles.text:
El pasado 17 de octubre entró en vigor en España el nuevo prefijo 400, una numeración que las empresas deben utilizar para realizar llamadas comerciales que ayudará a los usuarios a identificarlas. Sin embargo, solo hemos tardado tres días en toparnos con el primer intento de estafa. ¿Por qué? Bueno, como contó un vecino de Puente Genil (Córdoba), recibió una llamada de un supuesto trabajador de Iberdrola que consiguió hacerse con sus datos bancarios.
Según explica Cordópolis, el afectado presentó una denuncia ante la Policía Local después de recibir una llamada desde un número que comenzaba por 400. Los agentes señalan que se trata de un intento de vishing, una técnica de fraude telefónico en la que los delincuentes suplantan la identidad de empresas conocidas para ganarse la confianza de sus víctimas y obtener datos confidenciales o, en el peor de los casos, dinero.
El prefijo 400 identifica una llamada comercial, pero no garantiza que sea segura
Lo curioso es que el Gobierno había reservado esta numeración precisamente para que los ciudadanos pudieran reconocer más fácilmente las llamadas comerciales. Se trata de números de nueve cifras que empiezan por 400 y que solo permiten realizar llamadas, no recibirlas. Es decir, no puedes devolver una llamada a estos números.
¿Significa esto que todas las llamadas con el 400 son fiables? La propia Policía Local de Puente Genil advierte de que no. Los estafadores pueden aprovechar la confianza que genera una numeración aparentemente oficial para engañarte, e incluso existen técnicas que permiten falsificar el identificador que aparece en la pantalla de tu móvil.
Por eso, si recibes una llamada inesperada en la que te solicitan información bancaria, contraseñas o códigos de verificación, lo mejor es no facilitar nada y contactar directamente con la empresa a través de sus canales oficiales. Y si ya has compartido tus datos bancarios, la Policía recomienda avisar inmediatamente a tu banco para evitar posibles operaciones fraudulentas.

articles.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
articles.text:
German defense technology company Quantum Systems confirmed that it detected an incident in late October that was part of an active cyberattack by "hostile actors."
The company responded quickly, working with relevant authorities to resolve the issue swiftly and ensure its unmanned systems could safely resume operations.
Quantum Systems is a German defense technology company that builds reconnaissance and interceptor drones, along with other unmanned systems and the software that controls them.
Its drones are in service with Germany’s military, and in October Germany announced funding to build tens of thousands of Quantum Systems interceptor drones in Ukraine for Ukrainian forces.
Quantum Systems believes it was targeted because of its recent announcement of support for Ukraine and says it is working closely with state authorities to investigate the attack.
“The European defense industry has been facing persistent cyberattacks for years,” Quantum Systems stated without making a specific attribution.
“Companies at the forefront of supporting Ukraine are being targeted precisely because our work is critically relevant to customers’ security.”
Update server compromised
According to reports from Der Spiegel and the Financial Times, citing internal sources, the compromise occurred via a malicious QBase update file.
QBase is Quantum Systems’ ground-control and mission-planning software, so the point of the compromise was the vendor’s update distribution server.
Der Spiegel identified the Vector reconnaissance drone, known as Falke in German military service, as one of the aircraft whose missions are planned with QBase.
The German outlet reports that the unscheduled update delivered to customers raised alarms within Quantum Systems, but it is unclear how many actually installed it.
Additional reports claim that the German armed forces grounded Quantum Systems drones as a precaution, excluding the company's systems from a recent military exercise.
The response reportedly involves the military counterintelligence (MAD), the domestic intelligence service (BfV), and the federal cybersecurity agency (BSI).
In July, another drone manufacturer, the Australian CubePilot, which also openly supports Ukraine, was targeted by a DNS hijacking attack that caused severe operational disruption.
DNS hijacking could, among other things, be used to deliver malicious updates to downstream users of CubePilot’s drone systems, though such a level of compromise was never confirmed.

articles.title: La empresa gallega Sargadelos cree que Nvidia copió su logotipo de uno de sus diseños: "En el fondo, nos gusta"
articles.text:
No pocas empresas, al sospechar que una multinacional les ha copiado, llaman inmediatamente a los abogados. Claro, a ver cómo litigas con Nvidia, la cual, tras su sorpaso a Apple, se ha tirado más de un año siendo la marca más valiosa del planeta. Así que una pequeña firma gallega de cerámica ha elegido otra postura: publicar la comparación en su propia web y que sean los clientes quienes opinen.
Sargadelos colgó en su blog de noticias una pregunta: ¿se parece el logotipo de Nvidia a la forma P de sus vajillas, un diseño que, asegura, crea y comercializa desde hace más de cincuenta años? La marca ya ha emitido su veredicto, que es que sí, que a su juicio es una copia, pero se lo toman con humor: “Que nos copien, nos prestigia y, en el fondo, nos gusta”. Pero ahora mismo bastante tendrá Jensen Huang tras su dimisión, a quien le crecen los amantes con cada nueva declaración. Su renuncia forzada como CEO nos recuerda que nadie es intocable. Y eso aplica tanto para Nvidia como para Sargadelos: ambas han estado a punto de morir un montón de veces.
Un ilustrado entre hierro y caolín. La empresa, lo que se dice gallega, no es del todo. Porque todo empieza con Antonio Raimundo Ibáñez, un asturiano de Oscos nacido en 1749 en una familia noble sin fortuna que se instaló en Ribadeo y prosperó con el comercio marítimo. Entretanto, la mítica “n” de nVidia data de 1993, el mismo año de la fundación, la cual se mantuvo sin alterar hasta 2006, cuando llegó el rediseño actual: el ojo perdió el negro, la tipografía se volvió más gruesa y la cursiva se sustituyó por una N mayúscula.
Sigamos con nuestro relato: en 1791 levantó con un socio la siderurgia de Sargadelos, que tras un contrato de munición en 1794 acabó fabricando desde cañerías hasta fuentes y barandillas. Con la protección de Godoy, el negocio creció, y en 1806 abrió la primera fábrica de loza de Galicia, aprovechando el caolín de la zona y el hueco que dejó la falta de cerámica inglesa. Carlos IV lo hizo marqués en 1808. Pero en 1809, en plena guerra de la Independencia, lo asesinaron.
Esplendor y ruina. La fábrica sobrevivió al marqués, pero a duras penas: cerró en 1832 y renació con nuevos socios. Su gran momento llegó en 1845, cuando una sociedad de Santiago asumió la gestión y trajo ceramistas ingleses de Staffordshire. En 1849 daba trabajo a más de mil familias y repartía su producción con 205 carros y 22 barcos de cabotaje. Eran los años de la célebre serie de la góndola y de las vajillas para Isabel II. Pero el regreso de la familia Ibáñez al mando en 1862, un puñado de pleitos y la falta de inversión la hundieron. En 1875 cerró para siempre. ¿Para siempre?
Un pintor, un exilio y un laboratorio. Durante casi un siglo, Sargadelos fue un recuerdo local. Hasta que Isaac Díaz Pardo, pintor, ceramista e intelectual galleguista, dio en los años cuarenta con un libro de 1922 sobre las antiguas fábricas. De las ruinas, en 1949 abrió un taller en O Castro de Samoedo, en Sada. Aquí ya se empieza a gestar una idea.
En 1955 viajó a Argentina, donde coincidió con exiliados gallegos como Luis Seoane, y de aquellas conversaciones nació en 1963 el Laboratorio de Formas, una iniciativa sin ánimo de lucro para rescatar, a través del diseño, la memoria artística de Galicia. Todo muy arty. En 1970 se inauguró una nueva fábrica circular en Cervo, junto a las ruinas de la original. Dos años después fueron declaradas Conjunto Histórico-Artístico.
Azul cobalto y muchos libros. El nuevo Sargadelos combinó el blanco y el azul cobalto con motivos prerrománicos y medievales, cruceiros, figuras mitológicas y series de retratos, de Rosalía de Castro a Picasso. De hecho, este rincón fue mucho más que una fábrica: tuvo editorial propia, un museo de arte contemporáneo en Sada y galerías que funcionan a la vez como tiendas y librerías de literatura gallega y portuguesa.
Quiebras, plantes y desplantes. Pero aquí no acaba la historia. Díaz Pardo dirigió el grupo hasta que, a comienzos de los 2000, otros accionistas lo apartaron. Murió en 2012, a los 91 años. Y, con una crisis en ciernes, la empresa volvió a tambalearse: en 2004 tomó el mando Segismundo García, y en 2013 la empresa pidió protección ante sus acreedores y despidió a 70 trabajadores. En 2014 se declaró insolvente, con unos cinco millones de deuda. Lo lógico era cerrar. Hasta que las aguas volvieron a su cauce y en 2016 volvieron a anunciar beneficios.
El último susto llegó en abril de 2025: la Inspección de Trabajo detectó 36 deficiencias de seguridad en Cervo, entre ellas la exposición a polvo de sílice, que había causado silicosis a, al menos, dos empleados. García respondió a una multa de 5.000 euros anunciando el cierre inmediato de la fábrica.
El ERTE y el cierre fantasma. Si Huang salvó seis veces a Nvidia, la supervivencia de Sargadelos esta vez dependió de la Xunta. Intervino, aflojaron la cartera ante una factoría de tanto valor histórico y se reanudó la producción. Pero (sí, este artículo tiene más giros que una novela de García Márquez), y este pero es importante, en noviembre se repitió la sombra de una muerte anunciada con un ERTE para 86 trabajadores. Fue entonces cuando Segismundo García dimitió como consejero delegado y, si bien sigue como administrador único, ahora es un consejo asesor quien toma las decisiones.
Marca incombustible. Con todo, Sargadelos vive uno de los mejores momentos en cuanto a imagen pública. Hoy día producen joyería, perfumes y hasta juguetes infantiles. Sus diseños han aparecido en películas de Almodóvar, ha colaborado con Chipperfield o Jasper Morrison y este verano Estrella Galicia lo eligió para un casco de Marc Márquez inspirado en sus grifos de cerveza. El grupo mantiene abiertas las dos fábricas, de Cervo y Sada, donde suma unos 245 empleados aproximadamente.
La ironía de la copia. Por eso la pulla a Nvidia tiene su gracia. Ibáñez montó su fábrica imitando la loza inglesa, con técnicas importadas de Bristol y jarrones inspirados en Wedgwood. Más de dos siglos después, Sargadelos disfruta del otro lado de la historia, de ser la casa a la que, dicen, le han copiado.
El patrón artístico al que aducen se ha visto en decenas de cuadros y composiciones arquitectónicas, pero aquí queda la duda, en el aire. Y que Nvidia conteste es lo de menos: ya ha logrado que se hable de una vajilla en la que es la mejor campaña de marketing en el peor momento de Nvidia del último lustro.

articles.title: Frammer AI launches live sports platform with Astro Malaysia as first customer
articles.text:
Frammer AI launches live sports platform with Astro Malaysia as first customer
Frammer AI launches its live sports platform with Astro Malaysia, turning match footage into social media clips in under 30 seconds.
The Indian AI video technology company can turn live sports footage into social media highlights in under 30 seconds, helping broadcasters reach fans while matches are still underway.
A goal, a last-minute winner or a match-defining moment can quickly become yesterday’s news on social media. Sports broadcasters need to get these moments in front of fans while the action is still fresh.
Frammer AI is looking to make that process faster with the launch of its live sports platform, bringing Astro Malaysia on board as its first customer. The partnership marks Frammer’s entry into sports, expanding its AI-powered video technology beyond news and entertainment.
Using its proprietary technology, Frammer can turn live sports footage into social media content in under 30 seconds. The platform is designed to help broadcasters publish highlights while matches are still unfolding, rather than wait for the event to end.
Turning live matches into social content
The platform converts live feeds into match highlights, vertical videos, player- and event-based clips, branded videos and other social media content. It lets rights holders create and distribute more content around every match without relying on large teams of editors and producers.
Astro, Malaysia’s leading content and entertainment company, is Frammer’s first sports customer. The broadcaster holds major sports rights, including the Premier League through the 2027/28 season and AFC competitions through 2028/29.
The collaboration will help Astro deliver match highlights and key moments to audiences across digital platforms, giving fans more ways to follow their favourite teams and players.
Nivendran Veerappan, Vice President and Head of Broadcast and Platform Engineering at Astro, said the partnership supports the company's commitment to bringing fans closer to live sports, wherever they choose to watch.
A new market for Frammer AI
The launch comes as sports streaming continues to grow. The global segment is valued at around $40 billion this year, with demand supported by new leagues, teams and events, expanding competitions, new formats and growing interest in niche sports.
Frammer believes this creates an opportunity for sports rights holders to get more value from the content they already produce and the rights they invest in. Faster content creation and distribution can help them reach audiences across more platforms and create additional opportunities for engagement and commercial returns.
"Astro as our first sports customer is a huge milestone as we enter the sports space," said Suparna Singh, CEO and Co-Founder of Frammer AI. She added that the company's goal is to help clients generate more content and audience value from every hour of sport they invest in.
Founded in 2023 by the former management team of New Delhi Television (NDTV), Frammer provides an AI-powered video studio for sports, entertainment and news.
Its clients include Medialive in Portugal, ABS-CBN in the Philippines, Media Prima in Malaysia, and The India Today Group and Network18 in India.
The company's technology also supports live streaming, key-moment creation, vertical short videos, automated FAST channels, and distribution across multiple platforms.
With Astro as its first sports customer, Frammer is taking its video infrastructure into a market where speed matters as much as the moment itself.

articles.title: 6 millions d'identifiants volés ont été récupérés par la police : comment savoir si vous êtes concerné ?
articles.text:
Europol vient de frapper un nouveau coup contre le monde des cybercriminels. Ce jeudi 12 novembre, l’agence européenne de police annonce avoir démantelé l’infrastructure de trois logiciels malveillants : Gootloader, CastleRAT et StealC. Avec l’aide de géants de la cybersécurité, les forces de l’ordre de neuf pays, dont l’Allemagne, les Pays-Bas, le Royaume-Uni et les États-Unis, ont saisi 235 serveurs et 257 noms de domaine.
Cette nouvelle opération d’envergure s’inscrit dans le cadre d’Endgame, « le plus grand effort international jamais mené contre les facilitateurs de rançongiciels », explique Europol dans son communiqué. En juin dernier, l’opération menée par la police européenne a déjà abouti à la disparition de près de 15 000 sites piratés. Quelques semaines plus tard, l’opération Endgame a permis de neutraliser deux autres virus redoutables, Amadey et StealC.
Trois virus loués aux pirates
Les trois logiciels malveillants démantelés cette semaine étaient mis à la disposition d’autres cybercriminels, moyennant le versement d’un abonnement en cryptomonnaies. Selon les investigations d’Europol, Gootloader se cachait surtout dans de faux documents juridiques, diffusés sur des sites compromis en amont. Il s’agit « souvent des sites WordPress ». Une fois le document téléchargé, l’ordinateur de la victime était rapidement infecté par Gootloader, ce qui finissait par aboutir à l’installation d’un ransomware. Les forces de l’ordre ont neutralisé plus de 650 sites web utilisés pour diffuser Gootloader au cours de l’opération.
Apparu l’an dernier, le malware CastleRAT permettait de prendre le contrôle intégral d’un ordinateur à distance. Le virus « a entraîné le chiffrement de nombreuses données, la paralysie de systèmes informatiques entiers, et a contraint les entreprises et organisations touchées à payer des rançons », précise Europol. De son côté, StealC était conçu pour dérober les mots de passe, les identifiants et les « identités numériques » stockés sur les ordinateurs infectés. Une fois déployé, le virus aspirait toutes les informations qu’il pouvait.
À lire aussi : Fuite de données – près de la moitié des Français ont été piratés cette année
Vos identifiants ont-ils été piratés ?
En fouillant dans les serveurs des pirates, les enquêteurs ont mis la main sur un véritable trésor numérique. Europol a découvert « plus de 6 millions d’identifiants de victimes » sur les serveurs. Selon les autorités, « les suspects utilisaient ces identifiants, volés aux victimes après les avoir infectées, pour les vendre et pour qu’ils soient ensuite utilisés dans d’autres cyberattaques ».
Les victimes vont être en mesure de vérifier si elles sont concernées. Les données volées par CastleRAT vont en effet être transmises à plusieurs plateformes de cybersécurité, dont le site Have I Been Pwned. Ce site, développé par le chercheur Troy Hunt, permet de vérifier gratuitement si son adresse mail figure dans une fuite de données. La plateforme open source, devenue l’alliée du FBI il y a plusieurs années, met régulièrement à jour sa base de données avec les dernières fuites recensées.
Il suffit de saisir l’adresse sur la page d’accueil du site. Si elle n’apparaît dans aucune fuite, un message vert vous le confirme. En cas de piratage, un avertissement rouge apparaît à l’écran avec les détails des violations concernées. Le site précise également quelles informations personnelles ont été compromises, comme votre nom, votre adresse ou votre IBAN. Si c’est le cas, changez immédiatement le mot de passe concerné, et activez la double authentification partout où celle-ci est disponible.

articles.title: Siri AI Developer Preview Lets iOS, iPadOS, and macOS Apps Integrate with Siri
articles.text:
Apple released the Siri AI Developer Preview in the 27.3 beta releases of its operating systems, enabling developers and apps to integrate with the assistant and hand off actions to it. During the Preview, access to Siri AI is restricted to developer builds and internal TestFlight testers.
Apple says that Siri AI is an entirely new version of its assistant which is "profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal".
Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more.
These new capabilities let users make natural language requests and have Siri AI carry out any custom action supported by the app. The framework also supports complex requests through Skills, a new feature that lets developers "teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience".
If a request does not specify an app name, it will automatically be routed to the app currently in the foreground, the app associated with an active Live Activity, or the app previously mentioned in the ongoing conversation. This allows users to continue conversations across an app and its Live Activity, or a different app altogether. While an app is running in the background, however, it will receive only requests that explicitly mention its name.
Requests can also include actions across apps, such as finding content in one app, sending it to another, and perform an action there.
Commenting on Apple's announcement, Reddit user sixtypercenttogether noted:
In my limited testing so far it does what it says. If you include a good description on your intent and parameters, Siri can figure it out. THIS is what Siri should have been all along, all the way back in 26.0.
User Medical_Lengthiness6 compared Apple's approach to integrating Siri AI to Google's AppFunctions:
Doing it via app intents was the right move. Google could have done this with the android intents but instead decided to make a completely different agent skills sdk that you have to implement.
All Apple Intelligence features, including Siri AI, may be subject to usage limits, with extended, premium access planned the future. Finally, developers besed in the EU should be aware that Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS.

articles.title: Steam's review queue is delaying indie launches, and developers blame a wave of AI-made games
articles.text:
In context: These days, almost anyone can get an AI chatbot to code a playable game in a few hours. The result is that social media is packed with people showing off their creations, many of which are being submitted to Steam for approval. Developers say that the growing line is now long enough to push genuine indie games past their own launch dates.
TwoMenGames is one of the studios caught up in this situation. The small team was supposed to release its first game, Amazing Slot Survivor, today. But the slot machine-themed roguelike never received Valve's approval in time. Instead, the studio posted that Steam's review was simply taking longer than expected, so it removed the release date and brought back the game's demo for now.
Rami Ismail, who co-created the indie hit Nuclear Throne, is stuck in the same line. His new turn-based train defense game, Australia Did It, was due on November 10. Yet its publisher, Mystic Forge, says the game has now spent weeks waiting on Valve's build review. So far, nobody can say when that will end.
Ismail gave Eurogamer a clearer timeline. The game entered the queue on October 20 and failed on November 5 over a minor controller input bug. His team patched it the same day. Since then, Valve hasn't sent a meaningful reply, even after several follow-ups.
Weirdly, waits like this used to be a console problem. Ismail says Steam had always been much quicker. Back then, submitting a game 10 to 14 days before launch was usually enough to fail Valve's review twice and still ship on time.
For its part, Valve admitted in a Steamworks post earlier this month that reviews were taking up to 12 business days, well past its usual three to five. It pinned much of that on a jump in submissions and on re-reviewing builds that fail basic checks. So now developers must play their game through Steam for at least five minutes before submitting.
The post doesn't blame AI, though. Valve also recently made clear it won't ban AI-made games from Steam. Ismail thinks that hands-off stance is backfiring. If bad actors can submit several cloned games a day, he argues, Valve will eventually need fees, restrictions or extra hoops that hurt genuine developers.
Valve says more changes to its review process are on the way. In the meantime, anyone planning a Steam launch should probably ignore the seven-business-day buffer Valve's own documentation still recommends and submit much earlier.

articles.title: Microsoft’s global outage may be worse than Amazon's or CrowdStrike's, expert says
articles.text:
A global outage taking down a wide range of Microsoft 365 services remains ongoing Friday morning.
The outage started midday Thursday, impacting users of Microsoft email, cloud, and AI services. Microsoft has documented the full list of services impacted by the error, while moving early Friday morning to protect customers around the world from losing emails during the extended disruptions.
“Recovery actions are ongoing,” the Microsoft 365 Status account confirmed on X. “To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours.”
Similar to recent world-shaking outages of widely used tech like Amazon Web Services and CrowdStrike, the Microsoft disruption looks like “one of the biggest outages of all time,” Ciaran Martin, the former head of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre, told NBC News. Possibly even “worse,” he suggested.
Businesses, hospitals, police departments, and schools were among those scrambling to work around the outage. In Japan, it disrupted government IT infrastructure, according to deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki. NBC’s report documented various harms, noting that “few public bodies were immune from the outage.” In some cases, doctors couldn’t send patients “important” updates on medication changes or follow-up care.
The financial sector suffered, too, with people blocked from making bank transfers since they couldn’t receive verification codes.
Justice systems were also hobbled. The Supreme Court in the Philippines saw its legal work derailed, NBC reported. And one US sheriff’s office in Colorado reported that the outage made it difficult for people to post bond for prisoners’ immediate release.
It’s unclear how many users were affected, but Microsoft estimated in January that the total number of paid Microsoft 365 commercial subscriptions exceeded 450 million.
Microsoft blames failed server health checks
On a status page, Microsoft said “we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident” and promised to “share a full Post-Incident Report with root cause and defense-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete.”
“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” Microsoft said on X.
But Microsoft’s public statements make clear that the tech giant was blindsided by the outage and struggled for hours to find mitigations that could reliably restore user access.

articles.title: Uber confirms hackers stole thousands of drivers' license information in data breach | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Uber is notifying thousands of drivers that their personal and driver’s license information was stolen during an October data breach at one of the company’s tech providers.
In notices filed this week with several U.S. attorneys general, including California, the ride-hail giant said it was notified on October 9 by the provider that hackers broke in and stole internal credentials, which were used to access Uber’s data.
The company said it subsequently began notifying affected drivers that their personal information was stored with the provider.
TechCrunch has learned that the provider is Fireworks AI, which lets developers access and use open AI models. Fireworks reported a data breach last month in which hackers stole its customers’ information, including billing data and some private AI datasets.
Online productivity startup Notion confirmed its data was also stolen in the Fireworks hack.
“The notices to drivers are in relation to a security incident impacting one of our third-party vendors, Fireworks.ai, which had access to some Uber data,” an Uber spokesperson told TechCrunch, deferring our questions to Fireworks.
Uber did not say how many customers are affected by the breach, nor how many drivers it was notifying about the incident.
When reached by email, a spokesperson for Fireworks confirmed that the company identified a security issue involving unauthorized access to some of its systems, which affected customer data, but the spokesperson did not address our questions about the incident.
According to data breach notices seen by TechCrunch, the stolen data includes driver’s licenses of 2,567 individuals in Massachusetts, 3,430 people across South Carolina, and 1,873 residents of Rhode Island. A filing with Illinois showed that some state residents had their driver’s license information stolen, but that the number of affected people was pending. Uber also notified drivers who live in California, but did not say how many had their information stolen.
The number is expected to rise as more data breach notifications roll in.
Fireworks attributed its breach to a financially motivated cybercriminal group whose goals are to sell stolen tokens for accessing large language models, or LLMs.
No known cybercriminal group has taken credit for the data theft.
This is Uber’s second known data breach this year. The company reported a security incident at its Uber Freight truck shipping unit, for which an extortion gang took credit for stealing data.
Updated with a response from Fireworks.
