articles.title: „Nvidia ist Nvidia wegen Jensen“: Warum Mitarbeiter jetzt Huangs Rückkehr an die Unternehmensspitze fordern
articles.text:
Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang tritt nach Affäre zurück: Warum Mitarbeiter jetzt seine Rückkehr fordern
Erst kürzlich ist Jensen Huang als Chef von Nvidia zurückgetreten. Auslöser war eine Affäre mit einer mutmaßlichen chinesischen Spionin. Der Skandal erschüttert nicht nur das Unternehmen, sondern auch die Börse: Mit einem Wert von bis zu 5,8 Milliarden Dollar gilt der Chiphersteller derzeit als das wertvollste Unternehmen der Welt. Laut Tagesschau brach der Aktienwert nach dem Rücktritt um bis zu 13 Prozent ein. Seit dem Höchststand Anfang Oktober haben Anleger:innen somit rund ein Drittel eingebüßt. Trotzdem setzen sich Mitarbeiter:innen jetzt dafür ein, dass Huang auf seinen Posten zurückkehrt.
Huang gesteht mehrere Affären
Lange Zeit galt Huang als das Gesicht des KI-Booms. Seit der Gründung im Jahr 1993 leitete er Nvidia und führte das Unternehmen zu Rekordzahlen. Bei Konferenzen und öffentlichen Auftritten predigte er stets die wichtige Rolle der neuen Technologie in allen Lebensbereichen. Am Wochenende folgte dann der Paukenschlag: Huang gab zu, seine Ehefrau mehrfach betrogen zu haben. Eine seiner Affären steht im Verdacht, vom chinesischen Geheimdienst angeworben worden zu sein. Mitte der Woche folgten Berichte über ein Verhältnis mit einer Nvidia-Managerin.
Wegen Huangs Affäre mit der mutmaßlichen Spionin, hat sich inzwischen auch das FBI eingeschaltet. Er selbst beteuerte, nicht gewusst zu haben, dass sie eine Spionin sein könnte – auch gegenüber dem US-Präsidenten. Die beiden haben in den vergangenen Jahren ein enges Verhältnis aufgebaut. Trump gab an, Huang selbst auf den Fall angesprochen zu haben, und nimmt ihn jetzt in Schutz. „Er sagte, dass er keine Ahnung gehabt habe, dass sie eine Spionin war, und ich glaube ihm das wirklich“, so der Präsident auf einer Pressekonferenz im Weißen Haus.
„Wenn ihr an die Mission glaubt, holt den Chef zurück
Huangs Rücktritt macht deutlich, dass der Großteil der Prozesse innerhalb des Unternehmens stark auf seine Person zugeschnitten waren. Laut Bloomberg berichten rund 60 Manager:innen direkt an ihn. Außerdem soll er bei offenen Fragen jederzeit erreichbar gewesen sein und Feedback beigesteuert haben. Nvidia-Finanzchefin Colette Kress hat seinen Posten in der Zwischenzeit kommissarisch übernommen. Laut internen Mitteilungen, die Wired einsehen konnte, fordern allerdings zahlreiche Mitarbeiter:innen Huangs Rückkehr.
In einem Beitrag wurde der Vorstand aufgefordert, die Meinung der Belegschaft zu berücksichtigen, bevor Maßnahmen ergriffen werden. Dieser hatte seitdem mehr als 1.600 Kommentare erhalten, in denen sich mehrere Mitarbeiter:innen für den Ex-CEO aussprachen. „Wenn ihr an die Mission glaubt, holt den Chef zurück“, schrieb eine Person. Eine weitere kommentierte: „Wir sind alle Menschen und können Fehler machen. Jensen hat so viel Gutes geleistet und verdient eine zweite Chance.“
In den Stunden nach dem Rücktritt veröffentlichten laut Wired mehrere Mitarbeiter:innen Linkedin-Beiträge, in denen sie ihre Unterstützung für Huang bekundeten. Eine dieser Personen soll ihr Vertrauen in dessen Führungsqualitäten sogar als „unerschütterlich“ beschrieben haben. Eine Person, die lange für Nvidia gearbeitet hat, sagte gegenüber Wired, dass der Wunsch nach Huangs Wiedereinsetzung intern weit verbreitet sei. Da sie nicht offiziell mit der Presse sprechen darf, wollte die Person anonym bleiben. Sie befürchte, das Unternehmen werde ohne seinen Gründer an der Spitze leiden. „Nvidia ist Nvidia wegen Jensen“, so die anonyme Quelle.
Laut Wired hätten viele Mitarbeiter:innen erwartet, dass der Vorstand seine Untersuchung zunächst abschließen würde, bevor größere Veränderungen folgen. Stattdessen verließ Huang das Unternehmen genau zu dem Zeitpunkt, als die Untersuchung begann. „Wenn Amerika den Mann im Stich lässt, der geholfen hat, seine Zukunft aufzubauen, dann verdient diese Welt Jensen Huang nicht“, heißt es laut Wired in der internen Nachricht.

articles.title: 8 Nigerian startups bag $4k each at FMYD, Cascador youth founders pitch day - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Eight Nigerian startups have each won NGN5 million (US$4,000) in non-dilutive funding at the pitch day of the Founders Programme run by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development (FMYD), through the Nigerian Youth Academy (NiYA), and Cascador.
The pilot programme drew more than 19,000 applications after launching on International Youth Day in August, with 17 founders from 13 states selected for a four-week accelerator. Participating startups are tackling challenges such as post-harvest losses, malnutrition, waste, vaccine cold chains, clean energy and digital education.
Implemented by technical partner Sapphital, the programme offered training in sales, customer service and investment readiness, as well as regulatory sessions with agencies including NEXIM Bank, SEC, NITDA, NAFDAC and the Nigeria Data Protection Commission.
The eight pitch day winners are SewPro, Biuda, Sparklean Station Nigeria, Backel Food Services, Shellify, Rèkool Access Technology, Agrosavvy Consult and Craft Planet. The remaining nine founders will each receive NGN1 million (US$750), and all 17 get access to Sapphital’s SMECore ERP platform.
“We share NiYA and FMYD’s commitment to giving Nigeria’s ambitious young founders the capital and practical support they need to build stronger businesses,” said Trish Thomas, CEO of Cascador. “Seeing eight deserving founders secure funding at Pitch Day is an encouraging outcome for the pilot.”
All graduates keep NiYA alumni status and priority for future opportunities. The academy aims to train 7 million young Nigerians within two years.

articles.title: De Batman a 007: Robert Pattinson podría ser el nuevo James Bond
articles.text:
Robert Pattinson sería la primera opción de Amazon como nuevo James Bond, según reporta Puck News (vía ScreenTime). El actor británico todavía no tendría el papel asegurado, pero habría recibido la oferta más suculenta entre quienes conforman la lista corta definitiva para ser el próximo 007.
De momento, los montos supuestamente presentados no se han dado a conocer. No obstante, la información citada indica que Amazon MGM Studios puso a disposición de Robert Pattinson un contrato por tres películas y una cantidad de dinero superior a la que ofreció a los otros dos candidatos todavía en carrera.
En los casos de Josh O’Connor y Jack Lowden, los otros dos intérpretes considerados para ser el siguiente James Bond, la propuesta habría sido por cuatro películas, pero con un acuerdo económico más bajo. Si lo que se reporta es certero, Amazon seguramente espere una respuesta de Robert Pattinson antes de avanzar con cualquiera de las alternativas restantes.
El panorama que se presenta tiene lógica. Después de todo, Robert Pattinson es lo que en Hollywood se conoce como un A-lister; es decir, una estrella de primer nivel. Si bien el actor fue una sensación adolescente de la mano de la saga Crepúsculo, desde 2020 se ha convertido en una figura repetida en producciones de primer nivel. Sus trabajos en Tenet, The Batman, La Odisea y Mickey 17, por solo citar algunos títulos, lo han catapultado como una de las figuras más codiciadas de la actualidad.
Robert Pattinson podría ser el próximo James Bond
Queda claro que Robert Pattinson está transitando el momento más prolífico de su carrera, lo que le da lógica al presunto interés de Amazon de tenerlo como próximo James Bond. No obstante, su contratación también podría ir en contra del plan de tener a un actor más joven y desconocido encarnando a 007 en el cine.
Ese fue uno de los grandes mandatos tras la finalización del ciclo de Daniel Craig. Y si bien Pattinson no es viejo bajo ninguna medida, su edad actual (40) es mayor que la que tenía Craig cuando debutó en 2006 con Casino Royale (38). Además, como ya hemos establecido, está en las antípodas de ser un desconocido.
Más allá de sus cualidades como actor, otro punto a favor para posicionar a Robert Pattinson como el nuevo James Bond es que ya sabe lo que es trabajar con Denis Villeneuve. El intérprete es parte de Dune: Parte tres, que se estrenará el próximo 18 de diciembre.
Todavía no se sabe cuándo se anunciará al nuevo James Bond, sea o no Robert Pattinson. Es un hecho que Villeneuve se pondrá manos a la obra con la próxima película de 007 recién después de terminar con la gira promocional de la tercera entrega de Dune.

articles.title: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock
Amazon Bedrock provides built-in, zero-instrumentation cost attribution that traces every inference call back to the IAM principal that made it. The identity flows along with organizational tags, into AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR 2.0) and AWS Cost Explorer while keeping data inside the AWS security boundary. This post shows you how to use these capabilities to answer three questions that every FinOps and AI Platform leader asks as AI tool adoption scales: What is the real per-user cost? Which teams generate the most spend, and does that spend correlate with the value they deliver? How should next year’s budget scale with headcount and adoption?
The approach works identically regardless of which AI coding or productivity tool makes the call. Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenAI Codex, ChatGPT Work, and OpenCode all invoke Amazon Bedrock through one of two inference endpoints: bedrock-runtime or bedrock-mantle, and Bedrock’s attribution mechanism operates at the endpoint layer, beneath any tool-specific logic. You configure identity propagation once, and every tool that routes inference through Bedrock inherits per-user cost visibility automatically.
By the end of this post, you will have AWS IAM Identity Center configured with your external identity provider for per-user attribution, session tags (team, cost center) flowing into CUR 2.0, Amazon Athena queries and dashboard options for ongoing cost visibility, and a clear understanding of Bedrock-native usage controls to enforce spending limits.
How Amazon Bedrock attribution works
Amazon Bedrock records the IAM identity of every inference caller with no changes required to your API calls. When a user invokes a model through either the bedrock-runtime or bedrock-mantle endpoint, Bedrock captures the caller’s full IAM ARN, including the session name for federated users and publishes it to CUR 2.0 in the line_item_iam_principal column. In billing data, usage is aggregated per principal and per usage type for each export interval: one hour in an hourly export, one day in a daily export. CUR does not contain per-request cost. For per-prompt detail, use model invocation logs or request metadata tagging.
Optionally, you can attach tags to IAM principals or pass session tags during federation to add organizational dimensions. These tags appear in CUR 2.0 with the iamPrincipal/ prefix and in Cost Explorer as filterable dimensions. The mechanism supports four access patterns: IAM users, per-application roles, federated identities, and large language model (LLM) gateways proxying to Bedrock. For a comparison of all four, see Introducing granular cost attribution for Amazon Bedrock. This post follows the federated identity pattern, which is the natural fit for AI coding and productivity tools where each developer or knowledge worker authenticates individually.
Amazon Bedrock offers additional attribution mechanisms beyond IAM principal tracking that organizations can layer depending on their needs (see Appendix A for a comparison). With Application Inference Profiles, you can tag spend by workload on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. With Projects and Workspaces, you can isolate and tag spend on the bedrock-mantle endpoint. Per-request metadata tagging provides per-prompt token-level detail in model invocation logs for workloads that need granularity finer than finer than CUR 2.0’s per-usage-type aggregation per export interval. You can combine these, for example, IAM principal attribution for per-user dollars on your invoice alongside per-request metadata tags for per-prompt detail in logs. The choice depends on your goal (see Track usage and costs in Amazon Bedrock).
The attribution problem
The developer and productivity tools run on each user’s machine and call Amazon Bedrock directly, or through an LLM gateway. Users authenticate by assuming a shared IAM role, so every API call appears as assumed-role/<role>/<session-name> in billing. If every user assumes the role with the same fixed session name, or calls go through a gateway’s own role, CUR aggregates spend to a single principal. With IAM Identity Center, the session name is the user’s sign-in name, so each user gets their own principal. You can further enrich it with session tags (team, cost center, project). These fields flow into CUR 2.0’s line_item_iam_principal column and cost allocation tags with the iamPrincipal/ prefix, making per-user spend queryable alongside the dollars, with zero changes to your Bedrock API calls.
Claude Platform on AWS and Claude for Enterprise route inference through Anthropic-managed infrastructure. For Claude Platform on AWS, usage is visible by workspace and API key in Anthropic’s admin console, and workspace tags flow to AWS billing. For Claude for Enterprise, per-user usage is visible in Anthropic’s admin console and Usage and Cost API. Spend limits are enforced natively by Anthropic.
Prerequisites
Before starting, make sure you have:
- An AWS account with IAM permissions to access Bedrock models you intend to use.
- AWS IAM Identity Center enabled in your management account.
- An external identity provider (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or Ping Identity) with SCIM provisioning capability.
- AWS CLI v2 configured on developer machines.
- AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR 2.0) enabled with IAM principal data and delivered to an S3 bucket.
- Cost allocation tags activated from the management (payer) account.
- An Athena table configured to query CUR 2.0 data (see the GitHub sample to get started).
Step 1: Configure IAM Identity Center with your external IdP
Configure your external identity provider as the identity source in AWS IAM Identity Center. Navigate to IAM Identity Center → Settings → Identity source → Change identity source. Select “External identity provider” and configure SAML 2.0 or SCIM connectivity with your IdP. Enable SCIM provisioning to automatically synchronize users and groups, including organizational attributes like team and department.
Configure attribute mapping for session tags by navigating to Settings → Attributes for access control. Map your IdP’s organizational attributes to session tags that will flow into CUR 2.0. These attributes propagate as session tags (aws:PrincipalTag/Team, aws:PrincipalTag/CostCenter) on every API call the user makes, including every Bedrock invocation through both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints.
Step 2: Create a permission set for Bedrock access
Create a permission set in Identity Center that grants Bedrock invocation access. Each user gets their own session within this permission set. This is the foundation of per-user attribution. The specific IAM actions depend on which Bedrock endpoint the tool calls.
Tools that call the bedrock-mantle endpoint (such as Codex and ChatGPT Work) require bedrock-mantle:CreateInference and related actions scoped to a Project resource. Tools that call the bedrock-runtime endpoint (such as Claude Code and Claude Desktop) require bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream scoped to the relevant foundation model or inference profile ARNs. You can combine both in a single permission set if your organization uses tools across both endpoints.
Note: These resource patterns are a starting point. Narrow them to the specific inference profiles and Projects that you approve. Assign this permission set to the relevant groups synchronized from your IdP. Policy changes are instant and universal, audit is centralized through AWS CloudTrail with each user’s identity, and users do not receive long-lived AWS credentials.
Step 3: Configure user workstations
Users configure their AWS CLI profile once, no custom scripts, credential helpers, or browser automation required. The following ~/.aws/config entry establishes the SSO session:
Users authenticate by running aws sso login --profile bedrock, which opens the browser, authenticates through the IdP, and caches credentials locally. The AWS CLI and SDKs refresh the access token automatically until the IAM Identity Center session ends (8 hours by default). The core trade-off in configuring session duration is between security posture and operational convenience.
Step 4: Point tools at Amazon Bedrock
Each AI tool needs only a standard configuration change to route inference through Bedrock. Because Bedrock attribution operates at the endpoint layer, no tool-specific instrumentation is required. The tool authenticates using the AWS credential chain established in Step 3, and Bedrock captures the caller identity automatically.
Claude Desktop reads third-party inference settings from OS-native managed preferences (/Library/Managed Preferences/com.anthropic.claudefordesktop.plist on macOS, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude on Windows). Author the configuration once in the in-app window (Developer → Configure Third-Party Inference) and choose Export to produce a .mobileconfig or .reg for your mobile device management (MDM) system. For per-user attribution, use in-app AWS sign-in, each user authenticates against IAM Identity Center inside the application, with no AWS CLI on the device:
Configuration is read at launch. Users must quit and reopen the application. If developers already run AWS CLI v2, set inferenceBedrockProfile instead and the app runs aws sso login for them.
Claude Code CLI reads the standard AWS SDK credential chain, including SSO profiles. If AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK is set, Claude Code authenticates with that key and does not use the credential chain, so calls are attributed to the IAM user behind the key. Disable it when you want per-user SSO attribution.
Set awsAuthRefresh in the settings file to automatically re-authenticate when credentials expire:
Pin model versions before fleet rollout so a new release doesn’t change what users invoke:
Codex and ChatGPT Work read ~/.codex/config.toml. Both the desktop app and CLI consume the same configuration layers. For the bedrock-mantle endpoint:
For the bedrock-runtime endpoint, use inference profile IDs:
Set AWS_PROFILE in the environment for both endpoints. For the desktop app, place environment variables in ~/.codex/.env since desktop applications may not inherit shell environment variables. If AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK is set, Codex uses it before the SSO profile and calls are attributed to the IAM user behind that API key. Unset it when you want per-user SSO attribution.
Step 5: Enable cost attribution in CUR 2.0
From the AWS Billing Console (Billing → Data Exports → Create export), configure delivery to S3 in Parquet format with hourly or daily granularity. Select “Include caller identity (IAM principal) allocation data” to populate the line_item_iam_principal column. Bedrock’s IAM principal cost tracking works for both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints.
Creating the export in the management account captures all accounts’ Bedrock usage. If you created a CUR 2.0 data export before IAM principal attribution launched, you must create a new export with the caller identity option selected.
Activate cost allocation tags after users have signed in and made at least one Bedrock call. Tags appear in Billing only after the principal has made a call. In the management account, open Billing → Cost allocation tags, filter by type IAM principal, and activate Team and CostCenter:
Allow up to 24 hours for tags to appear and up to 48 hours to see them in CUR 2.0 and Cost Explorer. Activation is not retroactive. Bedrock meters and bills input, output, cache-read, and cache-write tokens separately. A single hour of activity under one IAM principal typically produces four CUR rows.
Step 6: Query cost data with Amazon Athena
Once CUR 2.0 is delivered to S3 and an Athena table is configured, query usage and cost at your desired granularity. The following query extracts per-user cost:
For daily spend trend per cost center:
Athena charges by data scanned. Columnar Parquet and the billing_period filter keep queries inexpensive.
Step 7: Visualization
AWS Cost Explorer requires zero setup. Group by tags once they are activated. AWS Quick Sight connects to Athena for interactive dashboards with anomaly detection that alerts on unexpected spend spikes. You can integrate with the CUDOS dashboard, an open-source Cloud Intelligence Dashboards (CID) framework that provides detailed cost insights. Grafana with the Athena plugin renders CUR data as time series alongside existing infrastructure metrics.
Implementing per-user usage controls
Once per-user cost visibility is established through IAM principal attribution in CUR 2.0, organizations need enforcement mechanisms to help prevent uncontrolled accumulation. Numerous approaches exist today, each trading enforcement latency against operational complexity.
AWS Budgets with budget actions is the lightest option requiring no custom infrastructure. Set a budget threshold filtered by IAM principal tags, and attach an action (such as applying a deny policy) that triggers when the threshold is breached. The trade-off: AWS Budgets updates up to three times a day, and Bedrock charges can take up to 24 hours to appear in billing data, so a high-velocity user can overshoot by up to a day before enforcement takes effect.
Amazon CloudWatch alarms and AWS Lambda offer near-real-time enforcement using Bedrock’s native CloudWatch metrics (InputTokenCount, OutputTokenCount, Invocations) filtered by model ID or inference profile. Enforcement latency drops to 1–5 minutes. To get user-level granularity with this approach, use Application Inference Profiles or per-user roles.
Amazon DynamoDB-based quota tracking enforces limits at the authentication layer. A Lambda function increments per-user token counters in DynamoDB and withholds credentials once a limit is exceeded. Enforcement takes effect at the next credential refresh, not on individual API calls, but removes the billing-data lag inherent in budget-based approaches.
LLM gateway proxy delivers per-invocation blocking across Bedrock models and SDK workloads, at the cost of highest operational complexity and added latency on every request. See Multi-Provider Generative AI Gateway.
Organizations typically layer these options: CUR 2.0 for reporting, a gateway or DynamoDB-based enforcement for real-time control, and AWS Budgets as a backstop. For the full reference, see How to limit usage and cost on Amazon Bedrock.
Conclusion
Amazon Bedrock’s IAM principal attribution gives you per-user cost tracking for every AI developer and productivity tool that routes inference through Bedrock, with no custom credential scripts, per-user IAM roles, or additional infrastructure. Users authenticate with aws sso login, the same flow they use for other AWS access, and every Bedrock invocation automatically carries their identity into billing data.
Each component can be adopted incrementally. Start by connecting your IdP to Identity Center and assigning a Bedrock permission set to get session-level attribution in CloudTrail immediately. Activate cost allocation tags to surface that data in CUR 2.0. Add Athena queries and dashboards as reporting requirements grow. Layer usage controls, from AWS Budgets to real-time gateway enforcement, based on your organization’s tolerance for enforcement latency.
Regardless of which AI tools your organization adopts today or adds tomorrow, the attribution and control mechanisms described here operate at the Bedrock platform layer. Configure once, and every tool that calls Bedrock inherits the governance.

articles.title: The context problem: It's what's really breaking AI agents at scale
articles.text:
The context problem: It’s what’s really breaking AI agents at scale
AI models are getting smarter, tokens are getting cheaper, and agents are improving. But the context gap sits between the modern enterprise and agentic nirvana, keeping many companies from realizing the ROI they hoped for from their AI investments.
As with most problems we’ve seen in the AI era, tech companies are rushing to fill the gap. The New Stack recently spoke with Sri Desikan, an Elastic executive focused on search, to learn more about the AI context gap and how his company is tackling the challenge.
The context gap is easy to understand. As Desikan explains, “frontier models are getting better and better and better,” but if you don’t feed them proper context, “all that money you’re spending on tokens is going to waste.” Getting your agents the information they need, when they need it, quickly, is the ticket to moving from impressive demos to durable automation.
The enterprise is feeling the pinch. AI models can reach out to MCP servers to request information, but merely connecting a company’s corpus to a bridge isn’t enough. You can’t just “shove all this data into [a model’s] context window,” Desikan argues. Why? Because doing so is both computationally expensive (lots of tokens!) and slow.
So what do we need to do? Pre-conform corporate data into an AI index that knows where data is stored and how it relates to other data. Desikan described the process as creating a “container which stores metadata about everything in your enterprise.” Under this formulation, AI agents can access correct, useful information faster and with lower token burn (in some examples, sharply lower).
There’s another wrinkle worth considering. If you follow Elastic’s guidance and pre-compute your AI context (the index), you can “make sure that stale information” isn’t included, letting companies “know how the LLM is going to think.”
Of course, using AI to pre-prepare data for use by AI agents raises all sorts of privacy and agentic autonomy questions, which I got into with Desikan. Hit play if you want to go deeper on those issues. But looking at the conversation as a whole, I was encouraged by how well-thought-out industry approaches to novel problems seem; nothing that bedevils us today necessarily has to bother us next quarter.

articles.title: Who will succeed Jensen Huang? The race to find Nvidia's next chief begins
articles.text:
Who will succeed Jensen Huang? The race to find Nvidia's next chief begins
Jensen Huang’s departure ends a 33-year leadership era at Nvidia, triggering a search for his successor. Names including Lisa Su, Rene Haas and Tim Cook have entered the conversation, with Trump’s endorsement of Cook adding an unexpected twist.
Nvidia has begun its search for a permanent chief executive officer after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned on November 12, ending a 33-year run at the held. The company board has said it would consider candidates from inside and outside the company.
Meanwhile, the chief financial officer Colette Kress has been appointed the interim CEO.
The leadership crisis follows a week of mounting controversy at the chipmaking company, which is a key player in the global AI race. Nvidia faced scrutiny over reports of a possible foreign intelligence operation targeting Huang.
On November 8, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a message to employees. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he wrote.
The statement followed reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, a company scrutinised by US authorities over suspected assistance to Chinese customers seeking advanced Nvidia chips subject to export restrictions.
The controversy deepened with reports of another relationship involving Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare.
On November 12, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Huang also had an intimate relationship with another female Nvidia employee, whose identity it did not disclose.
Nvidia’s board had earlier launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted in a foreign intelligence operation. It said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised."
The independent directors subsequently appointed former acting US attorney Joon H. Kim and law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the inquiry. No findings have been published.
US Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department had reached no conclusion on whether Alice Huang was a spy, while confirming that the FBI was examining the reports.
These developments come amid the wider backdrop of a tightening contest over access to advanced AI chips.
US export controls restrict the sale of certain high-end Nvidia processors to China. Reuters reported on November 12 that Chinese AI firms were seeking to reserve Nvidia-powered computing capacity at overseas data centres, partly out of concern that Washington could tighten restrictions on remote access.
A proposed US Remote Access Security Act, which would give the Commerce Department authority over cloud-based access to restricted technology, has passed the House of Representatives but it still requires Senate approval.
The search for a successor
Meanwhile, Nvidia’s board has appointed longtime director Harvey C. Jones as its first chair and formally opened the search for a successor. The company has not announced a shortlist.
Reuters identified CFO Colette Kress and Ian Buck, a senior engineering executive who joined the company in 2004 and helped develop CUDA (Compute Unified Device Architecture), as prominent internal candidates being discussed by analysts and investors.
External names floated by media outlets include Arm chief executive Rene Haas, who is also a former Nvidia executive; and AMD chief Lisa Su. Axios mentioned former Intel chief Pat Gelsinger, Google Cloud head Thomas Kurian, and Apple executive chairman Tim Cook in a broader list of potential names.
None has been announced by Nvidia as a candidate, and there is no publicly confirmed official shortlist.
US President Donald Trump added a political twist to the proceedings by publicly suggesting Cook for the position. He posted a statement, “There is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!”
Beyond the leadership change
The succession race matters because Nvidia is seen as more than a company selling graphics processors.
Founded in 1993, the company initially focused on gaming graphics before expanding into accelerated computing, which uses specialised processors to handle large numbers of calculations simultaneously. Its CUDA software, data-centre systems, and networking technology now form a broad platform for training and running AI models.
The next CEO needs to maintain Nvidia's technological advantage while managing customers, regulators, and the company’s increasingly strategic role in US-China technology policy.
Competition is also intensifying. On November 12, AMD updated its Instinct MI400 accelerator range, announced the MI450X GPU, and shared new performance results for its MI455X GPU on its Helios rack-scale system. The announcements underline company's efforts to challenge Nvidia in AI data centres.
Nvidia, meanwhile, announced a partnership with South Korea’s Rebellions and SK Telecom to connect Korean-designed AI processors with its infrastructure for sovereign AI projects. The planned Rebellions R200 systems are expected to be ready in 2028.
Kress has sought to reassure customers and investors about continuity. In her statement following the appointment, she said, “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead.”
Nvidia’s third-quarter fiscal 2027 results are scheduled for November 17, with Kress due to provide written financial commentary ahead of the investor call.
That will offer an early opportunity to assess operational continuity under the interim leadership. The bigger challenge, however, lies with the board.
Jensen Huang has been central to Nvidia's identity, strategy and influence for more than three decades. So his replacement has to be someone capable of managing not just a major semiconductor business but also an entire technology ecosystem.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Microsoft outage hits Equity, StanChart and Stanbic in Kenya
articles.text:
Kenyan banks turned to WhatsApp and call centres on Friday after a global Microsoft outage cut off their email, forcing several of the country’s biggest lenders to reroute customer queries.
Equity Bank and UBA Kenya asked customers to call or use WhatsApp. Stanbic Bank Kenya, part of South Africa’s Standard Bank Group, directed customers to its Voice Branch call centre or their relationship managers. Standard Chartered Bank Kenya told customers by text that its email service was unavailable.
Loop, NCBA Group’s digital bank, went further, saying both its email and in-app support channels were down and directing customers to phone lines and social media. None of the notices mentioned problems with payments.
Insurers also felt the strain, as Old Mutual Kenya apologised to customers after losing access to email. APA Insurance lost email as well as Microsoft’s SharePoint and OneDrive, according to an email seen by TechCabal.
The disruption shows how heavily Kenya’s financial industry relies on a single foreign cloud provider for the basic tools of daily operations, even as lenders move almost all customer business to digital channels.
Microsoft first said it was investigating mailbox problems shortly before 1 PM New York time on Thursday. That was 9 PM in Nairobi, the hour when Old Mutual’s Kenyan unit says its email went down.
Microsoft blamed a large number of servers becoming unexpectedly unavailable, which pushed extra load onto the rest of its infrastructure, and said it saw no sign of a cyberattack.
The failure spread to 74 countries and territories in about an hour, according to Downdetector. By Friday morning, Microsoft said service capacity had not yet returned to normal levels. It has given no estimate for full recovery.
UBA Kenya named Microsoft Outlook as the cause and offered customers phone lines, a WhatsApp number and their relationship managers.
“We wish to inform you that due to a global service disruption affecting Microsoft Outlook, our email services are temporarily unavailable. We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause,” UBA Kenya told its customers in a text on Friday.
Equity cited “a global service disruption” without naming Microsoft and asked customers to call or message it on WhatsApp. In a text to customers, Standard Chartered said only that its email was unavailable. None of the notices mentioned payment or mobile banking issues.
The exposure reaches well beyond Kenya. Equity serves 23.3 million customers and processes 89.7% of transactions on digital platforms. London-based Standard Chartered owns 73.89% of its Kenyan unit. Nigeria’s UBA operates in 20 African countries as well as in the US, the UK, France, and the United Arab Emirates.
Companies outside finance were hit too. Securex Agencies, a Nairobi-based security company founded in 1970, told clients to use its phone line and social media pages for “urgent security-related matters”. A travel agency told its clients it could not access its email due to the outage.
Friday’s failure is the latest in a run of Microsoft 365 disruptions this year. Outages occurred in January and July, and a late-August incident locked thousands of users worldwide out of their mailboxes.
Kenya has few local alternatives because a $1 billion Microsoft and G42 data centre, meant to host an Azure cloud region for East Africa, stalled when the government refused the payment guarantees the companies sought.
Kenyan officials have since said the project remains on track. East Africa’s live data-centre load stood at about 30 megawatts in 2025, according to an industry estimate.
A local data centre would not necessarily have shielded Kenyan users, because Microsoft runs its email and file services on shared global infrastructure. But the outage showed how few fallback options Kenyan companies have when that infrastructure breaks.

articles.title: Pane da Microsoft provoca suspensão de prazos na Justiça brasileira
articles.text:
A instabilidade global nos serviços da Microsoft provocou impactos também no funcionamento do Judiciário brasileiro. Nesta sexta-feira (13), o ministro Edson Fachin, presidente do Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ), determinou a suspensão dos prazos processuais em todo o país nos dias 12 e 13 de novembro.
A decisão atende a pedido apresentado pelo Conselho Federal da Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil (OAB), que apontou falhas graves nos serviços da Microsoft iniciadas na quinta-feira (12). A medida também se aplica aos processos em tramitação no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).
Segundo a OAB, a instabilidade atingiu o Microsoft 365 e comprometeu ferramentas de comunicação e trabalho utilizadas por órgãos do Poder Judiciário em diferentes partes do país. Com a determinação, a contagem dos prazos processuais será retomada oficialmente na próxima segunda-feira (16).
Juízes poderão analisar casos específicos
A portaria assinada por Fachin também prevê a possibilidade de análise individual de situações que tenham sido afetadas pelas falhas tecnológicas, mas que não estejam restritas ao intervalo de 12 e 13 de novembro.
Nesses casos, os juízes e relatores poderão avaliar os pedidos mediante comprovação do impacto causado pela instabilidade, respeitando a legislação processual vigente.
Leia mais:
- Apagão da Microsoft: veja alternativas ao Office, Teams e Outlook
- Qual a última vez que você usou um fax? No apagão da Microsoft, empresas voltaram ao passado
- Apagões digitais expõem a dependência global de uma infraestrutura concentrada em poucas empresas
Pane afetou ferramentas do STF e tribunais estaduais
- A instabilidade também atingiu ferramentas utilizadas diretamente pelo Supremo. Na tarde desta sexta-feira (13), o STF confirmou problemas no e-mail institucional e no Microsoft Teams. Apesar disso, informou que os demais sistemas continuavam funcionando normalmente, sem prejuízo às atividades jurisdicionais, incluindo os julgamentos realizados no Plenário Virtual;
- O problema também provocou dificuldades para advogados acessarem o sistema de peticionamento do Supremo. Segundo a Corte, uma das possibilidades é que os profissionais não conseguissem receber por e-mail o código necessário para entrar na plataforma;
- Nos ofícios enviados ao STF e ao CNJ, a OAB também mencionou alertas dos tribunais de Justiça de Santa Catarina e de São Paulo sobre possíveis prejuízos ao atendimento e ao funcionamento de ferramentas institucionais;
- O presidente da entidade, José Alberto Simonetti, afirmou que o pedido buscava “prevenir prejuízos às partes, preservar a segurança jurídica e assegurar a regularidade da prestação jurisdicional diante de uma ocorrência extraordinária, de abrangência nacional”;
- A Ordem também alertou que a interrupção dos serviços poderia comprometer despachos virtuais, agendamentos de audiências, comunicação com unidades judiciárias e a organização do trabalho de magistrados e servidores, especialmente no regime de teletrabalho.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

At this year’s electronica, there was a clear emphasis on taking a system- and platform-level approach to enabling physical AI and edge AI. All the key chipmakers were talking about hardware-software platforms that help developers quickly build drones, physical AI and humanoid robotics systems, and use agentic AI to deliver edge AI systems.
We hear firsthand from our editors on the ground at electronica 2026 in Munich, Germany, in these two short videos.
Embedded and edge AI: Agentic tools, NPUs everywhere, and robot hands
Agentic AI is changing embedded development tool flows. Microcontroller makers, along with a growing number of smaller startups, are building AI agents for code generation and other design tasks. EE Times’ Sally Ward-Foxton notes that almost every microcontroller now has a dedicated NPU, and that companies such as Nordic Semiconductor want to be solution providers, not just silicon suppliers. We also talk about Europe’s strength in MCU design, why chipmakers are moving into software and subsystems, and the many robotic hand designs on show.
Power electronics: The AI data center dominates
Aaliya Shaukat, editor-in-chief of PowerElectronicsNews.com, talks about the show’s power side, which centered on the AI data center. Topics include solid-state circuit breakers and transformers, vertical power delivery, and recent deals such as Analog Devices’ acquisition of Empower Semiconductor. We also look at how wide-bandgap supply is being squeezed by data center demand, with Wolfspeed moving into GaN and Infineon scaling GaN on 300-mm wafers. Looking ahead, she expects data centers to remain the top story, with physical AI and humanoid robotics coming next.
Nitin Dahad is executive editor of EE Times. An electronic engineering graduate from City University, he’s been an engineer, journalist and entrepreneur. He was part of ARC International’s startup team and took it public, and he co-founded a publication called The Chilli in the early 2000s. Nitin has also worked with National Semiconductor, GEC Plessey Semiconductors, Dialog Semiconductor, Marconi Instruments, Coresonic, Center for Integrated Photonics, IDENT Technology and Jennic. Nitin also held a role with government promoting U.K. technology globally in the U.S., Brazil, Middle East and Africa, and India.

articles.title: Test Huawei WiFi Mesh X3 Pro : ce routeur Wi-Fi 7 est le plus beau que j’aie installé chez moi — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les routeurs se cachent d’habitude derrière la TV ou dans un placard, avec leurs antennes en éventail et leurs diodes clignotantes. Huawei prend le problème à l’envers avec le WiFi Mesh X3 Pro : il a conçu un objet de décoration qui fait aussi routeur. Le pack comprend un routeur principal et un petit répéteur, censés couvrir ensemble jusqu’à 120 m².
Pour ce test, je me suis concentré sur le routeur principal, branché derrière ma Freebox Ultra.
Fiche technique du Huawei WiFi Mesh X3 Pro
| Modèle | Huawei WiFi Mesh X3 Pro (routeur principal et répéteur) | 
| Norme | Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be), 2 × 2 MIMO, MLO, 4K-QAM | 
| Bandes | 2,4 GHz et 5 GHz, pas de 6 GHz | 
| Débits théoriques | 2,4 GHz : 688 Mbit/s 5 GHz : 2 882 Mbit/s soit 3 570 Mbit/s cumulés | 
| Antennes | 2 antennes en 2,4 GHz et 4 en 5 GHz, par appareil | 
| Ports du routeur | 2 × 2,5 Gbit/s WAN/LAN à détection automatique | 
| Ports du répéteur | 1 × 1 Gbit/s | 
| Mémoire | 512 Mo de RAM, 128 Mo de stockage | 
| Couverture annoncée | Jusqu’à 120 m² avec le répéteur | 
| Sécurité | WPA2 et WPA3, pare-feu, HomeSec, contrôle parental | 
| Application | Huawei AI Life (iOS, Android, HarmonyOS) | 
| Alimentation | Adaptateur 12 V, 24 W maximum par appareil | 
| Dimensions et poids | Routeur : 250,9 mm de haut, 123,2 mm de diamètre, 777 g Répéteur : 73,5 mm de haut, 114,8 mm de diamètre, 416 g | 
| Firmware testé | 4.3.0.6 (V71SP01C00) | 
| Prix | 249,99 € (routeur et répéteur) | 
Design : une montagne dorée dans le salon
Je n’ai jamais eu envie de montrer un routeur avant celui-là. Le X3 Pro prend la forme d’un grand cylindre de 25 cm de haut, posé sur un socle noir. À l’intérieur de la coque transparente se dresse une petite montagne aux reliefs dorés, rétroéclairée. Allumée le soir, elle ressemble à un sommet enneigé au coucher du soleil, ce que Huawei revendique d’ailleurs dans sa communication.
La conception est remarquable. Rien ne trahit la fonction de l’objet : pas d’antenne visible, pas de rangée de diodes, pas de grille d’aération apparente sur la face avant. Huawei a intégré des antennes en maillage métallique transparent dans la coque, pour qu’elles se fondent dans le décor. Je l’ai installé dans mon salon et c’est l’objet que les visiteurs remarquent en premier : pour une fois, c’est un compliment pour un routeur.
Le répéteur, beaucoup plus petit, reprend le même esprit dans un format bas et rond de 11,5 cm de diamètre. Il peut lui aussi servir de veilleuse.
Un éclairage réglable dans l’application
L’éclairage n’est pas un simple gadget allumé en permanence. Dans l’application AI Life, une rubrique « Effets d’éclairage » permet de choisir entre le motif « Montagne dorée », qui fait évoluer la lumière au fil de la journée, et un mode personnalisé. Ce dernier règle la luminosité et la température de couleur, d’un blanc chaud très orangé (2 000 K) à des teintes plus froides. On peut aussi programmer l’allumage et l’extinction, par exemple pour que la montagne s’éteigne la nuit, ou couper complètement la lumière.
Une consommation raisonnable
Huawei annonce un double système de ventilation, avec des ventilateurs en forme d’aileron de requin. Je n’ai pas mesuré le niveau sonore. La consommation, en revanche, reste contenue : j’ai relevé environ 8 W pour l’ensemble formé par le routeur et le répéteur, et jamais plus de 15 W en pleine charge. C’est bien moins que la limite de 24 W par appareil inscrite sur la fiche technique. Chaque élément utilise son propre adaptateur secteur.
Connectique : deux ports, c’est peu
Le routeur principal n’a que deux ports Ethernet. Ils fonctionnent à 2,5 Gbit/s, ce qui est appréciable : ils suffisent pour profiter d’une fibre à 2 Gbit/s ou relier un NAS récent. Chacun détecte seul s’il est branché à la box ou à un appareil local.
Dans la pratique, l’un des deux sert à relier la box. Il ne reste donc qu’un seul port pour brancher un ordinateur fixe, une console ou un NAS. Pour plusieurs appareils filaires, il faudra ajouter un switch, ce qui gâche un peu l’effet design du salon. Le répéteur propose un port à 1 Gbit/s supplémentaire, pratique pour une télévision ou une console dans une autre pièce. Il n’y a pas de port USB.
Un Wi-Fi 7 sans bande 6 GHz
Le X3 Pro porte l’étiquette Wi-Fi 7, mais il faut regarder de près ce qu’elle recouvre. Le routeur fonctionne uniquement en 2,4 GHz et en 5 GHz. Il lui manque la bande 6 GHz, la plus rapide et la moins encombrée, qui permet d’utiliser les canaux très larges de 320 MHz, la principale source de débit du Wi-Fi 7.
Huawei conserve plusieurs nouveautés de la norme. Le MLO permet à un appareil compatible de combiner les bandes 2,4 et 5 GHz pour gagner en débit ou en stabilité. La modulation 4K-QAM transporte 20 % de données en plus que la génération précédente, à condition d’avoir un excellent signal. Le tout repose sur deux flux spatiaux par bande, ce qui donne un maximum théorique de 2 882 Mbit/s en 5 GHz et 3 570 Mbit/s en cumulant les deux bandes.
Du 10 au 30 novembre, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1500 passe à 1 399 € au lieu de 1 899 €, support de lavage offert ! Sans fil, navigation LiDAR 360°, évitement précis des obstacles, tonte des bordures… La tonte sans effort, même pour les jardins les plus complexes.
C’est largement suffisant pour une fibre à 1 ou 2 Gbit/s et pour la plupart des usages. Mais ceux qui veulent tirer le maximum d’un smartphone ou d’un PC Wi-Fi 7 récent devront se tourner vers un routeur tri-bande. Notre guide des produits compatibles Wi-Fi 7 détaille ce qu’il faut regarder sur la fiche technique.
Installation et réglages du X3 Pro
L’installation se fait au choix dans l’application Huawei AI Life ou dans un navigateur. J’ai testé le parcours web : le routeur détecte le type de connexion (ici en DHCP, derrière la Freebox), puis demande un nom et un mot de passe Wi-Fi ainsi qu’un mot de passe d’administration. Le tout prend quelques minutes.
Quelques détails trahissent un manque de finition. Dès l’accueil, Huawei prévient qu’il collecte des informations sur l’appareil et le réseau. La page de fin affiche une clé de traduction brute, « guide.finish.lighttip », à la place d’un vrai texte, et l’outil de diagnostic laisse apparaître un code «   » dans un titre. L’interface web est aussi servie en HTTP, et Safari la signale comme « Non sécurisée ».
Des modes Internet complets pour remplacer une box
Le X3 Pro peut se connecter à Internet en DHCP, derrière une box, en PPPoE pour se brancher directement sur certaines fibres, en IP statique, ou servir de répéteur d’un autre réseau Wi-Fi. Un réglage VLAN et un clonage d’adresse MAC sont aussi proposés, deux options parfois nécessaires pour remplacer la box d’un opérateur. Je ne les ai pas essayées avec un abonnement réel.
Des réglages avancés limités
Au-delà de ces bases, le X3 Pro se montre moins généreux que la concurrence en réglages avancés. L’application va à l’essentiel : appareils connectés, pare-feu, éclairage, mises à jour, redémarrage et paramètres du routeur. On trouve un contrôle parental, qui limite le temps d’écran et bloque certains sites, la protection HomeSec contre les attaques par force brute sur le Wi-Fi, et un mode booster de jeu, dont je n’ai pas mesuré l’effet sur la latence.
Ceux qui aiment régler finement leur réseau resteront sur leur faim. Le routeur s’adresse clairement à un public qui veut un Wi-Fi qui marche sans y penser.
Un diagnostic visuel
L’outil de diagnostic intelligent est plus soigné. Il affiche un plan du logement à modifier, les appareils connectés avec la qualité de leur connexion, de leur débit et de leur signal, et une vue de l’occupation des canaux en 2,4 GHz. Une carte de chaleur de la couverture Wi-Fi peut être générée, mais je ne l’ai pas lancée : les zones vertes visibles sur les captures sont une illustration de l’application, pas un relevé de mon logement.
Mesh+ : un répéteur pour les grandes surfaces
Le pack comprend un répéteur qui étend le réseau du routeur principal. Huawei appelle Mesh+ ce réseau unifié : un seul nom de Wi-Fi pour toute la maison, et des appareils qui passent automatiquement d’une borne à l’autre en se déplaçant. Le constructeur annonce une couverture jusqu’à 120 m² pour l’ensemble.
Je n’ai pas mesuré les performances du répéteur ni la qualité de ce basculement. Les résultats ci-dessous concernent le routeur principal seul. Ils donnent une idée de ce que l’on obtient sans le répéteur, y compris à l’étage, là où il serait justement le plus utile.
J’ai néanmoins testé le répéteur. L’installation est très simple. En gros, vous branchez le X3 Pro sur le secteur. Vous reliez l’un de ses ports Ethernet au port LAN de votre box avec le câble fourni. À ce moment-là, vous pouvez ouvrir l’application Roaui AI Life ou directement l’adresse de configuration Internet indiquée sous l’appareil, et vous suivez l’assistant. Pour brancher le répéteur, c’est encore plus simple. Vous le branchez directement et simplement sur une prise électrique dans l’autre pièce, ou à l’étage en dessous ou au-dessus. Il se connecte automatiquement au routeur X3 Pro en Wi-Fi. Il n’y a aucun câble ni configuration manuelle nécessaire. Ensuite, vous pouvez le déplacer dans la maison. Il conservera sa configuration et rejoindra automatiquement le réseau Mesh.
Ce dernier possède également un port Ethernet gigabit. Vous pouvez donc le brancher à une prise murale pour créer un second point d’accès filaire, ou le laisser en relais sans fil. L’autre possibilité, c’est d’utiliser un adaptateur CPL Ethernet entre la prise électrique et le port RJ45 du répéteur. Ce modèle prend en charge le CPL jusqu’à 1 Gb, mais évidemment, les performances réelles dépendent fortement de l’état du circuit électrique de votre maison. Du côté du relais sans fil, il n’a pas de backhaul Wi-Fi dédié, ce qui signifie que le lien avec le routeur partage la bande avec les appareils clients.
Performances : du gigabit en Wi-Fi, mais pas plus
Ma méthode de test
J’ai mesuré le débit Internet réel avec le logiciel Ookla, depuis un PC portable Asus Zenbook A16, vers le même serveur à chaque fois. Le Zenbook est équipé d’une puce Wi-Fi 7, la Qualcomm FastConnect C7700. Je l’ai placé à environ un mètre du routeur, puis derrière un mur, puis à l’étage inférieur, avec un seul test par position.
Ces mesures passent par la Freebox Ultra et Internet. Elles reflètent ce que vous obtiendrez en navigation et en téléchargement, mais pas le débit maximal du Wi-Fi seul entre deux appareils de la maison.
Un détail compte pour lire les résultats : le Zenbook s’est connecté en Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) et non en Wi-Fi 7, en 5 GHz près du routeur et derrière le mur, puis en 2,4 GHz à l’étage. Le réseau était protégé en WPA2. Le Wi-Fi 7 réclame en principe le WPA3, ce qui pourrait expliquer ce repli.
1,5 Gbit/s à côté du routeur
À un mètre du routeur, le Zenbook atteint 1 521 Mbit/s en téléchargement et 927 Mbit/s en envoi. Windows indique un lien négocié à 2 402 Mbit/s, avec un signal excellent. Derrière un mur, le débit reste au-dessus du gigabit : 1 188 Mbit/s en téléchargement et 507 Mbit/s en envoi.
À l’étage inférieur, le PC bascule automatiquement sur la bande 2,4 GHz, plus lente mais qui traverse mieux les planchers. Le débit tombe à 187 Mbit/s en téléchargement et 71 Mbit/s en envoi. La connexion reste utilisable pour la navigation et la vidéo en streaming, mais on est loin des performances du rez-de-chaussée. C’est typiquement la situation où le répéteur du pack prend tout son sens.
Un smartphone Wi-Fi 7 à plus de 1,5 Gbit/s
J’ai aussi connecté un Xiaomi 18 Pro à un mètre du routeur. Le smartphone, lui, s’est bien connecté en Wi-Fi 7, avec un lien négocié à 2 882 Mbit/s, le maximum du routeur en 5 GHz. Le test nPerf affiche 1 570 Mbit/s en réception, 794 Mbit/s en envoi et 18 ms de latence. Un résultat proche de celui du PC, mesuré avec un autre outil.
Une latence qui grimpe sous la charge
Au repos, le temps de réponse vers le serveur Internet reste bas : 13 ms à un mètre, 14 ms derrière le mur et 16 ms à l’étage. Ces valeurs incluent tout le trajet jusqu’au serveur, pas seulement le Wi-Fi.
La situation se dégrade pendant les transferts. Ookla mesure aussi la latence pendant le téléchargement et l’envoi, ce qui montre comment le réseau réagit quand il est sollicité. Près du routeur, elle monte à 33 ms en téléchargement, mais à 112 ms pendant l’envoi. Derrière le mur, on passe à 112 et 138 ms. À l’étage, l’envoi la fait grimper à 566 ms. En pratique, une visioconférence ou une partie en ligne peut ramer si quelqu’un envoie de gros fichiers en même temps.
Ces mesures portent sur tout le trajet, box et serveur compris, et une seule série a été réalisée par position. Je ne peux donc pas attribuer ces pics au seul routeur. J’imagine qu’il faut activer le mode booster, qui se nomme « Jeu Booster » dans les options, pour améliorer la latence.
Prix et disponibilité du Huawei WiFi Mesh X3 Pro
Le Huawei WiFi Mesh X3 Pro est disponible en France depuis février 2026, au prix conseillé de 249,99 euros pour le pack comprenant le routeur et son répéteur.
À ce tarif, on trouve des systèmes Mesh Wi-Fi 7 tri-bande, avec la bande 6 GHz et davantage de ports. Le X3 Pro se paie surtout pour son design. Pour comparer avec d’autres modèles, notre sélection de routeurs, cartes et box Wi-Fi 7 fait le point sur l’offre actuelle.

articles.title: Jumpstarter platform helps SA entrepreneurs raise seed capital from their communities - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African civic-fintech Jumpstarter Crowdfunding is helping entrepreneurs, creatives and social impact organisations raise seed funding directly from their communities through a reward-based, all-or-nothing crowdfunding model.
Founded in 2012 and operating as a registered non-profit company (NPC), Jumpstarter allows project creators to run campaigns of between one and 60 days, with funds only released if 100 per cent of the target is reached. If a campaign falls short, pledges are returned to backers and the creator pays no platform fees. Backers receive non-financial rewards such as pre-ordered products, experiences or project perks, rather than equity or debt.
“South Africa has over 2.5 million micro, small and medium enterprises, and the vast majority of them face an early-stage funding gap estimated at between ZAR80 billion (US$4.8 billion) and ZAR100 billion (US$6 billion),” co-founder and chief operations officer Derek Whitehead told Disrupt Africa.
“Commercial banks demand collateral and historical balance sheets that grassroots innovators simply don’t have, while venture capital is concentrated in late-stage or hyper-scalable tech. Global platforms like Kickstarter and Indiegogo, meanwhile, lack native rand payment rails and add foreign exchange friction.”
Jumpstarter is led by Whitehead alongside co-founder and director Yaseen Kriel and director Zaid Kriel, supported by a network of advisers, digital marketing contributors and technology partners. The platform runs on Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, is managed via Salesforce CRM, and pairs campaigns with digital marketing support funded through a US$10,000-per-month Google Ad Grant.
That marketing support is central to how the startup differentiates itself from local rivals such as Thundafund, BackaBuddy and Uprise Africa.
“Unlike platforms that function purely as passive software directories, Jumpstarter acts as an active launchpad,” Whitehead said. “Our all-or-nothing model protects backer capital, our non-profit charter lets us charge lower fees, and we actively subsidise creator outreach through our Google Ad Grant.”
The model appears to be gaining traction. Jumpstarter has facilitated more than ZAR1.34 million (US$80,000) in community-backed capital across over 36 successfully funded campaigns, spanning food and beverage, creative arts, software, publishing, green-tech and community development. Notable campaigns include helping Cape Town’s Charly’s Bakery survive lockdown disruptions and backing the commercial launch of the Pirate Masters card game.
“Campaigns that engage our structured preparation and ad-subsidisation workflows regularly achieve between 100 and 108 per cent of their targets,” Whitehead said.
Jumpstarter charges a seven per cent fee on successful for-profit campaigns and five per cent for registered NPOs and schools, with third-party payment gateways PayGate and SnapScan deducting additional processing fees. As a non-profit, all surplus revenue is reinvested into infrastructure, campaign support tools and community pilot programmes. The organisation is self-sustaining, with operations also subsidised through partnerships with AWS, Salesforce.org and Google.
The startup was recently selected for the CATAPULT: Inclusion Africa 2026 cohort run by the Luxembourg House of Financial Technology (LHoFT), and while its operations are currently focused on South Africa, it accepts pledges from backers globally, including diaspora communities. It plans to expand its infrastructure and mobile money integrations into markets such as Kenya and Nigeria within the next 24 to 36 months.
The biggest challenge, Whitehead said, has been overcoming the “cold-start” problem faced by first-time creators.
“Many entrepreneurs mistake crowdfunding for a passive lottery, assuming that publishing a campaign will automatically bring in traffic. In reality, crowdfunding amplifies pre-existing momentum. Projects must rally their first 20 to 30 per cent from their immediate networks within 48 hours to trigger the social proof needed for broader discovery,” he said.
“Because unreached goals generate zero revenue for us, educating creators on narrative clarity, realistic budgeting and early community mobilisation remains our most hands-on task.”
The startup is also working to reduce checkout friction on mobile by integrating lower-friction payment options such as PayShap and instant EFT.

articles.title: Microsoft confirms Windows activation failures after November updates
articles.text:
Microsoft has confirmed that this month's Patch Tuesday security updates are causing Windows activation and licensing failures with 0x80041008 error codes.
According to a Wednesday service alert seen by BleepingComputer, this known issue affects organizations that automate Windows activation and licensing processes or use the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) command-line tool.
"Affected devices might encounter error 0x80041008, Invalid parameter (SWbemObjectEx), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys," Microsoft said.
"Devices that are being configured to use KMS activation might encounter errors when attempting to initiate their activation. KMS-activated devices typically remain activated for up to 180 days following successful activation."
The activation failures occur after executing the 'slmgr.vbs /skms-domain <domain>' and 'slmgr.vbs /ipk <key>' commands on client (Windows 10 21H2/22H2 and Windows 11 23H2) and server (Windows Server 2019/2022/2025) devices.
However, Microsoft added that customers with the KMS client key installed in their image and who don't use SLMGR for licensing management are unaffected.
"Devices that are already activated remain activated. Customers whose devices already have the appropriate KMS client key and KMS configuration, and who do not need to run the affected Slmgr.vbs commands, are not expected to be affected," the company noted.
While a fix will be available over the coming days, Microsoft advised affected organizations that need immediate mitigation to reach out to Microsoft Support for business.
In January, Microsoft addressed another known issue that was causing Windows license migration failures during upgrades because affected devices couldn't register with the Windows Activation server for digital licenses.
This week, it also confirmed that the November 2026 Windows 11 security updates fail to install on systems with the October 2026 preview update and that Windows updates released since the October Patch Tuesday are triggering SQL Server performance and stability issues.

articles.text:
[Mise à jour du 13 novembre à 16h11 : la messagerie revient progressivement. Microsoft dit continuer à constater une amélioration de la disponibilité de ses services, avec des files d’attente d’e-mails « considérablement réduites et se rapprochant des niveaux normaux », indiquait le compte Microsoft 365 Status vers 15 heures. Un peu plus tôt, l’éditeur faisait état d’une « amélioration plus large en Amérique du Nord » et d’une « amélioration durable sur une grande partie de l’Europe », ainsi que de « signaux de rétablissement encourageants » en Asie-Pacifique. Il prévient toutefois que « certains utilisateurs peuvent encore rencontrer des problèmes d’accès intermittents ou des retards dans la livraison des e-mails », le temps de résorber les messages en attente. La panne a aussi eu des effets en cascade sur des services tiers, comme ChatGPT et Claude.]
[Mise à jour du 13 novembre à 10h55 : la situation commence à se stabiliser. « Nous observons une première stabilisation et une amélioration des capacités à mesure que les actions de rétablissement se poursuivent », indiquait Microsoft à 10h24. L’éditeur précise aussi avoir porté à 48 heures le délai avant expiration des e-mails, « pour aider à préserver le courrier retardé pendant cet incident ». Les messages envoyés pendant la panne devraient donc être distribués avec retard, plutôt que perdus.]
[Mise à jour du 13 novembre à 8h48 : la situation s’améliore en partie, sans être réglée. Microsoft observe une reprise partielle dans certaines régions, mais reconnaît qu’elle n’est « pas durable ». En France, Outlook restait inaccessible ce vendredi matin. En Australie, le ministre de l’Intérieur Tony Burke affirme que Microsoft estimerait avoir affaire à « une mise à jour qui a mal tourné », comme lors de la panne CrowdStrike de 2024, ce que l’éditeur n’a pas confirmé publiquement, précise Reuters.]
Article original, publié le 13 novembre à 8h31
Les premiers signalements sont arrivés jeudi 12 novembre, peu avant 19 heures, heure de Paris. « Nous enquêtons sur des signalements d’utilisateurs qui rencontrent des problèmes pour accéder à leurs boîtes Exchange Online par plusieurs méthodes de connexion sur le continent américain », écrivait alors le compte Microsoft 365 Status sur X, en référence au service qui fait tourner Outlook. L’alerte s’est vite étendue à toutes les régions du monde, et la liste des services touchés s’est allongée au fil de la soirée : Teams, SharePoint, l’assistant Copilot ou encore des outils de cybersécurité réservés aux entreprises. En France, Outlook restait inaccessible ce vendredi matin, sur ordinateur comme sur smartphone, comme nous avons pu le constater à la rédaction.
 We’re investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543.
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026
L’ampleur de la panne est rare pour Microsoft. Downdetector a reçu environ 200 000 signalements d’utilisateurs, venus de plus de 70 pays, selon Bloomberg, qui la classe parmi les plus importantes de l’histoire de l’éditeur, dont les précédentes interruptions duraient rarement plus de quelques heures. Les conséquences se font sentir bien au-delà des bureaux. Au Japon, le ministère des Finances a indiqué ne pas avoir pu recevoir d’e-mails pendant presque toute la journée, et des ministères ont dû afficher leurs agendas sur papier. En Nouvelle-Zélande, les services d’immigration ont suspendu le traitement des demandes de visa. Aux États-Unis, des districts scolaires, des universités et des hôpitaux ont prévenu que leurs communications pourraient être limitées.
 Microsoft’s outage reports on November 12 reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour on Downdetector.
Microsoft says its Exchange Online incident began at 16:17 UTC. Reports to Downdetector about Outlook began climbing at about 17:25 UTC, 12:25 in New York. By 18:25, reports about five Microsoft services combined reached 19,650 a minute, against <15 a minute on an average Thursday.
Outlook reports alone peaked at more than 2,000 times their normal level.
Reports did not stay in the Americas. They jumped tenfold in the UK at 17:43, in India at 23:21 local time and in New Zealand at 06:55 local time. Between 17:00 and 18:55 UTC, nearly 3 in 10 reports came from outside the US. We count a country here once its reports reach ten times normal and at least 20 in five minutes.
Reports about Microsoft 365, Copilot, Teams and OneDrive each rose more than a hundredfold, and Azure about a hundredfold. Xbox, GitHub and LinkedIn, also Microsoft’s, rose far less.
Microsoft said a portion of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions. At 19:38 UTC, reports were still running at more than 11,000 a minute.
— Downdetector (@downdetector) November 12, 2026
Des serveurs qui retombent dès qu’ils sont relancés
Microsoft a d’abord parlé d’une partie de son infrastructure qui « subit une charge élevée dans plusieurs régions », avant de corriger le tir dans la soirée. « La charge élevée n’est pas due à une hausse du trafic, mais à un certain nombre de serveurs devenus indisponibles de manière inattendue, ce qui met sous tension le reste de l’infrastructure », a précisé l’éditeur. Ses ingénieurs ont ensuite découvert qu’« un processus central sur les serveurs touchés se retrouve débordé », ce qui les empêche de répondre et aggrave la perte de capacité. Microsoft assure n’avoir « connaissance d’aucune activité malveillante » à l’origine de l’incident, rapporte Bloomberg.
Pour tenter de reprendre la main pendant la nuit, Microsoft a suspendu tous ses déploiements, redémarré les serveurs touchés et redirigé une partie du trafic, sans résultat durable. « Les serveurs que nous avons remis en service peuvent redevenir inactifs dès qu’ils reçoivent du trafic », reconnaissait l’éditeur au milieu de la nuit, avant de commencer à reconstruire une partie de ses machines avec une configuration antérieure. Vendredi matin, le constat restait le même : « Nous observons une reprise partielle dans les régions où nous avons appliqué ces ajustements, mais ces actions ne permettent pas un rétablissement durable. » Microsoft ne donne toujours aucun délai de retour à la normale.
 We’re continuing our efforts to improve server stability to improve traffic flow. This includes adjusting traffic protocols, redistributing traffic, and applying strategic traffic blocking measures. We’re observing partial recovery across regions in which we’ve applied these adjustments; however, these actions aren’t resulting in sustained recovery, so we’re reviewing what additional actions we can take to improve overall infrastructure stability. More info under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as https://t.co/pYdahqxDv3 if the admin center is not available to you.
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 13, 2026
La panne gêne aussi les assistants d’intelligence artificielle qui se connectent aux comptes Microsoft pour lire les e-mails ou consulter l’agenda. Outre Copilot, Anthropic et OpenAI ont signalé que Claude et ChatGPT ne parvenaient plus à accéder aux services de Microsoft 365.
Que faire en attendant ?
Le problème vient des serveurs de Microsoft. Il est donc inutile de réinstaller Outlook, de réinitialiser son mot de passe ou de modifier ses paramètres. Le plus simple est de suivre l’évolution de la situation sur la page d’état des services de Microsoft ou sur le compte X Microsoft 365 Status, et de passer par un autre moyen de communication pour les échanges urgents. Microsoft prévient que le retour du service pourrait être progressif, à mesure que les applications se reconnectent.
Cette panne n’a pas de lien avec un autre incident survenu cette semaine sur la messagerie grand public de Microsoft, où des filtres anti-spam défaillants ont bloqué des e-mails légitimes pendant quatre jours.

articles.title: Ryanair adelanta a 60 minutos el cierre del equipaje facturado en todos sus aeropuertos
articles.text:
Tal y como contábamos en abril, Ryanair ha cambiado el límite de tiempo para entregar el equipaje facturado en el aeropuerto. Desde este martes 10 de noviembre, los mostradores de entrega de maletas y facturación cierran una hora antes de la salida programada, en lugar de 40 minutos como antes. Te contamos en qué cambia todo y en qué te puede influir.
Hay que facturar antes. El cambio solo afecta a los pasajeros que quieren facturar una maleta en el aeropuerto y deben acercarse a los mostradores de la aerolínea. En este caso, llegar tarde puede significar que se les deniegue el embarque y, según las condiciones de la tarifa, perder el valor del billete, tal y como apuntan desde El Confidencial. Básicamente, para tenerlo claro, para un vuelo que sale a las 12:00, la maleta debe entregarse antes de las 11:00.
En detalle. La aerolínea anunció la medida en abril y volvió a recordárselo a los pasajeros a finales de octubre. Dara Brady, directora de marketing de Ryanair, declaraba que el cambio dará a los pasajeros que facturan una maleta "más tiempo" para pasar el control de seguridad y de pasaportes y llegar a la puerta antes de que empiece el embarque, especialmente en las horas punta, cuando las colas son más largas.
Quiénes están afectados. Ryanair afirma que alrededor del 20 % de sus pasajeros factura una maleta. El 80 % restante viaja únicamente con equipaje de mano y mantiene su rutina habitual, según las propias cifras de la aerolínea.
Qué no cambia. La facturación online sigue cerrando dos horas antes de la salida, y que la regla no altera ni las dimensiones del equipaje ni las tarifas. Solo cambia el plazo límite para la entrega de las maletas. Esto se aplica a todos los aeropuertos en los que opera Ryanair.
El argumento de la aerolínea. Ryanair presenta la norma como una forma de proteger a los pasajeros. Afirma que el nuevo plazo debería reducir el pequeño número de viajeros que pierden sus vuelos tras quedarse atascados en las colas de seguridad o de pasaportes. Ya tuvimos el caso de Milán o el de Tenerife Sur y East Midlands, donde muchos pasajeros no pudieron embarcar por las largas colas en el control de pasaportes.
Entre líneas. Igual 20 minutos no es mucho sobre el papel, pero cabe destacar que la carga al final recae sobre el pasajero. Y es que las colas del aeropuerto siguen siendo las mismas, mientras que el tiempo disponible para cumplir con el plazo de entrega de equipaje se reduce. La medida también pone el foco en la minoría que factura maletas, un grupo al que Ryanair lleva tiempo empujando a viajar ligero a través de su estricta política de equipaje.
Kioscos de autoservicio. Paralelamente al nuevo plazo, Ryanair está desplegando kioscos de autoservicio para la entrega de equipaje integrados en su app, donde los pasajeros pueden facturar sus maletas e imprimir sus propias etiquetas de equipaje. La aerolínea tenía previsto disponer de ellos en más del 95 % de sus aeropuertos antes de octubre.

articles.title: Feijóo, sobre los autónomos que facturen menos de 85.000 euros: "No pagarán IVA"
articles.text:
Jordi Wild quiso saber qué pasaría con quienes ya llevan años pagando la cuota de autónomos. Alberto Núñez Feijóo respondió en la entrevista de The Wild Project con un umbral. "No pagarán IVA", dijo el presidente del Partido Popular (PP) sobre quienes facturen menos de 85.000 euros al año. En la práctica, explicó, dejarían de cobrar el impuesto sobre el valor añadido (IVA) en sus facturas.
La propuesta gira en torno al IVA franquiciado. La directiva europea para pequeñas empresas permite a cada país adoptar una exención nacional y fijar su umbral de facturación, con un máximo de 85.000 euros. A 13 de noviembre de 2026, la ley española del IVA sigue sin prever una exención general por facturar menos de esa cantidad.
La Comisión Europea explicó en marzo por qué decidió llevar a España ante la justicia europea. La exención dentro del país es opcional. Lo que España debe incorporar son las reglas para que las pequeñas empresas establecidas aquí puedan solicitar la exención en otros Estados miembros que la apliquen, si cumplen sus condiciones.
Feijóo presentó la medida como una vía para bajar precios o mejorar resultados y habló de un margen del 21%. Ese porcentaje es el tipo general del impuesto. El efecto en cada negocio dependería de cuánto cobre a sus clientes y del IVA que pague en sus compras, porque el régimen europeo limita el derecho a deducirlo cuando se trata de compras vinculadas a operaciones acogidas a la franquicia.
La cuota a la Seguridad Social iría por otra vía. Feijóo propuso que los autónomos que contraten a su primer trabajador se ahorren la cotización empresarial de ese contrato durante el primer año. Para el segundo, habló de una rebaja del 50% en función de la facturación. También planteó dar a los autónomos más margen para decidir cada cuánto declaran. El programa electoral del PP concreta dos declaraciones al año para quienes las presentan trimestralmente y una al año para quienes inician su actividad.
