articles.title: Toyosi Badejo-Okusanya on building Adaptive Atelier
articles.text:
The cinema is a useful place to begin a conversation with Toyosi Badejo-Okusanya about accessibility. She had seen the publicity for Barbie, a 2023 satirical fantasy comedy film directed by Greta Gerwig, and bought a ticket to watch it. There were no captions at her screening.
All the work of persuading her to come had succeeded, but at the point where she sat down to watch, much of the film was out of reach.
Badejo-Okusanya, who is deaf, knows what goes into getting a customer that far. Her career in marketing took her to Jo Malone London, where even the placement of a bottle on a shelf was something to think about.
“A report is something you file,” she says, “What a customer experiences is something you have to keep working on.”
She still notices where shops put things and wonders what the sales data told them. That attention to detail makes the cinema experience striking. A company can spend months making you want to see a film and fail to give a thought to whether you can follow it once you’re there.
She grew up in Nigeria, moved to London at 16 and studied law. Her family had expected a lawyer. They got the law degree, she says, and then she went into tech. She now runs Adaptive Atelier, a company that helps businesses find and fix barriers in their digital products. Its approach combines automated checks with testing by disabled professionals, whom it pays for their work.
We talked about growing up deaf in Nigeria, finding community in London at 16, and what made her stop looking for a regular job and give the company her full attention.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
Where did you grow up, and what would your family say you were like at ten? What would they say you still haven’t grown out of?
I grew up in Nigeria. If you asked my family about me at ten, I think they’d say I was finding my confidence. That’s around when I started secondary school, which was a big step: long days away from home for the first time, a new environment, far less of my parents to lean on. I think I handled it pretty well.
What they’d say I haven’t grown out of is the determination, and a habit of coming up with random things and then actually seeing them through, from the idea to the finished thing. The ideas were never the hard part for me. The finishing is the bit I enjoy.
What did the adults around you think you’d become? Did you ever want the life they imagined for you?
A lawyer. Everyone was certain, and for a long time so was I. I did study law, so I delivered that part, and then I went into tech, which I think surprised them.
But what I wanted from law was never really the title. I wanted to defend people who were being treated unjustly, and living with a disability showed me where that could happen. A lot of that unfairness turns out to be built into products and platforms before any person has the chance to be unkind, so that’s where I ended up working.
What do you remember about how people talked about deafness when you were growing up? When did you find your own words for it?
In Nigeria I heard “deaf and dumb” a lot. And when I said I was deaf, people would tell me, “Don’t say that! You’re not deaf.” I remember being confused, because by definition, that’s what I am.
Deafness was also spoken about in a religious way, as evidence that something had gone wrong somewhere and I needed to pray for God to fix me.
I moved to London at 16, and that’s when I found my own words for it. I found community, and I started to see it as part of what makes me stand out, rather than something to be repaired. It’s the way I am, and nothing can change that.
Before you worked in beauty, what did you find beautiful? Did working with brands like Jo Malone London change what you noticed when you walked into a shop?
I’d always loved marketing, so seeing a brand like Jo Malone London up close was a lesson in attention to detail. Luxury fashion and beauty are inventive and slightly eccentric in a way you don’t find everywhere.
It did change what I noticed in a shop. I now look at where products are placed, and I think about how data shapes what people buy and how different that looks from region to region. One example that stayed with me: fresher, woodier scents were more popular in APAC, while in EMEA people leaned towards stronger, oud-based ones. You never walk into a shop the same way again.
Can you remember a campaign you were proud of but couldn’t fully experience yourself? Did you say anything at the time?
Not one of my own that I can point to. The closest is films. When Barbie came out, and more recently The Devil Wears Prada 2, I went to the cinema like everyone else, and there were no captions, so most of it was out of reach.
Those campaigns invite you in from every billboard and every feed, and then the film itself doesn’t let you follow it. That’s a strange gap for an industry that thinks so hard about experience.
What did working with big brands teach you about how to get a decision made? When accessibility needed money, whose mind did you have to change?
That decisions are rarely made in the meeting. There are layers of approval, so you work backwards: find out who signs it off, build the business case for them, and look for the person who either owns the decision or genuinely cares about the cause. Nobody approves “it’s the right thing to do”. They approve a case.
When accessibility needed money, the minds I had to change were the CEOs and the C-suite, because that’s where the budgets sit.
You divide your time between Lagos and London. What feels easy in Lagos that people in London make unnecessarily complicated? And what works the other way round?
In Lagos I find it much easier to get in front of key executive teams than I do in London. And I don’t think about my race in Lagos, which is its own kind of ease.
The other way round, London has more legal obligations around accessibility, so organisations have a reason to act. In Lagos that pressure mostly isn’t there. I can explain that a large group of people is being left out, and many still don’t see it, because most of the people in the room can use those platforms without a second thought. Neither place has it worked out. They’re missing different things.
When did you realise you wanted to build Adaptive Atelier rather than spend your career advising other companies? What did you have to give up to find out whether it could work?
When I realised how many solutions could be built, and that as an adviser I would never get to set the terms. You make a recommendation, and someone else decides whether it happens.
What I gave up was chasing a 9-to-5. It was a tough decision. For a while I tried to do both, because that made more sense financially, but my attention was split and I was never giving either one 100%. So I decided to find out what would happen if I gave Adaptive Atelier everything.
That was almost two years ago, and, well, we’re still here. We’re building slowly, but towards one goal: inclusive solutions for all.
Who was the first person to pay you for work you’d done through Adaptive Atelier? What did they think they were buying, and was it the same thing you thought you were selling?
A financial institution. I’ll leave their name out of it. I think they thought they were buying a report: a list of what was wrong, something to put in front of compliance. What I thought I was selling was a way to see their product through a disabled customer’s eyes. A report is something you file. What a customer experiences is something you have to keep working on, and I think that gap is where most of the real work sits
Show me something your AI would pass that a disabled tester would send straight back. What does the person catch that the software misses?
The example I keep coming back to is from our own tool. When we scanned some Nigerian fintech homepages, we found an empty button. AdaptiveTest suggested a fix: add the words “Click me”.
Technically, that passes. The button now has a name and the automated check is satisfied. But a screen reader user hears “Click me” and has no idea whether it sends money or closes a pop-up. A disabled tester would send that straight back.
Software can tell you something is missing. It can’t decide what the label should say, whether alt text is actually useful, or whether a form makes sense when you can’t see it. That’s why I describe a scan as the first pass, not the finish line.
When a client pays for an accessibility test, how much of that fee goes to the people doing the testing? What has it taken to turn that expertise into steady paid work?
The principle is simple: disabled professionals do the testing through AdaptiveAlly, and they’re paid for it rather than being asked to give their expertise away. Testers are paid today and get to keep between 80-90% of the fee whilst Adaptive Atelier takes a commission per project.
Steady work is the harder part. A tester only earns consistently if clients keep coming back, which is why we built Test, Wiz and Ally as a loop rather than three separate products: the scan finds the issues, and human validation returns each time something changes.
Has a client ever wanted to be seen to care about accessibility more than they wanted to fix the problem? How did you handle that conversation?
I don’t think of it as bad faith. Many organisations come to accessibility through reputation, because that’s what gets attention internally. The risk is when the badge becomes the goal.
So I try to move the conversation from “how do we look?” to “what happens to a disabled customer on our checkout page?” Accessibility is a product and customer-experience responsibility. A statement, a scan or a personalisation tool on top of a broken journey doesn’t change what a customer actually experiences. The real test is whether a disabled person can complete the task on these digital platforms
In Sound Through My Lens, you tell parts of your own story in public. Has there been a moment you thought you’d share and then decided to keep for yourself?
Yes. I’m fairly open about parts of my story, but I’ve learned not to share something until I understand it myself. If I’m still in the middle of it, it stays with me. The stories in Sound Through My Lens are ones I’ve had time to make sense of, and I’d rather give people something considered than something raw that I might wish I’d kept. There are times when I have been discriminated against at global embassies because of my hearing aids and still haven’t shared those stories till today.
What does a good Saturday look like when nobody needs your opinion on accessibility? Where are you, who’s there, and what are you eating?
It starts slowly. No laptop and, if I can help it, nobody asks me anything. I like being with people I don’t have to explain myself to, which usually means friends who care about clothes, fashion, beauty and making things as much as I do. There’s food, of course, preferably cinnamon rolls, taken slowly, with good conversation. If there’s a project on the go, it’s about getting it from ideation to execution.
If we have lunch again in ten years and Adaptive Atelier has become everything you hoped it would be, what would still have to be true about your life for you to say you’re happy?
I’d want to still be someone who makes things for the pleasure of it, not only because they need to scale. I’d want my friendships and my creative life to have had the same attention I gave the company. And I’d want to be splitting my time between different countries because I like exploring new environments and cultures, not because the work demands it. If Adaptive Atelier has done what I hope, the world is a bit more accessible and I’m not the one who has to explain why.

articles.title: Law Enforcement Disrupts Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC Infrastructure
articles.text:
Law enforcement agencies in the US, Europe, Australia, and Canada have seized infrastructure behind the notorious Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware.
The investigators seized 235 servers and 257 domains associated with the malicious operations, severely crippling their distribution networks, Europol says.
Operating under the cybercrime-as-a-service model, Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC enabled ransomware attacks, data theft, and other cybercrime activities.
Distributed through compromised websites containing fake legal documents, Gootloader has been operating as a dropper for other malware families, including ransomware.
Active since at least 2018, Gootloader has infected over 25,000 computers and caused damages of approximately $28.8 million in the US, the US Department of Justice says.
According to the DoJ, the fresh disruption, part of Operation Endgame, led to the dropper’s removal from 100 servers. Europol reports that 14 servers and 218 domains associated with Gootloader were seized and 681 infected websites were cleaned up.
A remote access trojan (RAT) active since at least 2025, CastleRAT has provided threat actors with control over infected machines, which were then abused to deploy file-encrypting ransomware.
Law enforcement seized 120 servers and 39 domains used by CastleRAT’s operators, as well as victim data. HaveIBeenPwned says 180,000 email addresses and 893,000 unique passwords were retrieved.
Active since at least 2023, StealC functions as a stealer and a dropper, mainly focused on password, data, and identity theft. In a continuation of law enforcement action targeting the malware earlier this year, 102 StealC servers were disrupted.
According to Europol, the fresh law enforcement disruption led to the seizure of 6.4 million victim credentials, which have been shared with HaveIBeenPwned, DIVD, CheckjeHack, NoMoreLeaks, Sekoia, The Shadowserver Foundation, and NL-NCSC.
“The suspects were using these credentials, stolen from the victims after they infected them, to sell them and later be used for other cyber-attacks such as ransomware,” Europol notes.

articles.title: Nvidia procura substituto para Jensen Huang e mira CEO de concorrente
articles.text:
A Nvidia começou a avaliar possíveis substitutos para Jensen Huang e já procurou um nome de peso do setor de semicondutores: Rene Haas, CEO da Arm. Segundo informações do Financial Times e da Reuters, o executivo está entre os candidatos considerados pelo conselho da gigante de inteligência artificial (IA) após a saída de seu cofundador.
Huang anunciou sua renúncia na quinta-feira (12), depois de 33 anos à frente da companhia. Sua saída ocorreu em meio à repercussão de um escândalo envolvendo relacionamentos extraconjugais e uma cliente que, segundo suspeitas da inteligência dos Estados Unidos, seria uma espiã chinesa.
Haas, que lidera a Arm desde 2022, tem ligação antiga com a Nvidia. Ele trabalhou na companhia por aproximadamente sete anos, há mais de uma década, e mantém relação próxima com Huang e integrantes do conselho.
Apesar da abordagem, não há garantia de que Haas receberá uma proposta formal ou aceitará assumir o comando da Nvidia. O executivo também está entre os poucos nomes de fora da empresa considerados capazes de ocupar o posto.
Quem pode substituir Jensen Huang na Nvidia?
- Além de Haas, outro nome externo considerado é Lisa Su, CEO da AMD, principal concorrente da Nvidia no mercado de chips. A empresa também avalia possíveis sucessores dentro de sua própria estrutura;
- Entre os candidatos internos estão Colette Kress, diretora financeira que atualmente ocupa o cargo de CEO interina, e Ian Buck, responsável pela divisão de data centers;
- A transição representa um desafio considerável. Huang concentrou grande parte das decisões da Nvidia durante sua gestão e construiu relação de forte identificação com funcionários e investidores. Encontrar alguém capaz de assumir esse papel é uma tarefa especialmente delicada para uma companhia avaliada em aproximadamente US$ 4 trilhões (cerca de R$ 21,3 trilhões);
- O conselho também passa por mudanças. Harvey Jones, integrante da administração desde a fundação da Nvidia, em 1993, foi nomeado o primeiro presidente do conselho da empresa.
Leia mais:
- Trump tentou salvar Jensen Huang no comando da Nvidia antes de sua saída
- Projetos de IA na China ainda dependem de processadores Nvidia
- Caso Jensen Huang: o que acontece com o império dos chips após a queda da “Taylor Swift” da IA?
Relação entre Rene Haas e Nvidia tem capítulo curioso
A possível escolha de Haas tem um elemento adicional: a relação entre a Arm e a Nvidia no mercado de semicondutores.
A tecnologia da Arm está presente na maioria dos chips de smartphones do mundo e também é utilizada nos equipamentos de IA da Nvidia. Neste ano, porém, a fabricante britânica lançou seu próprio chip completo de IA, passando a disputar diretamente o mercado com empresas que também são suas clientes.
Haas também construiu relação próxima com Masayoshi Son, CEO do SoftBank, grupo japonês que controla a Arm e busca desenvolver ecossistema de IA capaz de rivalizar com o da Nvidia. Em abril, Haas também assumiu a liderança dos negócios internacionais do SoftBank.
O executivo já havia sido orientado por Huang durante sua passagem pela Nvidia. Depois de deixar a companhia, em 2013, Haas seguiu para a Arm.
A Nvidia, por sua vez, tentou comprar a fabricante britânica em 2020, em operação avaliada em US$ 40 bilhões (cerca de R$ 213 bilhões na cotação aproximada), mas o negócio acabou abandonado diante de preocupações regulatórias.
Enquanto avalia a sucessão, o conselho da Nvidia também supervisiona uma investigação independente sobre a conduta de Huang, conduzida por um ex-promotor federal. O caso ampliou o escrutínio sobre a governança e a administração da companhia.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: 'Wild Horse Nine' (★★★★☆), deliciosa tragicomedia de espías idiotas que puede darle el Oscar a John Malkovich
articles.text:
Aunque la campaña de premios apenas acaba de empezar, ya hay una película que suena muy fuerte para esta temporada. Wild Horse Nine, del director Martin McDonagh (Tres anuncios a las afueras, Almas en pena de Inisherin), lleva ya meses sonando muy fuerte en las casas de apuestas. Especialmente porque uno de sus dos protagonistas, el icónico John Malkovich, podría levantar su primer Premio Oscar a los 72 años. Por lo pronto, ya ganó hace unos meses la prestigiosa Copa Volpi a mejor actor en el Festival de Venecia.
En Wild Horse Nine, poco antes del golpe de Estado chileno de 1973, los agentes de la CIA Chris (John Malkovich) y Lee (Sam Rockwell) son enviados desde Santiago a la Isla de Pascua por su jefe de oficina, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Entre las emblemáticas estatuas de la isla, y mientras los veteranos compañeros se enfrentan a sus oscuros pasados y a las conspiraciones del presente, el nuevo vínculo de Chris con dos estudiantes rebeldes (Mariana di Girolamo y Ailín Salas) amenaza con dar un giro inesperado al viaje de todos a este remoto paraíso.
La soledad del hombre entre Moais
Como ya ocurría en Almas en pena de Inisherin, Martin McDonagh vuelve a presentarnos en Wilde Horse Nine un drama profundamente melancólico. Otra vez, una relación de dos amigos disfuncionales en una isla le sirve como vehículo para hablar de la soledad como la gran derrota del hombre.
Wilde Horse Nine es cine profunda y marcadamente triste. Fatalista incluso. El director presenta temas tan profundos como la pérdida de relaciones sociales, la corrupción del alma, la desconfianza del mundo o la actitud frente a la muerte. Todo ello, además, en un entorno único y místico que engrandece la naturaleza para empequeñecer al ser humano todavía más.
En ese sentido, el cineasta mantiene su esencia de amplios planos generales en los que sus personajes se difuminan entre las praderas de la isla y sus escarpadas costas. La pesadumbre que baña todo el filme acaba por empapar también al espectador, que no tiene más remedio que rendirse a ese ritmo lento, a ese aura pesimista y desolador.
Ironía política
Eso sí, entre tanto drama latente, Wild Horse Nine consigue el milagro de colar con brillante inteligencia muchísimo humor negro. Para empezar, el que destilan sus dos protagonistas, dos espías a los que se les presenta como grandes profesionales, pero cuya destreza parece quedar solo en el ámbito profesional. Son torpes, son absolutos idiotas, incapaces de comportarse como adultos serios. Las carcajadas por sus riñas y actitudes inmaduras van a ser constantes en el cine.
Además, el contexto en el que McDonagh sitúa a su película le permite sobresalir también como sátira política. El director indaga abiertamente la intromisión del sistema corrupto en la vida del hombre. Wild Horse Nine se lamenta por la muerte de la ideología, oprimida por los grandes poderes frente a los que el ciudadano no puede hacer mucho más que sentirse indefenso. O liarse a tiros para desquitarse, que viene a ser un poco lo mismo.
Más concretamente, el filme critica con dureza y ácida ironía la intromisión de Estados Unidos en otros territorios como Chile para desestabilizar gobiernos y democracias a su antojo. La cinta habla sin tapujos del apoyo norteamericano a Pinochet para derrocar a Allende. También se burla del asesinato de Kennedy con una sorprendente subtrama que aporta aún más capas al conjunto.
John Malkovich está de Oscar
No se puede acabar de hablar de Wild Horse Nine sin destacar, por encima de todo lo demás, el trabajo de un descomunal John Malkovich. El actor nos regala uno de los papeles de su vida, devora la pantalla a base de humor e histrionismo. Su personaje es un excéntrico anciano al borde de la muerte que resulta ser, además, un espía de leyenda totalmente pasado de vueltas.
El intérprete está inconmensurable, gigantesco, se crece en las rarezas de ese improbable protagonista con su inseparable sombrero. Si finalmente gana el Oscar -actualmente es el gran favorito junto a Matt Damon por La Odisea- será totalmente merecido. No solo sería justicia a toda una carrera de grandes trabajos, es que de verdad deja un papel sensacional. Es provocador, radical, capaz de despertar ternura y rabia a partes iguales.
Además, se apoya en la réplica de un también sensacional Sam Rockwell, quien simplemente destaca menos porque su personaje no está tan rematadamente loco (aún) y porque se mantiene en un registro muy similar al que ya le hemos visto en otras películas. En cualquier caso, no cabe duda de que Martin McDonagh se ha asegurado con ellos u dúo protagonista magnífico para Wild Horse Nine.
En resumen, Wild Horse Nine es, de nuevo, otra grandísima película de Martin McDonagh. Un drama a fuego lento y profundamente triste, aderezado con desternillantes dosis humor negro y un marcado mensaje político. Su melancólico y afilado guion está plagado de diálogos punzantes entre los que se dibuja el desasosiego de unos personajes indefensos ante su propio mundo en ruinas. Una película genial.

articles.title: Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
articles.text:
Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom — and one of the tech industry’s biggest environmental liabilities. Its sought-after chips have triggered a new wave of water- and chemical-intensive factories, drained power grids from inside massive data centers, and set the stage for a looming e-waste problem.
Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
Nvidia’s environmental footprint extends way beyond its own offices.
Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia clashed with environmental groups seeking to hold the company accountable for its so-called “hidden” emissions. Huang has talked up the idea of using AI to fight climate change while his company’s supply chain emissions ballooned. Nvidia’s investments, meanwhile, have supported the buildout of data centers that have sparked intense backlash for both their local and global impact. Now, after the CEO’s shocking resignation amid a sprawling sex-and-espionage scandal, advocates are urging Nvidia to turn the page.
He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”
“Jensen Huang has failed to put climate responsibility at the heart of the company’s growth strategy, to slow down the unchecked expansion of data centres or to prevent its chips from being deployed in unethical applications like automated warfare,” Avex Li, Greenpeace East Asia’s project lead for AI supply chain campaign, said in a press release Thursday. The organization is now pushing interim CEO Colette Kress to commit Nvidia to decarbonizing by investing in renewable energy, as well as ensuring its technology is used in a way that “respects human rights.” Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge.
Huang has projected optimism about how AI can boost the adoption of renewable energy, even as the planet-heating emissions of tech companies — including his own — have grown in the generative AI era. “If you want to turn a corner on climate change, if you want a future that’s sustainable, lean into A.I. It is the best opportunity we have to get there,” Huang said in a September episode of The Ezra Klein Show, arguing that electricity demand for AI is leading companies to buy more sustainable energy.
In the same interview, however, he admitted data centers will rely on more fossil fuels in the near term, and that building up the infrastructure for AI will likely result in “an enormous amount of pain and suffering.” He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”
Nvidia’s supply-chain emissions have grown 725 percent since 2020, according to an analysis of the company’s public disclosures by research analyst Ketan Joshi and several environmental organizations, including Greenpeace and Climate Action Against Disinformation, published in September. It’s an increase of about 9.4 million metric tons of planet-heating pollution, roughly equivalent to the emissions from nearly 25 gas plants over a year. Supply chain emissions the company disclosed for fiscal year 2026 reached around 10.7 million metric tons of CO2, according to Nvidia’s latest sustainability report.
Joshi and his co-authors approximated how much greenhouse gas pollution comes from the use of chips the company sells, a category Nvidia doesn’t include in its sustainability reports. Those emissions could have reached 21 million metric tons in 2025, according to the report, based on estimated chip power consumption. That level of pollution puts Nvidia on par with Russia’s state-owned coal company, according to Joshi.
Those “indirect” emissions — from its supply chain and the use of its products — make up the bulk of Nvidia’s climate impact. The carbon footprint of facilities Nvidia actually owns and operates looks much smaller in comparison because Nvidia designs chips that other companies like TSMC then manufacture. Greenhouse gas emissions coming directly from Nvidia-operated facilities and vehicles only reached 9,822 metric tons in fiscal year 2026, the company’s sustainability report shows. And in 2025, the company reached a goal of matching 100 percent of its facilities’ electricity use with clean energy purchases.
Greenpeace wants Nvidia to extend that goal to its entire manufacturing supply chain. When Greenpeace activists disrupted Huang’s speech at Nvidia GTC in Berlin last month, he responded onstage by saying, “I’ll talk to you guys later … All important issues, but let me get through my keynote.” In the Thursday press release, Greenpeace says Nvidia has yet to meet with Greenpeace despite the organization’s attempts to “seek dialogue” with the company over the past two years.
“One of Huang’s defining legacies is inflating a speculative AI bubble, pouring billions of dollars into infrastructure with little regard for the real-world consequences inflicted on local communities and the climate,” Katrin Wu, Big Tech campaigner at Greenpeace International, said in an email to The Verge. “Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”
“Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”
Beyond Nvidia’s day-to-day operations, Huang threw his weight around as the CEO of one of the world’s most valuable companies — chumming it up with President Donald Trump and lobbying for the US to allow sales of its powerful chips to China. The company’s influence on the global economy extended beyond chips as it invested in data centers stocking its GPUs.
And with electricity supply often the thorniest bottleneck to building more and bigger data centers, Nvidia’s long tendrils reached into the energy sector as well. NVentures, the company’s venture capital arm, has funded battery recycling company Redwood Materials and startups developing AI tools to optimize power grids and make data centers more responsive to fluctuations in energy demand.
Nvidia joined one of those startups, Emerald AI, along with Google to cofound the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA) in September. The alliance advocates for strategies that tech companies promote as ways to keep data centers from overwhelming power grids or raising utility bills for other customers, including generating power on-site and making “flexible” facilities that can pause operations during times of peak energy demand. Notably, some environmental groups argue that those measures might just help data centers come online faster without fully insulating households from the impact that rising electricity demand has on their air quality or utility bills.
Whether Nvidia’s environmental footprint shrinks or expands from here will depend on whoever steps in to fill Huang’s shoes. Over the years, Greenpeace and other environmental groups have pointed out that despite having an outsize impact on the environment, Nvidia doesn’t necessarily come under the same public scrutiny as more consumer-facing brands like Apple or Google. Huang’s exploits have thrust the company into a new kind of spotlight, however, just as data centers increasingly face backlash from nearby communities. Nvidia won’t be able to hide from the glare.

articles.title: HDD mit SSD kombiniert: Diese neue 20-Terabyte-Festplatte hat aber einen Haken
articles.text:
HDD mit SSD kombiniert: Diese neue 20-Terabyte-Festplatte hat aber einen Haken
Heutzutage gibt es Speichermedien, die wir längst nicht mehr nutzen. Das liegt daran, dass neue Lösungen wie SSDs im Hinblick auf Geschwindigkeiten und Zuverlässigkeit mittlerweile viel besser als die Vorgänger sind. Zu diesen veralteten Speichermedien gehören sogenannte SSHDs, eine Kombination aus einer mechanischen HDD und einer SSD. Jetzt will Hersteller Seagate die Tage der angestaubten Speicherlösung wieder aufleben lassen.
Seagate Firecuda Forge: So funktioniert die Festplatte
Die neue Seagate Firecuda Forge kommt in zwei Konfigurationen: eine Version mit acht Terabyte und eine mit 20 Terabyte vorinstalliertem Speicher. Dabei handelt es sich um Massenspeicher im HDD-Format, mit dem die langfristige Datenspeicherung realisiert werden soll. Für häufig genutzte und schnell abrufbare Daten bietet die Seagate Firecuda Forge noch einen NVMe-Steckplatz für eine SSD.
Dabei musst du aber nicht selbst die Daten ständig zwischen HDD und SSD verschieben. Seagate nutzt das sogenannte Alkemi-System, um das automatisch umzusetzen. Die Festplatte erkennt anhand deines Nutzungsverhaltens, welche Daten besonders häufig aufgerufen werden, und verschiebt sie auf den schnellen Speicher. Werden die Daten wieder seltener genutzt und andere dafür häufiger aufgerufen, wechselt das System sie durch.
Grundsätzlich wird der Speicher der Festplatte dabei immer als Gesamtspeicher angezeigt. Du musst dir beim Verschieben oder Öffnen von Dateien also auch keine Gedanken machen. Laut Seagate richtet sich die Festplatte besonders an Gamer:innen, die ihre aktiven Spiele auf der SSD haben möchten, während die restliche Spielebibliothek auf der HDD verweilen kann. Ebenso ist die Seagate Firecuda Forge für Content-Creator:innen gedacht, die immer wieder neue Videoprojekte bearbeiten und danach langfristig speichern wollen.
Einen größeren Haken gibt es aber noch bei der Seagate Firecuda Forge. Für den Preis von knapp 700 Euro für die Variante mit acht Gigabyte und 930 Euro für die 20-Gigabyte-Version inkludiert Seagate keine NVMe‑SSD. Käufer:innen müssen den schnellen Speicher selbst erwerben und einbauen. Wer möchte, kann sogar die vorinstallierten HDD-Speicher austauschen. Eine NVMe‑SSD mit einem Terabyte Speicher von Seagate kostet etwa 160 Euro.

articles.title: pCloud ya está de Black Friday: tiene un descuento de más del 60% en todos sus planes de por vida de almacenamiento en la nube
articles.text:
Este noviembre, mes del Black Friday, es perfecto para renovar tu viejo móvil o comprar un nuevo televisor. También es un período en el que merece la pena considerar servicios como puede ser un almacenamiento en la nube, ya que hay varios con descuentos importantes. Uno de ellos es pCloud, alternativa a Google Drive que tiene ahora mismo un descuentazo en todos sus planes de por vida: parten de los 159 euros y solo es un único pago.
pCloud - 500 GB de almacenamiento de por vida
Un solo pago para evitar suscripciones mensuales o subidas de precio
pCloud es un servicio de almacenamiento en la nube que opera bajo la legislación suiza y que permite elegir entre dos regiones a la hora de almacenar nuestros datos: Unión Europea y Estados Unidos. Más allá de los distintos planes que ofrece (hablaremos de ello a continuación), destaca por ofrecer una interfaz de usuario muy fácil de usar y que permite acceder a nuestros archivos desde prácticamente cualquier dispositivo.
Cuenta con varias funciones que merece la pena reseñar. Una de ellas es que cuenta con una app de escritorio que funciona como un disco virtual, lo que nos ayudará a gestionar los archivos como lo haríamos con los de nuestro PC. Además, permite compartir archivos con otras personas (aunque no usen pCloud) y cuenta con herramientas como pCloud Photos para organizar nuestras fotografías y vídeos, o pCloud Docs, ideal para editar o colaborar en documentos y hojas de cálculo directamente desde la plataforma.
Ahora sí, hablemos de los planes. Los que tenemos en oferta son los que son para toda la vida, por lo que solo tendremos que pagar una única vez. Esto es ideal por dos razones: te evita tener una suscripción más y, además, te ahorra posibles subidas de precio. Estos son los precios de los cuatro planes de por vida que podemos elegir:
- 500 GB de almacenamiento: 159 euros (antes 279 euros).
- 2 TB de almacenamiento: 379 euros (antes 709 euros).
- 10 TB de almacenamiento: 1.099 euros (antes 2.799 euros).
- Pack 3 en 1 con 3 TB de almacenamiento, pCloud Pass y pCloud Encryption: 579 euros (antes 1.517 euros).
¿Cuál elegir? Va a depender de nuestras necesidades. Los 500 GB pueden ser suficientes para muchos usuarios, aunque la oferta más completa la tendremos con el Pack 3 en 1. La razón es que, además de disponer de 3 TB de almacenamiento, también tendremos un gestor de contraseñas (pCloud Pass) y una herramienta de cifrado (pCloud Encryption), la cual nos permitirá utilizar cifrado de conocimiento cero.

articles.title: Four friends want to change how South African e-hailing drivers make money
articles.text:
Four friends funded an e-hailing app with proceeds from their property-maintenance business—and now they want South African drivers to keep 100% of their fares. With 30,000+ registered drivers, Bro Cabs is betting subscriptions can beat Uber and Bolt’s commission model. In this week’s Coffee With…, PHATHISANI MOYO speaks to the founders.
The first version of Bro Cabs, a commission-free e-hailing platform for drivers, was not financed by a venture capital firm or a large technology investor. It was paid for by a property-maintenance business run by four friends who decided that if they wanted to build something of their own, they would have to find a way to fund it themselves.
They put some of the business’s proceeds towards developers, equipment and the work needed to turn an idea into a functioning e-hailing application. They could not afford every service upfront, but built relationships with people willing to help them get the product off the ground.
“We didn’t want to do things the conventional way,” Persy Qamata, Bro Cabs’ chief executive officer (CEO), told TechCabal in an interview on Monday. “We weren’t going to allow a lack of financing to prevent us from getting a minimum viable product (MVP) off the ground.”
The four founders, chief operating officer Msizi Mtolo, Qamata, chief marketing officer Cebile Magudulela and chief strategy officer Luther Mfetane, were entering an industry dominated by larger, established platforms.
But they were not simply trying to build another e-hailing application. They wanted to change how drivers pay for access to these platforms and how much of each fare they get to keep.
Bro Cabs uses a subscription model. Instead of taking a percentage of every trip, it charges drivers a fee to use the platform, allowing them to retain the full fare. The proposition is straightforward. Building a business around it is not. The founders must attract drivers and passengers, secure capital to compete with established operators and prove that subscriptions can sustain a growing business.
An idea shaped by the driver’s seat
The thinking behind Bro Cabs was sharpened by Mtolo’s experience after moving from KwaZulu-Natal to Johannesburg.
Before the company took shape, he worked in the rental-car industry and took several e-hailing trips a day. According to an account Qamata shared in a separate interview, this exposed Mtolo to the commissions charged by existing platforms and their effect on drivers’ earnings.
The fare displayed on an application is not necessarily what reaches a driver’s pocket. Fuel, maintenance and insurance all have to be paid, with platform commission taking another portion.
Mtolo’s experience helped the founders identify a problem they believed they could address. The group had already been working on a web-development project for small and medium-sized businesses. They initially planned to use those skills to develop an application for the taxi industry, but encountered resistance and redirected their efforts towards e-hailing.
Qamata says the group chose to enter an established industry and solve a problem they could see within it. Bro Cabs emerged from the idea that drivers should not have to surrender a percentage of every fare to access customers.
Building before asking for money
The property-maintenance business gave the founders a practical starting point. They wanted to show investors a product people could use, rather than an idea that existed only in a presentation.
They began with a minimum viable product, less sophisticated than the application they have today but functional enough for drivers and passengers to test.
“We understood that before approaching angel investors, we needed to demonstrate that the business was worth investing in,” Magudulela said. “We needed a working product and customers.”
They concentrated on Johannesburg and initially targeted a specific market, including students. They wanted to learn how people used the application and where it could find its first customers.
Early progress depended as much on relationships as technology. Developers worked with them despite the company’s limited resources, while drivers frustrated with established platforms were open to an alternative. Some supporters put Bros Cabs stickers on their vehicles.
The platform began a pilot in Braamfontein, central Johannesburg, in July 2025. The founders initially aimed to register 50 drivers and 100 commuters. Qamata said that within two months they had signed up 710 drivers and 1,150 commuters. The company opened the platform to the public in November 2025.
A different way to pay for a ride
The subscription model is the clearest expression of what the founders want to change.
Traditional e-hailing platforms generally charge drivers a commission on completed trips. Bro Cabs takes a different approach, charging drivers a subscription fee to access the platform while allowing them to keep 100% of their fares. Its published options have included R30 ($1.81) a day, R150 ($9.04) a week and R600 ($36.14) a month.
Qamata says the approach was influenced partly by Namma Yatri, an Indian mobility platform that has demonstrated an alternative to conventional commission-based e-hailing.
“We were introducing something new,” he said. “We hadn’t seen a model in Africa where drivers paid upfront to use an e-hailing platform while retaining 100% of their earnings.”
That difference also raises questions for investors: will enough drivers pay a subscription, will the platform attract passengers, and can recurring income cover the costs of expansion?
The founders argue that drivers should be able to keep more of the money they generate. Magudulela links the issue to the households that depend on driving income.
“Remember, we’re talking about driver earnings. When drivers earn more, their families benefit,” he said. “There are many households that depend on the income generated through driving.”
A Bolt-commissioned Ipsos study published in April 2026 found that 70% of surveyed South African gig workers used ride-hailing to supplement other earnings, while 30% relied on it as their primary source of income. The survey covered 250 respondents across several types of gig work, not e-hailing drivers alone.
Bro Cabs says it wants to reach both groups, including people who own vehicles but are not yet part of the e-hailing market and those with other jobs who want to earn additional income from their cars.
The work of building a market
A subscription may appeal to drivers, but it does not automatically bring passengers. Drivers need customers to make the fee worthwhile, while passengers need enough available cars to trust the service. Building both sides requires sustained investment.
Bro Cabs has tried to address this through driver associations and local partnerships. Mfentane said the founders have developed business-to-business relationships alongside the consumer-facing service.
The company is focusing on particular areas, including Pretoria and Rosebank, where it says it has established relationships that can support adoption.
Magudulela said the strategy is to build a presence where there is already a network of potential users, rather than sign up drivers across the country without knowing where demand exists.
“It’s better to concentrate on areas where partnerships are already in place,” stated the chief marketing officer. “We have the partnerships. What we need now is the funding to drive adoption.”
That means marketing and referral incentives. Magudulela says the company wants to use platforms such as TikTok and reward existing users for bringing new drivers and commuters onto the platform.
The founders cited over 30 000 registered drivers and over 20 000 registered riders, while the company said seven to eight people were working in its operation.
The company says it has also used partnerships with driver associations to accelerate expansion. In new markets such as Durban and Pretoria, Bro Cabs has offered 500 drivers free access to the platform, specifically targeting those joining through associations.
Convincing investors to come along
The founders said their first external investor provided a relatively small amount of capital and wanted to see how they managed it before committing more. They responded by tracking expenditure closely and explaining where the money was going, including marketing costs.
The reception from venture capital firms has been more difficult. Magudulela believes investors often look at the established position of e-hailing companies such as Uber and question how a smaller competitor can build enough scale to challenge them.
The subscription model raises further questions about growth and retention. A platform charging a recurring fee must convince drivers that its service will generate enough trips to justify the payment.
“They tend to look at the potential return on investment,” Magudulela said. “If they put in R10 million ($602,000) today, how long will it take to generate a meaningful return?”
Luther Mfetane, chief strategy officer, described the experience of building a business in a market where established players have far greater financial resources.
“Everyone has a plan for how they’re going to win a boxing match until they get into the ring and get hit,” he said.
The founders want funding to expand beyond their current regional footprint. Mfentane believes a $1 million investment would help accelerate national expansion, strengthen marketing and build on the partnerships they have developed.
His co-founder,Magudulela, sees customer acquisition as a priority. Established platforms can spend heavily on promotions and discounts, a level of spending Bros Cabs cannot yet match.
The company is confident that it could capture between 10% and 20% of the market with sufficient funding..
For now, the four friends are building one driver and one passenger at a time. The money from maintaining properties and the first angel investment helped get them started. They must now prove that a platform allowing drivers to keep the full fare can also keep the business running.

articles.title: Citrix Patches 10 Critical NetScaler Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Citrix on Thursday announced patches for 28 vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, including nine critical-severity bugs.
The critical flaws stem from memory overflow issues in Packet Processing, SMPP traffic, DNS / DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH), NetScaler Push, Email OTP authentication, Endpoint Analysis (EPA/EPAS), and ICA proxy, and could lead to unpredictable/erroneous behavior or denial-of-service (DoS) conditions.
They are tracked as CVE-2026-120868, CVE-2026-107407 to CVE-2026-107410, CVE-2026-107412, CVE-2026-107415, CVE-2026-111334, and CVE-2026-120864.
Most of the remaining 19 security defects are high-severity weaknesses leading to similar outcomes. Citrix also patched several medium-severity bugs, including CVE-2026-111338, which exposes sensitive authentication material in a log file.
NetScaler ADC and Gateway versions 14.1-73.57 and later, 13.1-64.39 and later, 14.1-73.58 FIPS and later, and 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1-37.293 and later contain the relevant patches.
Citrix urges customers to update their instances as soon as possible, and details CVE preconditions associated with some of the vulnerabilities.
On Thursday, the company also announced patches for a critical-severity flaw in NetScaler Console. Tracked as CVE-2026-120869 (CVSS score of 9.4), it could allow unauthenticated attackers to bypass controls and access restricted resources.
The security defect impacts all NetScaler Console 14.1 releases before 14.1-74.34.
Citrix makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, but vulnerabilities in NetScaler are a frequent target for threat actors.

articles.title: De League of Legends à Netflix: como a Riot Games transforma música, K-pop e skins em uma estratégia de consumo
articles.text:
Você não precisa jogar League of Legends para consumir League of Legends. Basta abrir uma playlist, assistir a um videoclipe ou encontrar um cosplay de Ahri, Akali ou Kai’Sa em um evento de cultura pop.
Essa é uma das características mais interessantes da estratégia construída pela Riot Games ao longo dos últimos anos: transformar personagens de seus jogos em figuras reconhecíveis também fora do universo dos games.
Na quinta-feira, 12 de novembro, a empresa deu mais um passo nessa direção com o lançamento global da coletânea “League of Legends: Music Video Collection – K-pop & More”, na Netflix. A seleção reúne videoclipes já conhecidos dos grupos virtuais K/DA, True Damage e HEARTSTEEL, incluindo produções como “POP/STARS”, “MORE”, “GIANTS” e “PARANOIA”. Por mais que as músicas não sejam inéditas, sua chegada ao catálogo da plataforma representa uma nova oportunidade de alcançar públicos que talvez nunca tenham disputado uma partida de League of Legends.
Mais do que divulgar músicas, a Riot está ampliando os lugares onde seus personagens podem ser descobertos, acompanhados e consumidos.
K/DA: quando personagens de videogame se tornam estrelas do K-pop
Lançado em 2018, o K/DA é um dos exemplos mais conhecidos da aproximação entre League of Legends e a indústria musical. O grupo virtual é formado por quatro campeãs do jogo: Ahri, Akali, Evelynn e Kai’Sa. Cada uma recebeu uma identidade visual inspirada no universo dos grupos de K-pop, com figurinos, personalidades e uma estética própria.
A estreia aconteceu com “POP/STARS”, música que combinou artistas reais, personagens digitais e uma produção audiovisual elaborada. O videoclipe apresentou as campeãs em versões diferentes daquelas que os jogadores estavam acostumados a encontrar nas partidas.
A proposta funcionava em duas direções: quem já conhecia League of Legends podia descobrir uma nova interpretação de suas personagens favoritas, enquanto fãs de música pop podiam conhecer o universo da Riot sem necessariamente jogar.
A conexão com o K-pop não é casual.
O gênero possui uma cultura de fãs fortemente associada à identidade visual dos artistas, coreografias, figurinos, videoclipes e participação coletiva. Ao adotar elementos dessa linguagem, o K/DA passou a oferecer experiências semelhantes às de um grupo musical convencional, ainda que suas integrantes sejam personagens fictícias.
As coreografias também ganharam destaque. Movimentos reproduzidos em vídeos e apresentações de dança permitem que o público participe desse universo de maneira ativa, mesmo sem conhecer as mecânicas de League of Legends.
O resultado é uma relação com os personagens que ultrapassa o próprio jogo.
A música continua sendo consumida mesmo quando o jogador sai do LoL
Um dos aspectos mais relevantes dessa estratégia é a permanência das músicas na rotina dos fãs.
Diferentemente de uma campanha publicitária tradicional, que pode perder relevância após o lançamento de um produto, uma música pode continuar sendo ouvida durante anos. “POP/STARS”, por exemplo, foi lançada em 2018, mas ainda pode fazer parte das playlists de quem acompanhou a estreia do K/DA naquela época. Serviços como Spotify e YouTube permitem que essas canções sejam consumidas independentemente do jogo.
O fã pode ouvir K/DA enquanto trabalha, estuda ou se desloca pela cidade. Em nenhum desses momentos precisa abrir o cliente de League of Legends para continuar em contato com o universo da Riot.
A chegada dos videoclipes à Netflix acrescenta outra possibilidade a esse comportamento. Ao reunir produções já lançadas em um serviço de streaming audiovisual, a desenvolvedora amplia os pontos de contato entre suas propriedades intelectuais e o público.
Essa circulação entre plataformas também pode apresentar as personagens a pessoas que conhecem o K-pop, mas não têm interesse imediato em jogos competitivos. Assim, League of Legends deixa de depender exclusivamente das partidas para permanecer presente no cotidiano de seus consumidores.
Como a música pode estimular o consumo de skins?
Existe também um interesse comercial por trás dessa aproximação entre música e videogame.
League of Legends é um jogo gratuito, mas oferece produtos digitais opcionais, como skins, que modificam a aparência dos campeões. Quando a Riot apresenta Ahri, Akali, Evelynn e Kai’Sa como integrantes de um grupo musical, ela não está apenas produzindo entretenimento. Também está criando novas identidades visuais para personagens que já fazem parte de seu catálogo.
As skins temáticas permitem que os jogadores utilizem essas versões dentro do jogo, estabelecendo uma ligação entre a experiência musical e a experiência competitiva. É nesse ponto que a relação emocional com os personagens pode influenciar o consumo.
Um jogador pode gostar de uma campeã por suas habilidades ou estilo de jogo. Mas também pode se identificar com sua personalidade, figurino, música ou participação em determinado videoclipe.
Nesse segundo caso, a skin deixa de representar apenas uma mudança estética e passa a carregar um significado associado à identidade do fã. A compra pode funcionar como uma maneira de expressar preferência por uma personagem ou demonstrar pertencimento a uma comunidade.
Isso não significa que ouvir K/DA necessariamente leve alguém a comprar skins. Para estabelecer essa relação de maneira quantitativa, seriam necessários dados de vendas e comportamento dos consumidores. Entretanto, a estratégia cria condições para que os produtos digitais sejam apresentados dentro de experiências culturais que o público já valoriza.
Em vez de divulgar uma skin apenas dentro do jogo, a Riot também constrói um universo musical que ajuda a dar significado àquele produto.
Cosplays e coreografias transformam fãs em participantes
A relação entre K-pop e League of Legends também aparece fora das plataformas digitais.
Cosplayers reproduzem os figurinos das personagens, enquanto grupos de dança apresentam coreografias inspiradas nos videoclipes. Essas manifestações são especialmente relevantes porque não dependem exclusivamente de conteúdo produzido pela Riot. Os próprios fãs passam a reinterpretar e divulgar os personagens.
Um cosplay pode chamar a atenção de alguém que nunca jogou League of Legends. Uma apresentação de dança pode alcançar pessoas interessadas em K-pop, mas que desconhecem o K/DA. Dessa maneira, a comunidade ajuda a ampliar a circulação cultural da marca.
Um exemplo dessa aproximação está na participação de um grupo brasileiro de cosplayers na programação associada à final do Mundial de League of Legends, em Nova York, em 14 de novembro. Coordenado pelo cosmaker Leon Martins, o quarteto formado por Farah, Yoshi, Mari Fujino e Larah foi escolhido para representar as integrantes do K/DA.
A apresentação visual do grupo é inspirada em “FIRESTARTER”, música lançada em outubro, reforçando a conexão entre o lançamento musical e a participação da comunidade. A iniciativa demonstra como o universo criado para um jogo competitivo pode se transformar em uma experiência artística, envolvendo figurino, performance e identidade cultural.
Riot Games também aposta em experiências presenciais
A estratégia de expansão para além das telas não se limita aos serviços de streaming.
No Brasil, a Riot Games promoveu uma ação presencial na Loja Meruru, no bairro da Liberdade, em São Paulo, no dia 2 de novembro. A ação transformou o estabelecimento em uma pop-up store temática dedicada aos grupos K/DA, True Damage e HEARTSTEEL.
O evento reuniu atividades relacionadas à cultura pop, incluindo espaços para fotografias com cosplayers, experiências interativas, produtos temáticos e encontros entre fãs. Também contou com a participação das ilustradoras Colour Alex e Ryumen Concept.
A escolha da Liberdade tem relação com a presença da cultura asiática no bairro e com o interesse do público por manifestações culturais como o K-pop. Nesse contexto, a experiência não exigia que o visitante estivesse interessado em disputar partidas de League of Legends. Era possível participar pela música, pelos personagens, pela arte ou simplesmente pelo interesse na cultura pop.
Para a Riot, esse tipo de iniciativa representa outra forma de fortalecer o vínculo entre os consumidores e suas propriedades intelectuais. O contato com o jogo deixa de acontecer apenas por meio de uma tela e passa a ocupar espaços físicos, criando oportunidades de interação entre fãs.
K/DA não é um caso isolado
Embora seja um dos exemplos mais conhecidos, o K/DA não é a única iniciativa musical da Riot Games. O grupo True Damage explora referências ao hip-hop, enquanto HEARTSTEEL apresenta uma proposta inspirada em grupos masculinos de pop.
Cada projeto utiliza personagens de League of Legends, mas trabalha com estilos musicais, identidades visuais e públicos potencialmente diferentes. Essa diversidade permite que a empresa alcance consumidores com interesses que vão além do gênero MOBA, categoria de jogo à qual League of Legends pertence.
O lançamento da coletânea na Netflix reúne essas iniciativas em um único catálogo, permitindo observar como a Riot construiu diferentes identidades musicais a partir do mesmo universo ficcional.
A estratégia também se conecta a outros projetos audiovisuais da desenvolvedora.
A série animada Arcane, produzida pela Riot Games e animada pelo estúdio Fortiche, com distribuição da Netflix, demonstrou como personagens e histórias associados a League of Legends podem alcançar espectadores que não conhecem o jogo.
A Fortiche também participou da produção de videoclipes do K/DA, como “POP/STARS” e “FIRESTARTER”, reforçando a relação estética entre animação, música e videogames. Embora sejam formatos diferentes, essas produções compartilham uma característica: tornam o universo de Runeterra acessível por outras portas de entrada.
O jogador não precisa estar jogando para continuar consumindo
O lançamento da coletânea na Netflix evidencia uma mudança importante na maneira como empresas de games podem construir suas marcas. A relação com o consumidor não precisa começar ou terminar quando ele abre e fecha um jogo. Ela pode continuar por meio de músicas, séries, videoclipes, eventos, produtos e manifestações criadas pela própria comunidade.
No caso da Riot Games, essa expansão também ajuda a fortalecer a identidade de personagens que possuem produtos digitais comercializados dentro de League of Legends. É uma estratégia que combina entretenimento, construção de marca e oportunidades de monetização.
Mas existe uma diferença entre ampliar o interesse do público e comprovar um aumento nas vendas. Sem dados específicos, não é possível afirmar quanto o sucesso musical do K/DA representa em receita para a desenvolvedora. O que se observa é a construção de um ecossistema no qual diferentes formas de consumo se complementam.
Um fã pode descobrir uma personagem por um videoclipe, interessar-se por seu cosplay, começar a acompanhar o jogo e eventualmente adquirir uma skin. Outro pode permanecer apenas como ouvinte das músicas. Em ambos os casos, a Riot conseguiu estabelecer uma relação com aquele consumidor fora do ambiente tradicional dos games.
A grande conquista dessa estratégia talvez seja justamente essa: transformar League of Legends em um universo que o público pode continuar consumindo mesmo quando não está jogando.

articles.title: 'Cómo robar un banco' (★★★☆☆), el director de 'John Wick' y 'Deadpool 2' se divierte con la loca rebelión de los youtubers
articles.text:
El director David Leitch, responsable de películas de acción de la talla de John Wick, Bullet Train o Deadpool 2, está de vuelta en su género favorito con Cómo robar un banco. La cinta acaba de llegar a los cines y, ya solo con su alocada premisa, todo apuntaba a que como mínimo iba a ser capaz de volver a entretener de sobra a sus espectadores a base de tiros, explosiones y humor negro.
En Cómo robar un banco, una banda de ladrones de bancos expertos en redes sociales retransmite sus audaces atracos, sin saber que su creciente fama los ha puesto en el punto de mira de un veterano agente del FBI y de una brillante ingeniera de software. Mientras este improbable dúo se acerca cada vez más a ellos, la organización criminal lleva sus límites al extremo, arriesgándolo todo por sus ideales y por el golpe más ambicioso de sus vidas.
La película está protagonizada por Nicholas Hoult (Mad Max: Furia en la carretera, X-Men: Días del futuro pasado), Zoë Kravitz (Mad Max: Furia en la carretera, The Batman), Anna Sawai (Shōgun, Fast & Furious 9), Rhenzy Feliz (El Pingüino, Runaways), Christian Slater (La Fuga, Mr. Robot), Pete Davidson (El Escuadrón Suicida, Transformers: El despertar de las bestias), y John C. Reilly (Chicago, Guardianes de la Galaxia). Un reparto que, unido a su llamativa trama, prometía mucha diversión.
Cine de atracos para la Gen Z
De Cómo robar un banco lo mejor que puede decirse es lo bien que se entiende a sí misma. La película no deja de ser cine de atracos, del de toda la vida, pero hecho para una nueva generación. Así lo entiende el director y eso es lo que consigue plasmar en la pantalla. El filme no renuncia a ninguna de esas dos vertientes de su naturaleza y logra un equilibrio muy sorprendente entre ambas.
Por un lado, la cinta presenta los ingredientes habituales de este tipo de historias. Una banda de personajes relativamente marginales y a los que el sistema les ha fallado por completo. Unidos en su desgracia, deciden rebelarse y organizar una serie de robos. Por supuesto, tenemos toda clase de planes alocados y sobrexplicados, vertiginosas persecuciones y tiroteos, policías acechando y esperando el más mínimo error...
Pero, a su vez, Cómo robar un banco también se lanza de lleno con las redes sociales. La cinta emplea incluso su lenguaje de una forma muy meta, con montajes imposibles, trucos de cámara totalmente exagerados, músicas y efectos de sonido atronadores o rótulos y gráficos extravagantes por todas partes. Y, lo más llamativo, una estética muy propia para estos atracadores con sus máscaras de animales y su sentido de "manada".
Una gamberrada salvaje
Por supuesto, Leitch se aprovecha de esto para lanzar un mensaje muy interesante, típico pero eficaz, sobre la rebelión de clases y el poder de las redes. Cómo robar un banco puede llegar incluso a romantizar la violencia contra el sistema corrupto y opresor. Curioso y profético, cuanto menos, que la película se estrene justo en pleno auge del movimiento Blocus y los altercados que asolan media Europa.
En cualquier caso, no hay duda de que Cómo robar un banco es tan salvaje y desquiciada que es imposible no pasárselo bien. Una gamberrada al más puro estilo Leitch, que le imprime perfectamente su sello para llevar en volandas al espectador de principio a fin. Aunque, eso sí, quizá sea una de sus películas más imperfectas. El ritmo vertiginoso palia sus pecados, pero se hace evidente que muchas situaciones son repetitivas y que cojean si se les da una mínima reflexión. Así solo pierde credibilidad.
Quizá uno de sus puntos débiles es que pretende ser más seria y dramática de lo que debería. El humor desvergonzado del que suele hacer gala el director aquí está un poco más mitigado y su componente trágico trata de fagocitarlo todo, especialmente en su segunda mitad. Y, aunque es consistente y sólido, solo son tópicos ya de sobra conocidos, predecibles y superficiales. En cualquier caso, eso sí, su carismático reparto es capaz de sostenerlo en todo momento.
En resumen, Cómo robar un banco es una película de atracos divertida y gamberra, que funciona bien por su trepidante acción y por su manido pero potente mensaje sociopolítico. Una crítica abierta y feroz contra las desigualdades y el deterioro de la vida para la clase media y la clase baja. Pero es algo superficial y se pierde demasiado en sí misma al volverse más dramática de lo que debería. Pese a su potencial para ser más ambiciosa, nunca llega a esos niveles y acaba siendo un sencillo entretenimiento palomitero.

articles.title: 1994 Jeep Cherokee owner hacks 32-year-old car with Claude AI to pass California smog tests — enthusiast reverse-engineered the ancient ECU for diagnostics and control
articles.text:
1994 Jeep Cherokee owner hacks 32-year-old car with Claude AI to pass California smog tests — using $15 in hardware, enthusiast reverse-engineered the ancient ECU for diagnostics and control
Car owner says they just did a bit of wiring and driving, crediting Claude and Codex with the rest of the job.
An AI enthusiast managed to get his old 1994 Jeep Cherokee to pass the California smog tests, all thanks to the help of AI and a little electronics wiring skill. This 32-year-old car had only a primitive engine computer, but after connecting it to a laptop via an Arduino Nano board, many settings could be read and eventually controlled.
The above video documents Muhammad Zulali’s journey from the Jeep failing consecutive smog tests, to managing to hook it up and get readings from the ECU, to tuning and fixing the engine emission issues. All the while, Claude provided guidance, and Codex wrote any required code.
This rather old Jeep was failing the California smog tests due to producing too much NOx at certain test speeds. It initially failed at 25mph. Then, after Zulali made some adjustments to the oxygen mix, it failed at both 25mph and 50mph. Yes, it got worse.
Zulali admits he was effectively making adjustments blind, and subsequent regulatory pollution tests cost nearly $100 each time. That’s clearly a big problem, but we have AI to help us in 2026. Actually, it was AI and a $3 microcontroller, contributing to a total bill of materials of no more than $15.
The first hurdle facing the possible AI solution was the question of how to interface an old car and a new laptop. Claude told the Jeep owner that the engine communicated on a Chrysler SCI bus at ~7,800 baud, which was electrically inverted compared to a typical serial port. An Arduino Nano can handle the required inversion and hook up the data to a modern computer. The Nano was breadboarded, with a few necessary wires, three of which connected to the 6-pin diagnostic plug in the Cherokee.
The first connection attempt was a success, but only coolant temperature and battery voltage were charted by the system to begin with. Zulali wanted more data points plus some controls to fix the smog test problem. After a couple of red herrings regarding the engine “running rich” with 22% extra fuel, based on other car model data, the Jeep owner got Claude to collect data from test drives. The AI logged engine data and fault codes during a drive at 25 mph and at 50 mph to see what was happening. It was also let loose to control things like fuel pressure.
With what looked like a credible diagnosis and solution in hand, Zulali wanted to reflash the car’s main ECU with AI-tweaked code that would mean it could pass all the California smog tests. Unfortunately, this car’s computer was just a few months too old to feature reflashable firmware. Instead, the Jeep owner got Codex to inject and run custom code inside a nearby EEPROM.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
“Claude did most of the diagnostic work and Codex did pretty much all of the memory work,” admits Zulali. “I just did the wiring and the driving.” He added that he didn’t need the services of a mechanic or a Chrysler dealer tool for this feat.
In addition to the video, the Cherokee emissions fixer has created a GitHub repository for this project, dubbed xj-scanner. It is free software distributed under the GPLv3 license.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

Why, apart from financial difficulty, continue to use a 32 year old emmisions factory?

No need to visit a dealership or buy an entire assembly of things to repair something. Registration (possibly historic) and insurance should be significantly cheaper too. They're perfect if you don't drive often or for long distances, and they also excel at driving through/over difficult conditions. Just beware the noise, uncomfortable seats, and neverending battle against rust. Reply

articles.title: The smallest version of Camp Snap’s retro digital camcorder fits on your keychain
articles.text:
Last week, Camp Snap launched a miniaturized version of its screen-free CS-8 video camera that was half the size of the original with a smaller grip designed to be easier for kids to hold. But it turns out the company wasn’t done shrinking its hardware. Camp Snap’s new CS-8 Micro is even smaller than the CS-8 Mini. It’s around three inches long and weighs just 1.5 ounces so you can hang it from your keys and, like its larger predecessors, it can capture video using one of five built-in filters.
The smallest version of Camp Snap’s retro digital camcorder fits on your keychain
The Camp Snap CS-8 Micro is just three inches long and adds a tiny LCD screen that’s only used as a viewfinder.
The CS-8 Micro will be available starting on November 17th at 11AM ET through Camp Snap’s online store, Target, and Urban Outfitters for $39.99, and similar to the collectible Kodak Charmera, the Micro is being sold in sealed mystery boxes. Colors like hot pink, lilac, lime, and orange will be easier to find, while vintage classic (black) and glow in the dark will be much rarer.
Unlike the original CS-8 and CS-8 Mini, the new Micro does include an LCD display, but it’s only used as a viewfinder. You can’t watch, edit, or delete anything you’ve captured on the camera itself. You need to transfer the videos to a phone or computer using a USB-C cable to enjoy them, or move its included 4GB microSD into a card reader.
As Camp Snap has been progressively shrinking its retro camcorder, it’s also reduced its resolution. The original captured videos at 4K, while the CS-8 Mini did 2.7K. The CS-8 Micro is limited to 720p, but carries forward features like an 8x digital zoom and a selection of five filters that include vintage effects that add flicker and grain to emulate the look of 8mm film. Camp Snap estimates the Micro’s 4GB microSD card can hold 45 to 6o minutes of video, while its battery life is estimated to be 30 to 45 minutes on a full charge.
Correction, November 13th: The Camp Snap CS-8 Mini will launch on November 17th.

articles.title: Tierhaare adé, Rasen startklar: Black-Friday-Deals bei eufy
articles.text:
Black Friday Saugroboter für clevere Haushalte: Roboter von Anker eufy gegen Tierhaare und für die Rasenpflege – bis zu 300 € sparen
Black Friday lohnt sich, wenn Technik dir Arbeit abnimmt, statt neue zu schaffen. Vier Modelle von Anker eufy sind jetzt so günstig wie lange nicht: HydroJet E35 und C30 Edge gegen Tierhaare, die Mähroboter C15 und E15 für die Gartensaison. Jetzt clever kaufen, später Zeit gewinnen.
Anker eufy Saugroboter HydroJet E35: Mit 35.000 Pa gegen tiefsitzende Tierhaare im Teppich
Nach dem herbstlichen Fellwechsel sammeln sich lose Tierhaare im Teppich. Dazu kommt Schmutz, den die Vierbeiner bei nassem Wetter ins Haus tragen. Beides setzt sich tief im Teppich fest – selbst wenn die Oberfläche sauber wirkt.
Der Anker eufy Saugroboter HydroJet E35 (799 € statt 999 €) entfernt Tierhaare und Schmutz mit 35.000 Pa Saugkraft aus der Tiefe des Teppichs. Die Bürste mit DuoSpiral verhindert Haarwickel um die Walze, die Filtration mit AeroTurbo erhält die volle Saugkraft – bis zu 365 Tage. Wer viel kocht, profitiert vom HydroJet-Wischsystem 2.0: Die Rolle erhält laufend Frischwasser und streift Schmutzwasser sofort ab – Küchenfett wird nicht verteilt. Die ThermoFresh 8-in-1-Station entleert den Staubbehälter, wäscht die Rolle bei 60 °C und trocknet sie ohne bleibende Tiergerüche; der Staubbeutel mit 2,5 l hält bis zu 60 Tage. Dein Zuhause wird vor den Feiertagen tiefenrein – ohne täglichen Aufwand.
Anker eufy C30 Edge: Saugkraft auf Flaggschiff-Niveau für kleine Wohnungen mit Haustieren
Wer wenig Platz hat und das Budget im Blick behält, findet im Anker eufy C30 Edge (519 € statt 699 €) eine passende Lösung. Wie der E35 bietet er 35.000 Pa Saugkraft – im Test unter identischen Bedingungen hob er eine doppelt so hohe Wassersäule wie der Roborock Qrevo Edge (20.000 Pa). Dazu kommt eine All-in-One-Station mit nur 31 cm Höhe; das Wischpad fährt dank MopMaster 3.0 für lückenlose Kantenreinigung um 76 mm aus, und der Staubbeutel reicht für bis zu 60 Tage.
Im Saugtest unter identischen Bedingungen hob er eine Wassersäule mehr als doppelt so hoch wie der Roborock Qrevo Edge.
Mähroboter C15 und E15 von Anker eufy: 300 € günstiger – auspacken, aufstellen, mähen lassen
Das beste Schnäppchen außerhalb der Saison: jetzt 300 € sparen, im Frühjahr auspacken – der Rasen mäht sich praktisch von selbst. Kein Begrenzungskabel, kein RTK, keine Installation: TrueVision kartiert den Garten in rund fünf Minuten automatisch – und der Mähroboter legt direkt los. Während andere im Frühling den vollen Preis zahlen und Kabel verlegen, lehnst du dich zurück. Der Anker eufy C15 Standard mit Garage (699 € statt 999 €) passt für Gärten bis 500 m², der E15 mit Garage (899 € statt 1.199 €) für größere oder getrennte Flächen wie Vorder- und Hintergarten.
Alle Angebote: 10. bis 30. November auf anker.com/de und bei Amazon. Ob Tierhaare im Teppich oder der erste Rasenschnitt im April: Clevere Technik schenkt dir Zeit zurück.

articles.title: Vous avez un smartphone Samsung ? Attention avant de migrer votre passe Navigo chez Google
articles.text:
Depuis le 13 novembre 2026, Île-de-France Mobilités (IDFM) confie la gestion du passe Navigo sur Android aux services Google. Un changement d’infrastructure majeur qui vise à simplifier le passe Navigo sur Android : il n’y a plus besoin de faire tourner l’application Mes Tickets Navigo en arrière-plan et tous les smartphones sont logés à la même enseigne. C’est une bonne nouvelle pour la plupart des smartphones… mais une moins bonne pour les utilisateurs Samsung.
Depuis 2019, les smartphones Samsung bénéficient d’un avantage technique : une puce sécurisée permet aux titres Navigo de fonctionner avec le téléphone éteint ou sans batterie, exactement comme sur iPhone depuis 2024. Le changement d’architecture met fin à cet avantage : les appareils Samsung sont traités comme les autres Android, avec de l’émulation logicielle et les services Google.
Quels sont les smartphones Samsung concernés par le changement ?
Aujourd’hui, le passe Navigo sur Android fait cohabiter deux technologies :
- l’eSE (embedded Secure Element) est une petite puce physique, isolée du reste du téléphone, qui stocke les titres comme une vraie carte Navigo et peut fonctionner téléphone éteint.
- Le HCE (Host Card Emulation) est un logiciel qui imite une carte sans contact et a donc besoin que le téléphone soit allumé pour répondre au valideur.
En fonction de votre appareil Samsung Galaxy, vous n’êtes peut-être pas concernés par cette regression. Seuls les smartphones haut de gamme ont droit au système avec la puce sécurisée, les autres étaient déjà émulés par le logiciel. Il existe deux cas de figure :
- Vos titres sont dans l’application Mes Tickets Navigo (HCE) : (votre numéro de support, visible dans l’application Île-de-France Mobilités, commence par H) votre Samsung fonctionne déjà comme n’importe quel téléphone Android, par émulation logicielle. La migration vers Google ne vous fait rien perdre, au contraire, vous allez gagner des nouveautés.
- Vos titres sont dans la puce sécurisée du téléphone (eSE) : sur les téléphones haut de gamme ou récents, c’est la puce Samsung qui stocke vos titres, qui apparaissent normalement dans l’application Samsung Wallet. Vous risquez donc de perdre des fonctions en migrant sur Google (et vous pouvez refuser la migration).
Qu’est-ce que je perds si je passe chez Google ?
Comme l’ancien système Navigo (l’app secondaire Mes Tickets Navigo), le système de Google repose sur l’émulation logicielle (HCE), qui a besoin que le téléphone soit allumé pour fonctionner. En migrant, un Samsung qui utilisait sa puce sécurisée perd :
- La validation téléphone éteint ou sans batterie : avec la puce sécurisée, IDFM indique qu’il est possible de valider jusqu’à 24 heures et 15 validations après l’extinction, sur une liste de modèles compatibles. Cette possibilité n’est plus possible avec la migration vers la technologie HCE.
- La Galaxy Watch : le Navigo dans Google Wallet ne fonctionne pas sur montre au lancement et IDFM ne donne aucun calendrier. Si vous souhaitez utiliser votre montre, il faut rester sur l’ancien système.
- La gestion depuis l’app Samsung Wallet : il faut passer par Google Wallet, Île-de-France Mobilités, RATP ou SNCF Connect. On perd aussi le paiement Samsung Pay pour recharger sa carte.
Et qu’est-ce que je gagne en passant sur l’infrastructure Google ?
Le nouveau système apporte plusieurs avantages aux téléphones Android et IDFM et Samsung ne prévoient pas de déployer ces nouveautés sur les puces sécurisée eSE :
- Jusqu’à 20 cartes par téléphone : le nouveau système permet de stocker plusieurs cartes, contre une seule aujourd’hui. Une seule fonctionne avec le téléphone en veille, les autres doivent être déclenchées depuis une app.
- La sauvegarde des titres : ils suivent votre compte Google quand vous changez de téléphone.
- L’achat de tous les titres dans Google Wallet, y compris les forfaits semaine et mois avec un compte IDFM Connect.
- Le paiement par Google Pay dans les applications partenaires.
Samsung Wallet, Google ou iPhone : quelles différences ?
|  | Samsung avant le 13 novembre | Android avant le 13 novembre | Android/Samsung après le 13 novembre | iPhone | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stockage des titres | Puce sécurisée (eSE) | Émulation logicielle (HCE) via Mes Tickets Navigo | Émulation logicielle (HCE) via Google | Puce sécurisée (eSE) | 
| Validation sans déverrouiller | Oui avec une seule carte | Sur certains téléphones | Oui, avec la carte par défaut | Oui, avec la carte par défaut | 
| Validation téléphone éteint | Oui | Non | Non | Oui | 
| Montre | Galaxy Watch | Non | Non, pas au lancement | Apple Watch | 
| Nombre de cartes | Une seule | Une seule | Jusqu’à 20 | Plusieurs | 
| Sauvegarde des titres | Via Samsung Wallet | Via Mes Tickets Navigo | Oui, via Google | Oui, via iCloud | 
Comment refuser la migration vers les services Google ?
Si vos titres sont dans la puce sécurisée et que vous tenez à la validation téléphone éteint ou à votre Galaxy Watch, vous pouvez refuser la migration si l’application Île-de-France Mobilités vous la propose lors d’un rechargement.
Autre option : n’utiliser que Samsung Wallet, qui vend déjà des titres Navigo et devrait, a priori, conserver l’ancien système pour l’instant.
J’ai un nouveau Samsung : où créer ma carte Navigo ?
Sur les nouveaux smartphones Samsung, c’est une carte Google qui sera installée par défaut, sans la puce sécurisée. Il reste possible de créer une carte à l’ancienne depuis Samsung Wallet seulement.
Et pour ma Galaxy Watch ?
Le système de Google ne gère pas les montres pour l’instant. Pour charger un passe Navigo sur une Galaxy Watch, passez par Samsung Wallet et évitez les applications Île-de-France Mobilités ou Google Wallet. L’Apple Watch est la seule montre officiellement supportée désormais.
Apple, le grand gagnant de ce changement
Pour l’écosystème Android dans son ensemble, la bascule chez Google est une bonne nouvelle : la plupart des téléphones gagnent des fonctions qu’ils n’avaient jamais eues et n’ont plus besoin d’une application supplémentaire.
Pour Samsung, il y a un goût amer. Les Galaxy étaient les premiers et les mieux servis en Île-de-France depuis 2019 : ils doivent désormais choisir entre les nouveautés de Google et les avantages de leur puce sécurisée. Ajoutons qu’il y a d’autres perdants : les utilisateurs d’un Android sans services Google (GrapheneOS, Huawei…) perdent le droit d’utiliser le passe Navigo sur leur téléphone.
Le vrai gagnant s’appelle Apple. L’iPhone cumule puce sécurisée, un mode Express sans batterie, plusieurs cartes et le support de l’Apple Watch. Pour un usager francilien, il offre aujourd’hui de loin l’expérience Navigo la plus complète.
